For years, whistleblowers have publicly alleged that the United States government is withholding what it knows about UFOs (now formally referred to as “unidentified anomalous phenomena” or “UAP”).

Those allegations gained new weight this past May, when the U.S. Department of War began the process of releasing hundreds of declassified documents, images and videos as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters.

These recent disclosures raise an old question: If the U.S. government is officially acknowledging that UAP have been observed, could claims of contact with the non-human intelligence allegedly operating them also be true? To understand what a claim of actual contact would even mean, it helps to start with the framework that first tried to categorize these encounters.

In 1972, American astronomer J. Allen Hynek proposed a three-part “Close Encounters” framework for classifying UFO experiences that has shaped the field since the late 1940s.

A “Close Encounter of the First Kind” (CE-1) is a visual sighting from less than 150 metres away. A CE-2 involves physiological effects on the surrounding environment. A CE-3 involves observing non-human entities operating the UFO.

Five years after Hynek’s book appeared, Steven Spielberg’s 1977 film Close Encounters of the Third Kind established CE-3 in popular culture.

open image in gallery For years, whistleblowers have publicly alleged that the United States government is withholding what it knows about UFOs ( Getty Images )

Communicating with UAP

Later researchers expanded Hynek’s classification. A “Close Encounter of the Fourth Kind” refers to abduction into a UAP. A “Close Encounter of the Fifth Kind” (CE-5) alleges human-initiated communication with the non-human intelligence operating UAP, whether extraterrestrials, time-travellers or so-called interdimensional beings.

Those who claim to have had such encounters are commonly called — as in Spielberg’s newly released film, Disclosure Day — “experiencers.”

CE-5 is not just a category of experience, though. During the past three decades, it has developed into a ritual protocol practised by a global community. Groups gather in wilderness settings around the world with the intention to initiate contact using various techniques. Some use laser pointers to send visual signals into the sky and geiger counters to measure fluctuations in radiation levels.

Stroboscopic light and musical entrainment have also been observed alongside mantra recitations, and transcendental meditation focused on “coherent thought sequencing” (where practitioners visualize their consciousness extending into deep space before sending a telepathic invitation to the operators of UAP to visit Earth).

Practioners of CE-5 ritual protocol also report telepathic communication, “photon dialogue” through flashing lights and bodily sensations from UAP that they interpret as interspecies communication.

Shamanism with a technological twist

Is CE-5 a new religious movement?

Although practitioners reject the label “religion,” their activities constitute a protocol enabling extraordinary experiences with superior, sky-dwelling entities. The fact that their efforts to connect with extraterrestrials draw upon telepathy and altered states of consciousness suggests a ritual form commonly associated with shamanism, yet with advanced technological mediation.

Calling CE-5 a “religion” may also reduce convictions about extraterrestrial presence from questions of reality to matters of belief or conspiracy, reflecting the long-standing cultural dismissal of UFOs and “little green men.”

Religious or not, CE-5 practitioners draw on 80 years of UFO lore to advance a cosmology in which consciousness is a fundamental property of the universe that enables telepathic communication with superior, non-human intelligence visiting Earth.

CE-5 protocol also resembles a ritual séance. It combines transcendental meditation, cosmic visualization, telepathic communication and an experience of “internal communication” through which bodily sensations become direct signs of extraterrestrial contact.

This has interesting parallels with anthropologist Tanya Luhrmann’s research on Evangelical Christianity in America and how church-goers feel themselves to be in direct communication with God through bodily sensations and religious interpretations of their inner voice.

CE-5 practitioners regard extraterrestrials as benevolent, highly intelligent beings physically present in space and around Earth.

Are they, as religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka asked in her 2019 book American Cosmic: UFOs, Religion, Technology, the angels of the secular space age? Rather than genuine contact, do they instead represent an unconscious desire to re-enchant the de-spiritualized cosmos?

A salvation narrative

Many CE-5 practitioners believe that the U.S. government, in tandem with defence contractors, possesses recovered extraterrestrial craft and that scientists have secretly reverse-engineered alien technologies.

These claims have been advanced by figures with overlapping views such as former military and intelligence officers Col. Philip J. Corso, Luis Elizondo and David Grusch (who testified under oath before U.S. Congress that a secret arms race exists to recover and exploit non-human technology that has crashed or landed on Earth). The U.S. government has denied these claims.

Within CE-5 communities, the “disclosure” event in which the government admits to possessing alien technology also functions as a salvation narrative. That’s because official confirmation promises technological liberation from fossil fuels, leading to the dawn of a free energy civilization.

As in millenarian movements, the anticipated post-disclosure world is always imminent but perpetually deferred.

About the author Shayne A. P. Dahl is an Assistant Professor, Anthropology, University of Calgary. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

What if close encounters are real?

CE-5 bears many hallmarks of a new religious movement emerging from the intersection of science, technology and modern anxieties. It may indeed re-enchant a desanctified universe viewed through secular scientific frameworks.

Yet, UAP present an unusual challenge. The U.S. government has acknowledged that UAP are real, even as it maintains there’s no confirmed evidence of extraterrestrial origin. And so it’s possible that CE-5 may not be based solely on faith and imagination but on experiencers’ interpretations of authentic encounters with an advanced, non-human intelligence.

Regardless of whether the anomalous experiences reported during CE-5s involve genuine contact with non-human intelligence, the practice has certainly emerged as a ritual of cosmological transition.

It encourages participants to experience the universe not as dead empty space but as a cosmic community in which we, ancient by our own reckoning, have only just awakened to our place in the galactic neighbourhood.

Either way, it’s time for scholars of the humanities and social sciences to take seriously UAP and the possibility of non-human intelligence. The stigma is fading.

President Donald Trump believes that cumulative inflation under his second term will be the lowest of the past six administrations – despite persistently high prices that his administration continues to struggle with.

The president posted an infographic on Truth Social Sunday showing cumulative inflation rates for each of the last six administrations, measuring the total percentage change in consumer prices over four years under each president.

At the top is former President Joe Biden, who saw a cumulative inflation rate of 21.20 percent over the four years he was in office.

At the bottom of the chart sits Trump’s second administration with a 4.71 percent inflation rate – however, the data is incomplete because Trump is only 18 months into office. The president pointed that out in a separate Truth Social post.

When examining cumulative inflation at the 18-month mark of each presidential term, Trump’s second term has the fourth-highest inflation rate.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump appeared to flex that his second term had lower cumulative inflation than past presidencies – though it’s missing six months of data ( Getty )

Mediaite was the first to report on the Truth Social post.

Though Trump ran on a platform to lower everyday costs, in part by lowering inflation, the president has struggled to maintain that promise because his war with Iran has pushed consumer prices up.

The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has disrupted global trade and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, causing gas and oil prices to rise. As of August 10, Americans are paying, on average, $4 per gallon of regular gasoline.

Between June 2025 and June 2026, consumer prices rose 3.5 percent overall.

Rising costs have reflected poorly on the Trump administration.

In a July Fox News poll of 1,003 people, just 24 percent said they approved of Trump’s handling of the economy.

open image in gallery Trump posted an infographic on Truth Social, seemingly flexing that cumulative inflation under his second term is lower than any of the past six administrations – however, it used incomplete data from Trump's current term ( realDonaldTrump/ Truth Social )

Just 33 percent of people said they felt they were “living comfortably” in a recent Marquette Law School poll – a 7 percentage point decrease from the number of people who said they were living comfortably in January.

Yet, Trump has consistently tried to insist that he’s bringing costs down.

While delivering remarks in Michigan last month, the president said that “inflation dropped by the largest amount in more than six years, because we’re doing it right”

“They tried to blame high prices on me,” Trump told rally-goers.

While Trump is correct that inflation dropped quickly in June, his statement excludes some key context.

The decrease in inflation in June came after months of increases largely attributed to higher oil and gas prices due to the Iran war. The U.S. and Iran were following a ceasefire agreement in June – which subsequently fell apart in July.

Inflation was also still higher in June 2026 than it was at the start of Trump’s second term in January 2025.

The infographic, posted by the president, appears to have originated from an Instagram account called Yung Geeski.

Lara Trump, the president’s daughter-in-law, re-posted the infographic on Instagram earlier Sunday, calling it a “great chart” and including the caveat that the information was incomplete for Trump’s second term.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: How Jeff Bezos stacks up in Premier League owners rich list with Amazon chief on brink of mega-money Liverpool takeover
Sports.content:
JEFF BEZOS is set to join the minted club of Premier League owners.

The Amazon chief is reportedly part of an investment group closing in on a deal to buy a minority stake in Liverpool, with Sky News reporting a deal could be announced as early as this week.



The investor group is headed up by Amit Bhatia, who was previously a long-term shareholder at Queens Park Rangers, and has a net worth of around £23billion to his name.

However, that pales in comparison to Bezos, who reportedly has a staggering wealth of £213bn – with only Tesla‘s Elon Musk and Google co-founder Larry Page worth more.



But how does he stack up in the Premier League owners rich list?

SunSport has taken a look at the personal wealth of league owners, and ranked the top 10 if Bezos and co complete their stunning move.



1. Public Investment Fund – £1.2trillion

It is a bit tricky to calculate your net worth when it is directly tied to a country… but that is the sort of headache Newcastle have, which normally wouldn’t be much of an issue.

However the long arm of football financial fair play rules has put a stop to the limitless spending once seen by the likes of Chelsea and Manchester City, with Toon being forced to operate effectively with one hand behind their back since the takeover of the Saudi Public Investment Fund in 2021.

2. Liverpool – FSG + Jeff Bezos consortium* – £265bn+

As it stands, Liverpool are not even in the top 10 when it comes to the wealth of their owners, despite being the joint most successful club in England in terms of league titles, and the clear best in terms of European trophies.

Fenway Sports Group bought Liverpool in 2010, but they could now see their capital bolstered by the Bezos backed syndicate which also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin – worth £25bn – and Amit Bhatia – worth £23bn.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

3. Manchester City – Sheikh Mansour/Silver Lake – £24bn

The Newcastle before Newcastle, Manchester City are the original so-called oil club of the Premier League, and made the most of their limitless spending to put them in a position to win titles since the takeover in 2008.

Sheikh Mansour‘s personal wealth is a staggering £20billion, then you can add the Silver Lake group’s own financial muscle to take City’s total ownership worth to £24bn.

4. Manchester United – Glazers/Ineos – £20bn

Sir Jim Ratcliff is Britain’s richest man, but he is limited with his investment into Man Utd by only having a minority stake in the club which he bought in 2023 and completed in 2024.

The Glazers ownership of United was completed in a leveraged buyout back in 2005, but fans have made their feelings perfectly clear about it since then with a seemingly never-ending stream of protests.

5. Chelsea – Clearlake – £19bn

Todd Boehly and Behdad Eghbali led a group of investors from Clearlake capital in acquiring Chelsea from Roman Abramovich – and the UK government – in 2022.



They are worth around £19bn, and have flexed those muscles in the transfer market, even if many of the deals have not worked out and performances on the pitch are not reflecting it.

6. Arsenal – Stan Kroenke – £16bn

American billionaire Stan Kroenke acquired a majority share Arsenal in 2011, four years after becoming a minority shareholder.

Like United fans, Gooners were not happy at the team’s lack of success – even amid a stadium rebuild – before Stan’s son, Josh, took control of the club in 2018 and has overseen their rise to becoming Premier League champions once again.



7. Crystal Palace – Woody Johnson/Josh Harris – £13bn

Woody Johnson is one of several businessmen to own shares in Crystal Palace, though his 43 per cent stake acquired from John Textor is the largest.

Alongside him Josh Harris, David Blitzer and club chairman Steve Parish make up the club’s ownership, which has seen surprise FA Cup and Europa Conference League wins come in the last two seasons.

8. Fulham – Shahid Khan – £11bn

Automotive parts manufacturer Shahid Khan has a reported net worth of £11bn, and acquired Fulham in 2013 from Mohamed Al Fayed.



Khan, who also owns the NFL‘s Jacksonville Jaguars, oversaw the club’s yo-yo period in coming up to the Prem and falling back into the Championship between 2018 and 2022 before they settled and have remained ever since.

9. Aston Villa – Nassef Sawiris – £10bn

Egyptian billionaire Nassef Sawiris owns Aston Villa alongside American billionaire Wes Edens, making the club ownership worth an estimated £10bn following their purchase in 2018.

The club have since returned to the top flight and are now Champions League regulars under Unai Emery, while also just breaking the record for the biggest sale in Premier League history with the £117m they got from Chelsea for Morgan Rogers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

10. Everton – Friedkin Group – £9bn

The Friedkin Group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin, completed a majority acquisition of Everton in 2024 which ended years of choppy waters for them under the previous ownership of Farhad Moshiri.

TFG also own Italian side Roma, but their biggest move with the Toffees has been to complete their move from Goodison Park to the Hill Dickinson Stadium in 2025.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho was obsessed with Lionel Messi and ‘having a nightmare’ when preparing for El Clasico
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO was utterly obsessed with Lionel Messi, his former Real Madrid players revealed.

The Special One’s first stint at the Bernabeu lasted three years from 2010 to 2013.



In the battle with arch-rivals Barcelona, Los Blancos won the 2011 Copa del Rey and LaLiga a year later, briefly interrupting Pep Guardiola’s dominance.

But whenever Real faced Barca, Mourinho spent most of his time totally fixated on somehow stopping Messi.



And in his self-titled Netflix documentary, Mourinho admitted he suffered sleepless nights about that special man from Argentina.

Ex-Real midfielder Sami Khedira – now back at the Bernabeu as an assistant to Jose – said: “Preparing for the games was so funny because we spoke for two minutes about Barcelona.

“And then it was 40 minutes about Lionel Messi.

“He prepared every single detail.

“He changed some players, sometimes Pepe played as a No6, then Sergio Ramos.

“The most important thing was, ‘How can we stop Lionel Messi?’”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Mourinho added: “I was having a nightmare. ‘What can we do to stop him?’

“From the first [El Clasico] game, I knew that we couldn’t be better than them doing the same as they do.

“To beat them, we had to be different both on and off the pitch.

“We were football enemies in the sense we fought for the same cup, the same league, the same Champions League. I think it was a good thing.”



Barcelona won Mourinho’s first LaLiga El Clasico 5-0 at the Nou Camp. The feisty reverse fixture at the Bernabeu ended 1-1.

Barca came out on top in the Champions League semis, while it was Madrid who beat their bitter enemy in the Copa del Rey final.

Left-back Marcelo explained the mentality shift instilled by the boss.

He said: “Jose treated every game like it was a final.

“He got into our heads and changed our mindset.



“We started going into those games like it was life or death, like we had to win.”

And that saw him clash with captain Iker Casillas after the manager found out the goalkeeper had extended an olive branch to Barcelona midfielder Xavi to keep the peace between Spanish national team pals.

Spain won Euro 2008, the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with one of the greatest generations ever.

But Mourinho did not care for niceties and wanted nothing short of full commitment from his Real Madrid warriors in the raging battle against Barcelona.

He accused Casillas of being a traitor at the time.



And Mourinho – who revealed he agreed to replace Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013 – told his documentary: “I always say, in every situation, when you want to make a point, when you want to go right to the heart, you don’t do it to the little ones, you go to the big ones.

“There are things that I don’t accept and will never accept.

“And when somebody doesn’t respect me, it’s a problem.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I said, ‘This is Barcelona-Real Madrid. When you go to the national team, then you can kiss the guy. But not now. This is war.’”

Sports.title: Lando Norris’ ex Margarida Corceiro ‘spotted with former boyfriend Joao Felix in nightclub’ three years after split
Sports.content:
LANDO NORRIS’s ex-girlfriend has reportedly been spotted at a nightclub with her former flame, Atletico Madrid star Joao Felix.

Margarida Corceiro has been in an off-and-on relationship with the reigning Formula One world champ for the last couple of years.



However, with things cooling in recent months, the model was spotted with Felix at Praia na Villa nightclub in the Algarve, according to Portuguese outlet Record.

The pair, who ended their relationship around three years ago, did not arrive at the club together though.



The actress and social media star turned up with her friends, while Felix arrived with his.

According to reports, at some point during the night, they met and chatted until the early hours of the morning.

After unfollowing each other in 2024, following the reunion, Corceiro and Felix started following one another again on social media.

Corceiro split with F1 star Norris in February this year after a rollercoaster relationship.

Lando confirmed the pair had broken up once more in February 2026, saying he was a “single man”.

Corceiro, who also goes by Magui, is a 23-year-old Portuguese actress, model and influencer.



According to her IMDB profile, she is originally from Santarém, Portugal – a city about an hour outside of Lisbon.



She regularly wows fans with her social media posts, helping her rack up 2.5million followers on Instagram.

Sports.title: Former Newcastle badboy Nile Ranger claims he had heated brawl with ex-England star after he spat in his pasta
Sports.content:
EX-NEWCASTLE troublemaker Nile Ranger has admitted he scrapped Andros Townsend during international duty with England Under-19s.

According to Ranger, the altercation was sparked by Townsend spitting in his pasta.



Ranger was spilling the beans on the Undr The Cosh football podcast, as he discussed his run-in with Townsend while in Ukraine on international duty with England U19s.

A disagreement about pre-match preparation, in which Townsend told Ranger he had a “stinker” in a recent game, sparked the conflict.



Ranger said: “‘I don’t know why he was coming at me. Take your anger out on someone else bro because I’m not the one. I’ll just knock you out and then it’s just long.

“Anyway, we go down for food the next day and, you remember those old-school blue Lucozade bottles with the yellow top, he’s drinking from it and he’s spitting in my pasta.

“I’m looking around at players and being like – are you witnessing this as well? This is crazy antics right now.”

Ranger was not prepared to let his team-mate get off lightly, he said: “I can see Andros there, I’m on to Andros, and I’ve just crashed him.

“His head hits the bin and man are trying to stop me, Kyle Walker trying to stop me, but the rage inside is just going mad, going berserk.”

The clash with Townsend could be considered a tame disagreement in Ranger’s list of off-field mishaps.

As a teenager, he spent time in a young offenders’ institution following a reported armed robbery.

His first professional contract came at Newcastle, where he spent four years from 2009 to 2013.

However, he spent half of his Newcastle career out on loan at Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday.

The Toon opted against renewing his contract following a series of off-pitch controversies.



After leaving the North East, Ranger would go on to become something of a journeyman as he had spells at Swindon Town, Blackpool and Southend.

He then ventured into non-league with Spalding, followed by a short return to Southend, before playing for Boreham Wood, Kettering and Wellingborough Town.

He recently left Isthmian Prem side Chatham Town after joining them in January.

And after appearing in Baller League last year, he revealed a new career aged 34.

SunSport has reached out to Townsend for comment on whether he spat in Ranger’s pasta.

Sports.title: Keep or axe? SunSport’s Arsenal reporters have their say on Viktor Gyokeres with Gunners craving world-class forward
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are still in the market for a world-class forward this summer as Mikel Arteta looks to build on their title success.

The Gunners were unable to pull off an ambitious deal to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid and are now looking at alternative options.



With a serious lack of top quality left wingers on the market, Arsenal may have to shift their attention to the centre-forward position to bolster their attack.

But after splashing £63.5m on Viktor Gyokeres last season, it raises question marks over the future of the Swedish striker.



Fans and pundits alike were left unconvinced by Gyokeres’ performances at times last season, leading to speculation that he could be moved on if Arsenal do sign a new striker.

But with such a large outlay on a marquee player, Arsenal would have to seriously consider if trying to sell is worth the risk.

Here, SunSport Arsenal reporters Simon Collings and Joshua Hall debate whether it is time for the Gunners to cut their losses on Gyokeres.

Simon Collings – Sell and upgrade

Finding a buyer for Gyokeres will not be easy.

But if Arsenal can find a way to sell the Swede and upgrade, then they have to grab it.

The striker had a solid debut season in North London, finishing as the Gunners top scorer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And his performances around crunch time – especially in the Champions League semi-final triumph over Atletico Madrid – deserve a special mention.

It is hard to shake the feeling, though, that Gyokeres is not the right fit for Mikel Arteta’s side.

Some rusty performances in pre-season have done little to dispel that, especially when Arsenal are still in the market for a marquee forward.

The expectation is that they will push for a left winger, however there must surely be a temptation to get a new No9 in.



Arteta is a huge fan of Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez – and he looks readymade for this current team.

Gyokeres is someone who thrives off open space, direct passes and the ability to hurt opponents on the counter.

That is just not how Arsenal play, and nor is it how teams set up against them.

The challenge is often trying to pick the lock of a deep defence. Pre-season rust or not, that has never been Gyokeres’ strength.

It would suit Alvarez, though, and his technical quality would raise the level of the attack.



He would also bring fluidity, too, as he can operate out left or even as second striker if needed.

Gyokeres undoubtedly served a purpose for Arsenal last season and helped them win the Premier League for the first time in 22 years.

But if Arteta is being ruthless and wants to take this team to the next level, then the striker position is one area that can be upgraded.



It would be a bold call after one season – but history has shown us Arteta is never worried about that.

Joshua Hall – Keep and trust

There is no denying that Gyokeres hasn’t quite lived up to the lofty expectations he arrived with last summer.

But you can’t argue that he hasn’t done his job.

The Swede finished the season as Arsenal’s top goalscorer and helped them win their first league title in 22 years.

Question marks have arisen about his technical ability, but his goalscoring has remained undeniable – even if it hasn’t quite matched his form in Portugal.



The latter part of last season showed that Gyokeres was starting to increase his technical level too.

His performances against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League semi-final knitted together his brute force with cute interplay that helped the Gunners dismantle their opponents.

Now, with 12 months under his belt, Gyokeres will only be a better player than he was when he arrived at the Emirates.



Arsenal invested £63.5m in Gyokeres and would struggle to recoup that if they tried to move him on, forcing him out the door seems counterproductive after that outlay.

Arteta is keen to take his squad to a “different dimension” after their title success last season and a new attacker would undoubtedly help achieve that.

But it doesn’t have to be in place of Gyokeres, it could instead complement him.

Julian Alvarez is one name that has been discussed and the Atleti star would be a brilliant signing if Arsenal can pull it off.

He is so vastly different from Gyokeres and would give Arteta another option to throw at opposition defences.



But there is no need to push Gyokeres out to make space for the Argentine.

Arsenal already seem likely to lose Gabriel Jesus this summer, with Napoli leading the race for his signature.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Kai Havertz has been operating predominantly as a midfielder during the Gunners’ pre-season preparations.

Keeping Gyokeres around would mean Arsenal have two top quality strikers who can hurt the opposition in vastly different ways.

Sports.title: Arsenal make two changes to Emirates Stadium ahead of Premier League season kicking off
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are still celebrating last season’s title win – leading to two changes being made to the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners ended their 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions in May.



And they will get their battle to retain the crown underway when Coventry visit North London on August 21.

But, ahead of the newly-promoted side’s trip to the capital, Arsenal have given their home a slight makeover.



A silhouette of the Premier League trophy and Women’s Champions Cup have been added either side of the year 2026 on an advertising hoarding below the upper tier.

The addition is an update to the third tier hoarding, which wraps around the entire stadium and shows every trophy that the club has won.



Three huge CHAMPIONS signs have also been put up above the Emirates Stadium’s club shop.

Both alterations were on display for the first time when Arsenal lost to Borussia Dortmund yesterday.

Goals from Ethan Nwaneri and Viktor Gyokeres were not enough for Mikel Arteta’s side.

Samuele Inacio, Konstantinos Karetsas and Joane Gadou were on target as Arsenal suffered a 3-2 defeat and missed out on Emirates Cup glory.



It means the Gunners have suffered back-to-back losses, having also been beaten by Real Betis last week.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Arsenal are set to wrap up their pre-season schedule by welcoming legend Cesc Fabregas and his Como side to the Emirates Stadium on Wednesday.

And the reigning Premier League champions will take on FA Cup winners Manchester City with the Community Shield up for grabs on Sunday.



Arteta has been splashing the cash on reinforcements while adjustments are made to Arsenal’s home.

Bruno Guimaraes joined in a £75million move from Newcastle last week and was unveiled to the fans before the meeting with Dortmund.

That came after Illan Meslier’s arrival as a free agent and Piero Hincapie became a permanent member of the squad.

Christos Tzolis has also been a big-money recruit after a £34m deal was struck with Club Brugge.

Sports.title: Wrexham ‘closing in on huge £8million Premier League transfer’ as Ryan Reynolds & Rob McElhenney fund new promotion bid
Sports.content:
WREXHAM are inching towards an £8million deal for Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson, according to multiple sources.

Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney look prepared to bankroll another promotion push with the 26-year-old’s fee already having been agreed.



Both The Athletic and TalkSPORT report that Patterson is set to undergo a medical on Monday before sealing the deal, with no late issues expected to derail the move.

It could be a record-breaking transfer for the Dragons, whose current transfer record stands at £7.5m for Nathan Broadhead last year.



The shot-stopper will be Phil Parkinson’s third signing of the summer as he follows Danny Imray and Ben Whiteman to the Racecourse Ground.

The Sunderland academy product established himself as the club’s first-choice goalkeeper during the 2021/22 campaign.



He was instrumental in helping the Black Cats earn promotion to the Premier League in 2025, producing two crucial saves in the Championship play-off final victory over Sheffield United at Wembley.

But the arrival of Dutch keeper Robin Roefs last summer forced Patterson down the pecking order.

Millwall took him on loan in January.

He made 16 appearances in all competitions for the Lions and featured in both legs of their Championship play-off semi-final against Hull.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd are digging their heels in over two much-needed transfers as they desperately look to change reputation
Sports.content:
AN OFFICIAL at Manchester United said the busiest it got last week was involving the change of coach for the women’s team.

For context, United Women’s press office is depleted as they wait for a new hire to serve out their notice period. So others had to muck in.



Yet you can imagine jaws dropping from online fans whose happiness hinges on transfers. United have not announced an incoming for four weeks.

Sun Sport revealed at the time United would hit “pause” on transfer activity after the flurry of arrivals and reassess the lay of the land.

United have belatedly decided that it is a full back, rather than a winger, they could do with on their left-hand side.



That is not entirely out of choice.

For all the smiles and team bonding that the United squad will enjoy in Maynooth in Ireland this week, there is unease at hierarchical level that their highest earner is back on the books.

The inability to shift Marcus Rashford has effectively blocked United from recruiting a new winger or forward.

The lingering presence of Joshua Zirkzee has also had a bearing.

United cannot just stockpile players if there is not going to be a taker for the one at the back of the queue.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Matheus Cunha and Patrick Dorgu have played on the left wing for Michael Carrick and that is Rashford’s role.

So that is three left wingers. It would be senseless to add another with no guarantee that a club’s executive will pick up the phone and offer to take Rashford off United’s hands.

United have leverage to reinforce at left back as Luke Shaw’s deputy is the teenager Harry Amass.

United are prepared to cash in on Amass after his eye-catching performances on loan at Sheffield Wednesday.

United have misread the market, though. They took so long to decide on a left back that by the time they turned to Lewis Hall Newcastle had sold Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes for £244m.



The fire sale has to be extinguished at some stage.

Hall wants to leave Newcastle, which possibly gives United enough encouragement to persist.

But they have underestimated how they are viewed on Tyneside, where many are convinced a mythical rivalry continues from the Kevin Keegan era 30 years ago.



Newcastle have not sold a player to United since Andy Cole in January 1995, such a scandalous sale that Keegan addressed disgruntled fans on the St James’ Park steps.

United have bought players from Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham more recently.

United’s early error was to make a beeline for the Atalanta midfielder Ederson, who had a year left on his contract.

That deal collapsed and the £35m was at least better spent on Youri Tielemans.

Following the success of recruiting the Premier League-ready Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo last year, the logical first move was for Mateus Fernandes (Elliot Anderson was City-bound by then).



Real Madrid and Arsenal stepped aside to seemingly leave United with a free run at the Portuguese.

Then they were blown out of the water by Tottenham.

Anderson moved for £116m and Fernandes cost £85m. The market inflation means the going rate for a Premier League-class midfielder is a minimum £80m and United do not believe Alex Scott or Carlos Baleba are worth that.



It did not reflect well on United that their interest in winger Crysencio Summerville emerged only for him to take the money and run to Saudi Arabia.

As understandable as it was of United not to fork out £85m for the twice-relegated Fernandes, seeing two targets at West Ham go to relegation fodder and the Middle East is an unflattering look.

United’s financial discipline is overdue, though. They need a few calm summers to live down their reputation of overspending.

The Casemiro, Antony, Andre Onana and Rasmus Hojlund deals occurred within the past four years.

The salary structure is stricter. The days when Mino Raiola had United over a barrel are long gone and chief executive Omar Berrada publicly stressed before taking over at United that the club would not “overpay”.



Ideally, Bruno Fernandes would be the best-paid player to reflect his best-player status.

It is awkward for United that Rashford, scorer of 15 goals for his parent club in three years, is above Fernandes.

Glancing at the 13 Ineos-era signings, they only fell into the overpaying trap with Manuel Ugarte, a deal agreed for £50.75m.



United trumpeted that as a triumph, claiming Paris Saint-Germain wanted the £50m up front.

Berrada ensured United did not break the £60m barrier for a signing in his first summer in 2024.

That changed in the second out of necessity as United had failed to qualify for the Champions League in their worst season in 51 years.

Cunha had a release clause (£62.5m) and although negotiations for Mbeumo and Sesko took their overall fees north of £70m, the investments paid off. Their matchwinners banked 29 Premier League points.

As much as United are reining in their spending, they also have to live up to their billing as one of the world’s biggest clubs.



The players have been queuing up to talk up a title challenge and the squad needs more than Tielemans and Andrey Santos to be equipped for that.

United certainly have the headroom. Big earners are gone (Casemiro and Jadon Sancho), Champions League-related bonuses have kicked in from sponsors and Old Trafford regularly sells out.

City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham have made statement signings in Elliot Anderson, Bruno Guimaraes, Morgan Rogers and Sandro Tonali. At the time of their arrivals, Santos and Tielemans were not necessarily considered certain starters at the weekend.



The upcoming season will be the true litmus test of Carrick as a United coach, with no free midweeks.

United play their first seven games in 29 days. Carrick’s first seven matches in charge last term took place over 43 days.

When Carrick joined the coaching staff in 2018, he had a baptism of fire as assistant to Jose Mourinho.

On the pre-season tour of the United States, Mourinho’s first words related to United’s preparation were, “Our pre-season is very bad.” It got worse amid in-house briefing and counter-briefing.

Mourinho publicly agitated for two more players he never got. United will not encounter any rancour from the non-confrontational Carrick whilst the transfer window remains open.



Carrick has done barely any external media over the past month but is scheduled to speak to dedicated correspondents in Ireland this week.

It is an opportunity for him to make gentle demands or explicitly highlight weaknesses in the squad – no support striker for Benjamin Sesko, no outright defensive midfielder and no senior left back as the long-term heir to Shaw.

Amazon are scheduled to film Carrick’s sit-down with journalists. That the documentary was confirmed less than a month after Carrick’s promotion to permanent head coach spoke volumes of the stability United have enjoyed since Ruben Amorim engineered his sacking in a press conference.

Yet should Carrick toe the party line, it could count against him in the long run with the fanbase. It is a tactful balancing act, championing the current squad and acknowledging its flaws without going nuclear.

There is no danger of Carrick doing the latter. There are enough fans online who have done that already.

Sports.title: 'Dubois has ingredients to replace Taylor as face of boxing'
Sports.content:
Caroline Dubois "has the ingredients" to succeed Katie Taylor as one of the biggest stars in boxing, according to Most Valuable Promotions partner Nakisa Bidarian.

Ireland's undisputed super-lightweight world champion Taylor, who turned 40 in July, is set to fight professionally for the final time in an undisputed world super-lightweight title fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on September 5.

A week earlier, lightweight world champion Dubois will seek to maintain her unbeaten record when she defends her WBC and WBO straps against American Amelia Moore, live on Sky Sports on the undercard of Chantelle Cameron's clash with Mikaela Mayer.

Bidarian told Sky Sports: "For me, the poster fighters of the sport have been Amanda Serrano and Katie Taylor, the two of them have been real trailblazers.

"It's sad to see that arc transition in September for Katie, I think Amanda probably has one more fight left after August 21.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Caroline Dubois' clash with Terri Harper for the WBC and WBO lightweight title.

"But women's boxing has never been stronger. It's a young sport, it became an Olympic sport in 2012 where Katie was the beneficiary, and she's created a storied career for herself.

"But we feel good about the future of this sport we feel like we have a roster of athletes. Caroline Dubois is one who I think has the ingredients of Katie Taylor, Amanda Serrano, Laila Ali, Christy Martin and Ronda Rousey all there.

"Of course, the sport's going to miss Katie, of course the ring is going to miss Amanda, but the sport is in a great place."

Salita says Shields is 'definitively No 1'

Undisputed heavyweight champion Claressa Shields is already "definitively" the No 1 fighter in women's boxing, according to her promoter Dmitry Salita.

Two-time Olympic gold medallist Shields has been an undisputed champion in the professional ranks in three weight classes, winning all 18 of her fights.

Asked about Shields' status in the sport amid Taylor's career coming to a close, Salita told Sky Sports earlier this year: "Katie Taylor is a historic figure in boxing, and I've said many times - personally and professionally - that I'm a fan of hers and what she has done for the sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Claressa Shields says Britain's Caroline Dubois could even eclipse her own achievements.

"That said, Claressa Shields is definitively the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in women's boxing today.

"What separates Claressa is not just what she's accomplished in the ring which already stands on its own but the totality of her impact.

"There is something more to being a bona fide superstar than simply being elite in the ring. There's an "it" factor. The ability to headline, to sell out arenas, to create moments, to carry events regardless of the opponent - and Claressa has that.



"She may be the first woman in the history of the sport consistently selling out major arenas regardless of opponent."

Will Shields vs Price happen?

Shields is dropping down from heavyweight in an attempt to become middleweight world champion once more, with the 31-year-old taking on Australian Kaye Scott in Atlanta this weekend.

The fight could be a precursor for a possible blockbuster with Britain's own world champion Lauren Price, who currently holds three of the four welterweight belts.

Talks have previously taken place over Shields and Price meeting at the middleweight, and despite an impasse in negotiations, Salita remains optimistic the fight can happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Claressa Shields discusses a potential fight with Lauren Price and insists that the pair could fight in both America and back in the United Kingdom for a rematch.

"When Claressa went to Wales, we believed we had the framework of a deal in place, and we're still operating in that spirit," Salita told Sky Sports last month.

"I believe we're close. Claressa is moving down to 160 pounds because she wants to make this fight happen. She's already accomplished so much, but she's always looking for the biggest global fights.

"Lauren is an outstanding fighter and an Olympic gold medallist. This is one of the biggest fights that can be made in women's boxing, and we're confident it will happen.

"Claressa has always done her part to make the biggest fights possible, and this is no different. We're ready to continue the discussions."

Sports.title: Stella issues rivals warning over McLaren 'momentum' in title battles
Sports.content:
McLaren boss Andrea Stella has issued a warning to his team's rivals for the remainder of the 2026 season as he expressed confidence in the Woking squad's ability to maintain momentum once it has been gained.

The reigning constructors' champions claimed a long-awaited first victory of the season in the final race before the summer break as reigning drivers' champion Lando Norris dominated in Hungary.

The result brought Norris back to within 91 points of championship leader Kimi Antonelli, while McLaren closed the gap on the Italian's Mercedes team to 159 points. To retain his title, Norris would also need to leapfrog Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Charles Leclerc, while Ferrari are only 72 points back from Mercedes in the team standings.

While both margins are considerable, Norris' performance following a significant upgrade package in Budapest has provided Stella with belief that McLaren can continue to perform strongly over the remaining 12 rounds of the season, starting with the Dutch Grand Prix from August 21-23.

Asked whether his team can get back into the fight for world titles, Stella said: "That's a difficult question, but there's a very clear answer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Norris' victory last time out in Hungary, David Croft debates whether McLaren are now capable of winning further races or not

"If we can continue the season as we did in Budapest, we can still achieve a great deal. To do so, we must keep pushing with the development of the MCL40 and ensure we outpace our rivals - who certainly aren't standing still - in this race within the race, which is the competition over updates.

"The result will depend on how effective the solutions we bring to the track prove to be. In the first part of the season, we struggled more than we expected in this regard too, but I believe that in recent years, once we've gained some momentum, we've been able to maintain it."

McLaren were in a contrasting position this time last year, having reached the summer break with a 299-point lead in the constructors' standings, and Oscar Piastri leading team-mate Norris in what appeared to be a two-horse race for the drivers' title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

However, Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who trailed Piastri by 104 points with nine rounds remaining, staged a remarkable fightback to ultimately finish the season just two points behind Norris and 11 ahead of Piastri.

Stella added: "There are still 12 races left on the calendar, so there are plenty of opportunities given that 546 points are up for grabs.

"Of course, the gap in both championships is significant, but we remember last year's lesson well: after all, I always tell the team that if we've set up a new display cabinet to house the new, recent trophies at the McLaren Technology Centre, then we have a duty to do our utmost to keep filling it..."

Hungary upgrade represented 'change of direction'

McLaren had played down the upgrade package they brought to Hungary ahead of the event, but the results spoke for themselves as Norris took pole before showing searing pace to win the race.

The Brit ultimately beat Verstappen by 15 seconds but had he not been held up by Piastri for the first half of the race having been overtaken by his team-mate on the opening lap, the margin could have been far greater.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris snatches pole off Lewis Hamilton as Max Verstappen and George Russell struggle in Q3 at Hungaroring

Reflecting on the process that led to the latest upgrades, Stella said: "There wasn't a single event that changed course; rather, it was a growing awareness of the scale of the challenge we're facing and the adjustments we needed to make.

"Paradoxically, the enforced break in April probably allowed us to focus entirely on analysing the MCL40's performance and to fully understand that we needed to redirect or strengthen its development in certain areas of the car.

"It is clear that the Budapest weekend, which brought the first half of the season to a close, was the highlight: not only because of the result, but above all because the aerodynamic package we introduced at the Hungaroring is the result of this change of direction in development and has enabled us to make significant progress in terms of competitiveness."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

Stella also praised the work his team have done alongside engine supplier Mercedes to optimise the performance of their power unit.

"Over the past few months we've had the opportunity to deepen our understanding of the new power unit supplied by Mercedes HPP and to work with our technical partners to work out how best to utilise it," he added.

"It's been a long process, with its ups and downs, but one that's starting to bear fruit. That said, I expect that optimising the power unit will remain a complex issue throughout the 2026 season."

Sports.title: Amazon founder Bezos nears deal to buy stake in Liverpool
Sports.content:
Sky News understands a consortium including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is closing in on a deal to buy a roughly one-third stake in Liverpool.

Sky News has learnt that Fenway Sports Group (FSG), the Anfield club's controlling shareholder since 2010, is preparing to make an announcement about a transaction as soon as this week.

The deal will see Mr Bezos participate in an investor group alongside Eduardo Saverin, one of the co-founders of the social network Facebook.

The syndicate is led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and until recently a shareholder in Championship club Queens Park Rangers.

One source indicated that an announcement was expected in the coming days, although they cautioned that it could slip into next week.

If completed, the deal would install a trio of the world's wealthiest individuals as co-owners of the Reds, one of the most successful teams in the history of English football.

Mr Bezos alone has a fortune estimated by Forbes at over £207bn ($280bn), while Mr Saverin is said to be worth over £23.7bn ($32bn).

Their investment in Liverpool will reportedly value the club at £4.4bn ($6bn), making it one of the sport's richest-ever deals.

Sky Sports News has contacted Liverpool and FSG for comment.

Image: Amazon founder Bezos has an estimated fortune of over £207bn

While Mr Bezos has not previously been linked to deals in football, his prospective involvement in the Liverpool FC consortium underlines the extent to which sport is now viewed by wealthy investors as an asset class in its own right.

Mr Saverin, who is 44 years old, was part of a consortium which assembled an unsuccessful takeover bid for Chelsea FC during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

One insider said the deal was now expected to be slightly larger than previously thought, potentially involving a stake of over 30 per cent.

Nevertheless, if its valuation hits £4.4bn ($6bn), the deal will reinforce the huge financial success that FSG has enjoyed during its 16 years as the club's owner.

The Boston Red Sox owner acquired Liverpool for just £300m with the club in a troubled state financially.

The arrival of such a powerful consortium will fuel expectations that its members will ultimately seek outright control of the Reds.

A spokesperson for FSG said last month: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

FSG declined to comment further on the potential timing of a deal.

A spokesman for the consortium led by Mr Bhatia also declined to comment.

The last time a stake in Liverpool changed hands was in 2023, when Dynasty Equity bought a small interest valuing it at more than £3.3bn ($4.5bn).

Analysis: Why Bezos development should be met with some caution

Image: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos (right) is nearing deal to buy stake in Liverpool as part of Amit Bhatia's consortium (Evan Agostini/Invision/AP)

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"It is massive for the future of Liverpool. We have to be careful, though. There may be a few supporters uneasy at the prospect of being part-owned by one of the richest men in the world.

"When people invest or buy clubs, who previously don't have a link to the club, the duty is to ask why they want to invest. What is in it for them?

"There will be a section of Liverpool supporters who will be delighted at the prospect of Jeff Bezos, who is worth around £207bn, owning a stake in your club.

"I would treat the development with some caution - until we hear why this group of investors want to invest in Liverpool. People invest because they want to make money.

"A lot of rich people in recent years have thought it is worth owning a Premier League club. Not just because they can make you money and increase in value, but because they are a trophy asset.

"I think the deal will go through; it would value Liverpool at £4.5bn. The last big Premier League club that changed hands was Chelsea; it was worth £2.5bn.

"It is a stunning return for FSG. I reported on them buying Liverpool 16 years ago for £300m.

"Going forward, Liverpool will be even richer than they already are. They have a massive turnover and it will only get bigger with these investors."

Image: FSG have been in complete control of Liverpool since 2010

Sky Sports takes a look at some of the key questions surrounding the sale of a minority stake in Liverpool...

Who are Bhatia and Bezos?

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British Indian entrepreneur who has an investment banking background.

He currently manages a multi-asset investment firm called AyBe Capital, which invests in a range of diversified sectors including technology, media, property and real estate, consumer retail, and health.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is one of the most famous businessmen in the world and the owner of e-commerce giant Amazon, which he founded in 1994 out of his Seattle garage.

His other investments include aerospace company Blue Origin and venture capital firm Nash Holdings, which is the ownership vehicle for The Washington Post.

Sports.title: Super League's Final Charge: Play-off spots taking shape with five rounds left
Sports.content:
There are just five rounds of Super League action remaining and, with it, a whole lot of drama as Super League's Final Charge ramps up.

Seven teams remain in contention for a play-off spot and most of those are still eyeing a top-two finish.

In Super League, the two teams who finish in first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

There are going to be so many twists and turns along the way and you can catch them all live on Sky Sports.

With that in mind, let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

1) Leeds Rhinos (36 points)

Leeds Rhinos have been sitting pretty at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their five remaining fixtures.

They stayed top in spectacular fashion with a win over Wakefield Trinity in their latest game, showing they mean business.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last five matches, they face Leigh Leopards (H), York Knights (A), St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

That means they have three teams in their run-in who are hunting play-off places. If they can remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

2) Wigan Warriors (34 points)

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he is pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Bradford Bulls (A), Wakefield Trinity (H), Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

Wigan are likely to have their sights firmly set on ensuring they beat Wakefield and Leeds to pile on the pressure.

3) Wakefield Trinity (32 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caius Faatili produced an incredible run as he set up Caleb Hamlin-Uele's try for Wakefield against Leeds

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity. They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds.

Wakefield returned to Super League last year following their relegation in 2024 and have lit up the competition, their star-studded side becoming a formidable one.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Sinfield scored for Wakefield against his father's former side Leeds as rugby league legend Kevin watched on proudly

They have games against St Helens (H), Wigan Warriors (A), York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left. That is four teams out of the seven still in the fight.

They will look at York as an absolute must-win and crucial two points. The Wigan and Warrington games will also be key as they are two other teams right in the chase for a top-two spot.

4) Warrington Wolves (30 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Bradford Bulls and Warrington Wolves as Matty Ashton scored twice in a dominant 42-4 victory for the visitors

Warrington Wolves, along with Hull KR, have six matches remaining thanks to their rescheduled round-two match.

This was moved due to the Robins playing in Las Vegas.

With that, it is a more jam-packed Final Charge for them but also one gives Sam Burgess' side a good opportunity to prosper.

In their remaining fixtures, they face York Knights (H), Hull KR (A), Huddersfield Giants (H), Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

If the Wolves are going to be contenders, they will have to pick up points against the four lowly sides they face.

5) Hull KR (28 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Castleford Tigers against Hull KR from the Super League

The other side with six games remaining, Hull KR, are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way and climb as high up the table as possible.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their remaining six matches are against Catalans Dragons (H), Warrington Wolves (H), Toulouse Olympique (H), Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

Four out of the six are at Craven Park, which will only boost their chances. Wins against Catalans, Toulouse and Huddersfield will also be a non-negotiable.

6) Leigh Leopards (28 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against York Knights from the Super League

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Leeds Rhinos (A), Bradford Bulls (H), Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

No one can deny that is a difficult Final Charge, but if Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to show their steel now.

7) St Helens (24 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League

St Helens have five matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their most recent loss to Hull FC, it is fair to say St Helens look down and out.

However, they will now refocus and aim for five wins out of five to be in with a shout. If they win all five, they move to 34 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus announced his side will take on Hull FC in a Super League clash in Dublin on April 25

Not only that, they face some of the other play-off chasing teams so some matches basically become worth four points.

They will take on Wakefield Trinity (A), Castleford Tigers (H), Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

Four out of their five remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do somehow find some form, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.
