Sports.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
Sports.content:
Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”.

In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

The three confederations have started preliminary discussions about the organisation of new competitions along with Uefa’s repeated threats to boycott Fifa events. As things stand, next month’s under-20 women’s World Cup could take place without European teams and alternative options are being sought.

The letter is signed by the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, his AFC counterpart, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, and the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani. Efforts to unite around a suitable candidate to replace Infantino have stepped up since his privately backed plan was revealed and Montagliani is believed to be among the contenders.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” part of the letter reads. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it. When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

It strongly criticises Fifa’s response to the crisis, when a meeting between a small number of senior staff in Rabat was followed by an apology from Infantino that appeared not to show remorse for the scheme.

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani consoles Lionel Messi after the World Cup final. He is believed to be interested in running for the Fifa presidency. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment,” the letter says. “It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment – not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

The three presidents also call for an independent review, conducted by a body outside football, into the affair. Fifa had previously committed to presenting a full report to the Fifa Council at its next scheduled meeting.

The letter directly addresses concerns that countries may lose out on financial aid under a different leadership, saying it is “[not] about any member association losing the support it has earned, despite the fearmongering directed at our leadership to suggest otherwise”.

The letter concludes: “There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness … Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, with leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

51:14 Infantino hangs on by a thread and the overhaul at Newcastle | Football Weekly – video

Any candidates for the Fifa election must announce their bid by 18 November. The confederations are understood to consider all options in their push for Infantino to be replaced, provided they fit within Fifa’s statutes and governance framework.

While the letter outlines the stances of the three confederations, and particularly their leaderships, the story is more complicated within individual member associations. Few outside Europe have been willing to come out publicly against Infantino and only a small minority have been tempted to recall the letters of support they had sent backing his re-election next March. The influential African and South American confederations, Caf and Conmebol, have come out backing Infantino in recent days.

A number of larger member associations have written to Infantino asking for a meeting where he would be required to explain his actions around the FFE scheme. No response has been received. Nor has Infantino been in touch with federations to address his leading role in the turmoil.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 2: Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

The image of John McGinn hoisting aloft the Europa League trophy in Istanbul as the confetti cannons fired is crystallised in the minds of Aston Villa supporters, but less than three months on, plenty has changed since one of the club’s greatest days. Three major players from the starting lineup – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, two of whom scored – have exited, and another may follow if Arsenal make a serious play for the dependable Ezri Konsa.

A key trio of coaches have also left – the set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, assistant manager Pako Ayestarán and the influential individual coach, Antonio Rodríguez Saravia – but most importantly the common denominator and driver of Villa’s incredible rebirth remains in post. It is a good job Unai Emery enjoys a challenge. It has been a typically busy summer, with pre-season trips to Portugal, Indonesia and Hong Kong, plus the Super Cup against Paris St-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday and a friendly trip to Mönchengladbach to follow, but there is work to do if Emery is to repeat the feat of fourth place and break new ground, again, by securing Champions League qualification for successive campaigns.

After a terrible start, Villa edged over the line last season, but the landscape is unlikely to be so forgiving this time. Nobody played more minutes for Villa than Rogers and it was no surprise Villa’s alarming drop in form around spring coincided with Tielemans being injured. Villa need their replacements to work. João Gomes, a £38m buy from Wolves, looks a smart fit; the tigerish Brazil midfielder made the third-highest number of tackles in the division last season (107) and was fourth on the list for ball recoveries (194). Johan Manzambi is one of the game’s most exciting young talents, while Emery believes he can rehabilitate Alejandro Garnacho, who has joined on a season-long loan from Chelsea.

Only Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester City have amassed more Premier League points in the three-and-a-half years since Emery arrived, and while it would be foolish to write him off, every season his task seems to get that bit harder. He can still call on a core cast of reliable performers in Konsa, McGinn, Matty Cash, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins, while Boubacar Kamara’s return from injury this month is a timely boost. But it is hard not to wonder whether Villa have peaked.

Off-field picture

The response of a senior executive was telling when asked if qualifying for the Champions League makes life easier when it comes to meeting the financial rules. “Not easier but less difficult,” came the reply. Villa have since signed a lucrative shirt sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, worth about £20m per season, though Amnesty International warns Rwanda “is using sportswashing to deflect attention from its terrible human rights record”. Meanwhile, Villa Park’s makeover continues with the North Stand closed for the season, the stadium’s capacity falling to 37,000 during its redevelopment. The new-look stand will have a steel roof, modern facade and accommodate more than 50,000 supporters, and will be ready for 2027-28 and Euro 2028.

Owner-fan relationship

Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens will always be adored for putting Villa firmly back on the map, elevating them to become major Premier League players and, ultimately, as the people who gave Emery the keys to transform the club. Both joined the on-field celebrations in Istanbul in May, Sawiris with a claret-and-blue scarf around his neck. Michael Angelakis, chair of investment company Atairos and chief executive of Comcast, acquired a minority stake in 2023. The story goes that Sawiris, Egypt’s richest man, handed Emery a blank sheet of paper and asked him to design his vision when meeting the Basque for the first time in Madrid, at the home of the agent Jorge Mendes.

The manager

“He lives like a monk in a tracksuit,” was how Villa’s director of football operations and Emery’s right-hand man, Damian Vidagany, described the 54-year-old manager’s work ethic in the book Waking The Giant. During the season it is not unusual for Emery, who has an apartment in Birmingham city centre, to spend 12 hours a day at Villa’s Bodymoor Heath base, sometimes analysing footage on his laptop while on the exercise bike or treadmill, long after his players have gone. Emery’s squad have grown accustomed to long meetings, sometimes twice a day – one was held less than 12 hours after cementing their place in the Champions League after beating Liverpool in May, in preparation for Emery to clinch a record fifth Europa League title of his coaching career.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi looks pleased to be wearing the claret and blue. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

There were a few nerves at Villa as Manzambi illuminated Switzerland’s World Cup, concerns his price could balloon or that bigger fish may blow them out of the water. But Villa had done their homework and got a longstanding target over the line for a club-record £51m amid interest from rivals. Manzambi was on Villa’s radar long before he impressed against them for Freiburg in the Europa League final. Murat Yakin, the Switzerland head coach, described Manzambi as “a street footballer”, saying the 20-year-old’s humility and quality means he is capable of playing across the pitch. He played regularly as a No 8 in the Bundesliga and Emery is an admirer of his versatility.

Stat attack

Aston Villa scored 15 goals from outside the box last season. Seven teams had recorded more in one of the previous 17 Premier League campaigns, but no side in that period bettered their 8.4% shot conversion rate. As only 3.6% of attempts from this range are converted on average, Villa’s 2025-26 tally feels impossible to repeat.

Set for a breakthrough

It will be interesting to see if the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, son of former Plymouth and Shrewsbury forward Guy, can build on his encouraging pre-season form. Emery and his coaches are big fans of Madjo, a physical striker born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, so no wonder this month Villa welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) clearing Madjo to feature after Fifa rules prohibited him from playing after joining from Metz in a £10m deal in January. “English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo,” McGinn posted on social media. It has been a whirlwind 12 months for Madjo: he made his Ligue 1 debut last August aged 16, before scoring on debut for England Under-17s a few weeks later. Four goals in pre-season has led to a sense that his first competitive minutes for Villa are close.

World Cup impact

Amadou Onana, whose Villa career has been stop-start owing to injury, ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in Belgium’s last-16 win over the USA. Manzambi enjoyed a fine World Cup, even if his tournament also ended with a knee injury, ruling him out of Switzerland’s last 16 and quarter-final matches and delaying his Villa debut. Martínez made it to another final with Argentina. Konsa started every game for England before the semi-final against Argentina: his 72nd-minute introduction from the bench for Anthony Gordon widely pinpointed as a negative change that invited pressure.

Sports.title: Infantino hangs on by a thread and the overhaul at Newcastle: Football Weekly – podcast
Sports.content:
On today’s podcast: we’ve all been there … tried to sell the World Cup on a Monday, get threatened with a boycott on Tuesday, wildly backtrack on a Wednesday, and you’re issuing further denials on Thursday and Friday and Saturday.

Max and the panel take you through the Fifa story and find out if Gianni Infantino will cling hold to power. Beyond Uefa, is there enough of a groundswell to actually get rid of him?

Elsewhere, the panel play catch-up, talking about Eddie Howe leaving Newcastle, and paying tribute to Kevin Keegan.

There’s too much transfer news, and the start of the Carabao Cup was at the weekend. Plus, Rangers drop more points in the Scottish Premiership in Fitba Corner.

Support the Guardian here.

You can also find Football Weekly on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube.

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille valueing Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and open their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona are confident of landing Rodri from City, but will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint-Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester teenager Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of a deal for the 18-year-midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of messing with his mental health after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, are understood to have agreed four-year contracts with the option of a further 12 months. They are expected to have medicals on Monday.

McNeil, who has entered the final year of his Everton contract, appeared to be moving to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season.

They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League, but then pulled out. McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, wrote an emotional post on Instagram saying there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been affected.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

Johnson has been disappointing since moving to Palace, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given he signed a four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid, but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Palace are also finalising a deal to sign Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m. The Israel right-back had his medical on Sunday and is expected to sign a five-year contract. The 21-year-old’s move to Internazionale broke down last month after he failed a medical.

Sports.title: Arsenal step up push for defensive cover with Timber and Saliba sidelined
Sports.content:
Arsenal are stepping up their efforts to sign defensive cover for William Saliba after Mikel Arteta revealed Jurriën Timber is well away from returning to competitive action. Saliba will be sidelined for an extended period after breaking down during the World Cup with a back injury.

After Arsenal lost a second successive friendly when Borussia Dortmund won 3-2 on Sunday to lift the Emirates Cup in a performance that featured several defensive mistakes, Arteta would not be drawn on when the France defender is expected to return, but said it would take “some time to heal”.

There are also concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that led him to miss most of the run-in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

“William Saliba is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, an aggravated injury, so it’s going to take some time to heal.”

Pressed on how Arsenal will cope without Saliba, he said: “We have experienced that in the past, unfortunately. When he’s been available, he’s hit home and the stats are incredible. We know we lost a massive player, the same with Jurriën.”

Arsenal have had a bid for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected and are expected to return with a new offer for the England defender, who is also capable of playing at right-back. Villa value him at £60m, but with less than two years left on his contract Arsenal are unwilling to pay that much for the 28-year-old. The Premier League champions have also shown an interest in signing Cristian Romero from Tottenham, but any move for the Argentina defender is extremely unlikely given Spurs’ reluctance to sell to their north London rivals.

Arteta, who started with Cristhian Mosquera in central defence alongside Gabriel Magalhães against Dortmund, said Arsenal’s existing players must get up to speed before Sunday’s Community Shield against Manchester City, but did not rule out bringing in another defender.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better,” he said. “We conceded some poor goals today, in the way we competed especially. But that’s a collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players we have.”

Sports.title: Van Dijk looks forward to more quality arriving at Liverpool before new season
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk is ready to welcome Ronald Araújo as his new centre-back partner at Liverpool with the deal to sign the Barcelona defender almost complete.

Van Dijk played almost an hour, his first pre-season appearance, as Liverpool were beaten 3-2 by Monaco at Anfield, having led 2-0. The Dutchman fouled Aleksandr Golovin to concede a penalty just before the break, which Golovin scored.

Jérémy Jacquet remained absent, with Liverpool’s new £50m arrival being treated with kid gloves after an injury-hit spell at the end of last season with Rennes. Araújo has been signed to bolster Andoni Iraola’s defensive options, with Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni also sidelined.

“Any player that arrives at the club we will be welcoming,” Van Dijk said of Araújo. “I have no idea if it has been announced or not. I have not seen him so let’s see.”

Van Dijk was upbeat about Jacquet and the prospect of more transfer activity between now and the transfer deadline on 1 September. Liverpool are keen on adding to their forward line with Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola of interest.

“Let’s see what the next couple of weeks are going to bring. Any quality we can add to the team will definitely be welcome so let’s see.

“I’ve not seen any of him. I’ve spoken to him,” Van Dijk said of Jacquet. “I’ve seen him walking around and we have conversations. I can’t wait to see him back on the pitch and I hope that happens very soon. I’m not a doctor, so I don’t know exactly the situation, but I have a feeling this week he could be back on the pitch, hopefully as soon as possible.”

While Van Dijk accepted Liverpool are in a transition period after the sacking of Arne Slot, he revealed he has been in regular contact with Iraola and offered his full support to the new head coach.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Van Dijk said: “We had a great conversation in the first week when it got announced and the main thing for him to know is I am here for him regardless, anything he needs, wants to know, wants me to do for the team or whatever. Hopefully we will be successful this season.

“Nothing to take away from Arne and his staff, we had an amazing time together, but obviously last year [was] a disappointment. This year we have a new manager who has new ways of preparation, so we have to adapt to the new staff, different training methods. I liked working under Arne and I am sure I will like working under the new manager.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Endrick set for Villa loan? De Jong offered in Rodri deal?
Sports.content:
A sense of excitement is what Aston Villa need at the moment after selling off key players. What better way to create it than signing a prodigious talent from Real Madrid? The Villans have inquired about the Brazilian Endrick, who impressed on loan at Lyon last season, and may make a similar temporary move to the Premier League.

Manchester City are not particularly keen to sell Rodri but, with a year left on his contract money may well talk, especially if the midfielder wants to leave. Barcelona’s first bid was rejected but they are readying another. One idea is to offer Frenkie de Jong as part of the deal, so at least Enzo Maresca would have a shiny new midfielder to play with.

One player who could be leaving Camp Nou is the World Cup-winning goalscorer Ferran Torres, who has reportedly told Paris Saint-Germain he wants to pop across to the French capital. Not that a deal between the clubs has been agreed.

Another potential swap deal is on the cards between Everton and Crystal Palace. Calls have been made to discuss Dwight McNeil moving to Selhurst Park and Brennan Johnson swapping places with him at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The two wingers have struggled for game time perhaps a swap would reignite their careers. McNeil almost ended up at Selhurst Park in January before a late breakdown in talks left the player and his family furious.

Promoted Ipswich have been active in the market and could add the Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. A bid has been faxed over, leaving the Tractor Boys to play the waiting game, but they may face competition for his signature.

After what must have been a lot of wrangling, Chelsea have agreed to loan Filip Jörgensen to sister club Strasbourg. The Blues are well-stocked with players and need to bin a few who can’t be sent to Strasbourg, so they may allow Jamie Gittens to head on loan to Roma.

The departure of Bruno Guimarães will prompt a rethink at Newcastle, who rather desperately need a new central midfielder. Sandro Tonali was sold a while back, giving the club some cash to play with, but they still seem to be thinking about signing João Palhinha who is not wanted at Bayern Munich The former Tottenham man Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is another option. Palhinha is also of interest to Aston Villa, who have made contact with the Bundesliga champions.

Manchester United are planning for the future with a move for the Leicester teenager Louis Page. The 18-year-old came through the academy ranks with the Foxes, but is naturally more than happy to take the leap from League One.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

And finally: Shea Charles is closing on a move from Southampton to Fulham for a roaring £30m.

Sports.title: Newcastle’s Bruno Guimaraes replacement rejects club in bombshell transfer twist
Sports.content:
Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has turned down the opportunity to join Newcastle, talkSPORT understands.

The Magpies had zeroed in on Hojbjerg as a replacement for Bruno Guimaraes, who moved to Arsenal last Saturday.

2 Hojbjerg has previous Premier League experience Credit: Getty Images - Getty

It is understood Newcastle were ready to meet Marseille's valuation of Hojbjerg, but the Dane ultimately wanted to remain put.

Hojbjerg was viewed as an ideal candidate to fill the void left by Guimaraes due to his leadership qualities and vast Premier League experience.

Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg's extensive Premier League experience

The 31-year-old has over 250 top flight appearances to his name, with 145 made during his time at Tottenham and 109 with Southampton.

Hojbjerg last featured in the Premier League during the 2023/24 campaign.

The Dane's decision to reject Newcastle's proposal signifies yet another blow in what has been a tumultuous summer for the club.

Along with Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have both exited St James' Park this summer for significant sums.

Why this summer has been more chaotic than most for Newcastle

Gordon joined Barcelona prior to the World Cup for a cool £70m while Tonali became Tottenham's club record signing as they parted with £100m to land the Italian.

There's also been a change in the dugout as Eddie Howe chose to step down after five years in the dugout.

He has since been replaced by Matthias Jaissle, who joined from Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

Jaissle was almost dealt a crippling blow in his first game in charge of the Magpies when Anthony Elanga was stretchered off against Valencia on Saturday.

2 Jaissle could do with having a Guimaraes replacement lined up before Newcastle's Premier League opener Credit: Getty

Elanga was left worse for wear after he got clattered by Valencia's Jose Luis Gaya in the first half.

The ugly incident sparked a touchline brawl as incensed Magpies players vented their frustration over Gaya's reckless challenge.

Despite the severity of the challenge, Jaissle has since confirmed Elanga's injury 'wasn't serious'.

When is Newcastle next in action?

Jaissle will hope Elanga can fully recover in time for Newcastle's Premier League opener on August 23, when they host Liverpool.

Newcastle still have three additional friendlies to play before the season commences.

Jaissle's side next play Everton on August 12 before clashes against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg.

Sports.title: Ex-Man United star reveals he needs hip replacement just weeks after retiring
Sports.content:
Ex-Man United star reveals he needs hip replacement just weeks after retiring

Ashley Young has revealed he will have to undergo hip replacement surgery after retiring from professional football.

The former England international ended his playing career earlier this summer before turning 41 last month.



3 Young has revealed he requires a hip replacement weeks after retiring Credit: Getty

Young hung up his boots after helping Ipswich Town win promotion to the Premier League.

He made 13 Championship appearances for the Tractor Boys after joining the club last summer.

However, the right-back's final league outing came on January 20 as a hip injury curtailed his season.



Young has now admitted he will require a hip replacement in the future.

Young's surgery

Speaking on the High Performance Podcast, he explained: "I went down on my hip in November and had an injection.



"I have always said to myself: ‘If my body is saying you need injections, there is a problem, you need to think about retiring.’

"Basically I need a hip replacement, in November I was told I would need it in about 10 years time.



"I got to January and was due to have another injection which would have got me through to the end of the season, as I was saying to the specialist ‘I know it is painful, but I want to make sure I do everything I can possibly do to help the team.’

"About a week before I am about to have the injection, I go down on it in training and I am like ‘this is worse, I know it is a lot worse.’"

Young has since been given a two-year window before he will need the surgery.

3 Young has been given a two-year window for hip surgery after hanging up his boots this summer Credit: Getty



It comes after a specialist informed him his hip has become 'much worse' in recent months.

The Premier League winner was even forced to miss training for three months at one stage last season.

He added: "From January to the end of the season, I literally had two or three months where I couldn’t train, it was that painful.

"I saw the specialist again and said ‘I’m not going out like this.’ He said he didn’t want to give me another injection as it would weaken the area.



"I asked him ‘are you telling me I can’t play football again, you can say it if you want, trust me if I get an opportunity to be back on the pitch, I’ll be back on the pitch.’

"The last two months of the season I was training every day and he was like ‘it is not possible, you shouldn’t be training.’"

3 Young won six trophies including a Premier League title with United Credit: Getty

Young's career highlights

Young made a total of 762 senior club appearances across spells with Manchester United, Aston Villa, Watford, Everton, Inter Milan and Ipswich.



He also scored seven goals in 39 caps for the Three Lions between 2007 and 2018.

His time at United saw Young win six trophies including the Premier League, Europa League and FA Cup.

Meanwhile, he later lifted a Serie A title in Italy with Inter.

Sports.title: Newcastle star is one of Europe’s top young keepers who even played up front for former club
Sports.content:
Newcastle star is one of Europe’s top young keepers who even played up front for former club

'Quite simply, when Lukas Hornicek was your goalkeeper, you didn't concede many goals.'

That statement will be music to the ears of Newcastle fans, who have been told their new No.1 is as safe a pair of feet as he is hands.



6 Hornicek impressed on his unofficial Newcastle debut as the Magpies beat Valencia Credit: Getty

Hornicek completed a £25.7million move to Tyneside from Braga at the end of last month and remains the only Newcastle signing during the current window aged older than 21.

The Czech shot-stopper started all but one league match for the Liga Portugal outfit last season to help them secure a fourth-place finish.

On paper, he is an ideal fit for new head coach Matthias Jaissle’s usual high defensive line; only five goalkeepers in Europe’s top 10 leagues registered more keeper sweepings (45) according to Opta last term.



That style of play was first cultivated in the academy of one of Hornicek's first clubs - FK Pardubice in the Czech First League.

Ladislav Matras, now head coach of the regional football academy at the club, first started working with Newcastle's new No.21 when he was in the Under-12s through to Under-15 level.



Hornicek 'really was exceptional'

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com, Matras said: "I remember that in the Under-12 team, whenever we needed to keep a clean sheet, Lukáš played in goal.

"But if we desperately needed to score, we simply pushed him up front. He really was exceptional, both as a footballer and as a person.



"I never heard anyone say a negative word about him. He has always been a fantastic young man and an outstanding athlete."

He continued: "To be honest, I don't think he had any obvious weaknesses. Our goalkeeper coaches – Tuček, Volšík, Shejbal and others – worked with him on every aspect of goalkeeping in a comprehensive way.

6 The young goalkeeper featured at last year's Euro Under-21 Championship finals in Slovakia, starting in Group B fixtures against England Credit: Getty

"He always had outstanding physical attributes, which is a huge advantage for any goalkeeper.



"He was exceptionally tall for his age, but despite that, he was also remarkably agile and athletic.

"Because he had plenty of experience playing outfield, he was also very comfortable with the ball at his feet.

"He quickly outgrew the competition in his own age group, so we decided to move him up a level. In fact, he practically skipped the Under-14 category altogether and went straight into the Under-15 team."

Hornicek's ability with his feet saw him boast the second-best 100 per cent success rate at sweeping behind Barcelona's Joan Garcia (52).



Matras added: "He was outstanding in almost every position on the pitch. He could play anywhere without any problems, but he was always naturally drawn to goalkeeping, and we were all very happy about that.

6 The 6ft 6inch shot-stopper was an unused substitute for all three of Czechia's Group A fixtures at the World Cup Credit: Getty

"I don't want to take anything away from the other boys in his age group, but there was always a huge difference between having Lukas in goal and having anyone else there.

"Quite simply, when Lukáš Horníček was your goalkeeper, you didn't concede many goals!"



That was most evident last term when the 6ft 6in star recorded 24 clean sheets across all competitions.

Hornicek even saved three of the 10 penalties he faced, including one from Morgan Gibbs-White in a 1-0 defeat for Nottingham Forest.

6 Newcastle moved quickly to beat out other European clubs to his signature

His rapid rise to the top comes as little surprise to those at Pardubice, with Matras revealing that 'there were many European clubs that showed serious interest in him.'



The biggest sale in club history

Horníček went on trial at Bayer Leverkusen in 2017 and within two years had joined Braga on loan shortly after his 17th birthday.

Carlos Vicens' side made the move permanent after a year in what was Pardubice's biggest sale in the club's history.

Vít Zavřel, Chairman of the Board, told talkSPORT: "Our long-term priority is to invest these funds in a way that brings the greatest possible benefit to the future of FK Pardubice.

"If the club receives extraordinary income, it is directed primarily towards the club's further development rather than simply covering its day-to-day operating costs.



"Specifically, the money will be invested in infrastructure, the continued development of our youth academy, women's football, and creating even better conditions for the first team.

"Our goal is to build the club systematically and with a long-term vision, so that FK Pardubice continues to grow stronger both on and off the pitch and keeps moving to the next level."

6 Horníček made 12 league clean sheets as Os Arcebispos qualified for the Conference League in fourth last season Credit: Getty

Horníček, meanwhile, has gone from strength to strength since leaving his boyhood club - making his Primeira Liga bow in May 2022.



He played an integral part in Braga's run to the Europa League semi-finals, with his seven clean sheets in 14 matches the most of any goalkeeper in last season's competition.

Horníček was rewarded for his form with a senior international debut in May during a 2-1 friendly win against Kosovo.

He was also part of his country's World Cup finals squad this summer before sealing a Premier League switch to St James' Park.

Matras explained to talkSPORT: "For that journey to turn into such a wonderful story is something you can only dream about.



"We are all incredibly happy for him, and we're all cheering him on to reach the very highest level. He has an unbelievable future ahead of him, and he truly deserves it."

6 He will reunite with Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres in the Premier League when Newcastle face Arsenal Credit: AFP

"It's impossible to put that feeling into words", Matras said of the pride in his former starlet becoming Newcastle's first Czech goalkeeper since Pavel Srníček.

"I'm incredibly proud of all my colleagues at FK Pardubice, everyone at the Regional Academy, and all the people who played a part in developing such an exceptional footballer and person as Lukáš Horníček.



"I'm convinced there isn't anyone in Pardubice—or even anywhere in the Czech Republic—who won't be supporting him and wishing him every success."

Sports.title: Where to watch Community Shield: FA make change in 20-year first with Erling Haaland set to return for Man City
Sports.content:
Where to watch Community Shield: FA make change in 20-year first with Erling Haaland set to return for Man City

A rare Community Shield clash takes place this weekend as Arsenal face rivals Manchester City away from Wembley.

The Gunners feature after winning their first Premier League title in 22 years, coming up against Man City, who lifted the FA Cup.



3 Arsenal are playing in the Community Shield after winning the Premier League title Credit: Getty

Both Premier League giants are going to want to get their hands on the first domestic trophy available this campaign.

Their star-studded squads are more than used to playing at Wembley, but in a major change made by the FA, that is not where this year's game is going to be played.

Due to scheduling issues, the Community Shield will not be played at Wembley and instead at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.



It is the first time in 20 years that this fixture has been played at the ground in Wales.

The game between Arsenal and Man City has been moved as music artist The Weeknd is booked in for concerts at Wembley.



So, Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca are going to have to travel with their squads over to Wales for the traditional season opener.

Where to watch Community Shield

The Community Shield will take place on Sunday, August 16.

Kick-off at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff is set for 3pm.

Fans can watch the game live on TV on TNT Sports, while the action will also be available to watch online via HBO Max.



You can 

3 The season opener will not be played at Wembley due to a scheduling conflict Credit: Getty

talkSPORT will also have live coverage of the game from Wales.

Commentary will be coming from Sam Matterface and former England captain Stuart Pearce.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

3 Maresca will only have Haaland and three other stars back days before the game Credit: Getty



Community Shield: Haaland returns

Erling Haaland has not featured at all in Man City's pre-season so far, having had an extended post-World Cup break.

But he's set to return to City training on Wednesday, along with record signing Elliot Anderson, Nico O'Reilly and Marc Guehi.

That only gives Haaland and the English trio five days back with the squad before the Community Shield takes place.

So, will they come straight back into the starting line-up? Or will Maresca take his time reintroducing them?



They are likely to play some part in the game, but it would be a boost for Arsenal if Haaland and co. weren't to start.

Omar Marmoush scored twice in City's win over Atletico Madrid last time out, so the Egyptian could get the nod up front.

Sports.title: Arsenal push to sign new centre-back but are way off Premier League rival’s valuation
Sports.content:
Arsenal push to sign new centre-back but are way off Premier League rival’s valuation

Arsenal are set to step up their efforts to sign a new centre-back before the transfer window closes.

The Gunners have identified the area as a position in need of strengthening amid a potential injury crisis.



3 Mikel Arteta is keen to sign a new centre-back amid Arsenal's injury issues Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta is currently without both William Saliba and Jurrien Timber through injury less than two weeks away from the new season.

Their absences leave Gabriel Magalhaes, Piero Hincapie and Cristhian Mosquera as his only senior recognised central defenders.

Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa is Arsenal's leading target in the position, talkSPORT understands.



A previous approach worth £35million has already been knocked back by the Europa League winners.

Villa value Konsa in excess of £60million, with two years still remaining on his contract.



The England international, who joined the club in 2019, made 48 appearances across all competitions last season.

Arsenal's centre-back search

Several players have been considered by Arsenal at centre-back throughout the summer.



The Gunners have shown recent interest in Cristian Romero amid uncertainty over his Tottenham Hotspur future.

However, the Spurs captain looks set to sign for Atletico Madrid after agreeing personal terms with the club.

John Stones also emerged as a potential signing earlier in the window.

3 Arsenal are set to launch a fresh approach for Konsa, who Villa value at over £60million Credit: Getty



The former Manchester City star has since joined Inter on a free transfer, though.

Arteta's Injury headache

Arteta's desire to strengthen at centre-back has been enforced by the injuries to Timber and Saliba.

The latter has been sidelined since suffering a back injury during France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain last month.

Meanwhile, Timber missed the tournament entirely after he was forced to withdraw from the Netherlands' squad.



Arteta addressed both players' returns following his side's Emirates Cup loss to Borussia Dortmund on Sunday.

He explained: "Jurrien is progressing really well. He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

3 Saliba and Timber are both sidelined less than two weeks before the season starts Credit: Getty

"William Saliba is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, an aggravated injury, so it’s going to take some time to heal."



When asked how Arsenal will cope without Saliba, he added: "We have experienced that in the past, unfortunately.

"When he’s been available, he’s hit home and the stats are incredible. We know we lost a massive player, the same with Jurrien."

The Gunners conclude their pre-season schedule at home to Como on Wednesday.

That match will be followed by the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday against FA Cup winners City.



Arsenal then begin their Premier League title defence with a home clash against newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday, August 21.

Sports.title: Liverpool have serious defensive concerns but must sign £100m-rated man this summer
Sports.content:
Liverpool have serious defensive concerns but must sign £100m-rated man this summer

Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony admitted Liverpool's defending in pre-season gives him 'anxiety'.

The Reds have shipped an alarming seven goals in their last two pre-season friendlies, with three coming in a loss to Monaco on Sunday.

3 Iraola has already warned Reds fans it'll take time before the players are fully up and running in his system Credit: Getty

MacAnthony was especially worried that Monaco's winner was scored via a set-piece.

It was a glaring issue for the Reds last term as they conceded 23 goals from set pieces in the Premier League.

Only Leeds (24), Crystal Palace (25) and Bournemouth (26) conceded more.

Given new Reds boss Andoni Iraola was in charge of Bournemouth last term and they shipped the most, there is serious work to be done.

Although MacAnthony was under no illusion pre-season is rarely an accurate representation of what happens once the campaign properly gets underway, he feels there is still cause for concern.

What was Darragh MacAnthony's verdict on Liverpool's defending?

"Defensively, we should worry," MacAnthony, who doubles as a Liverpool fan, said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"You saw things at the weekend, set-piece goals conceded. That was a real issue for Liverpool last year. The winner for Monaco was a set-piece, someone not picking up a player who's got a free header from three yards out. That happened too often last year.

"(Virgil) Van Dijk, making a mistake again, being clumsy. He's not often clumsy.

"Look, it was messy, defensively. There were a lot of great points attacking-wise, some of the young players did really well. But defensively, we give you anxiety watching the last two games.

"As much as it's pre-season and you've got wingers playing at right-back and midfielders playing at centre-back, it's just a mish-mash at the moment that's uncomfortable to watch.

3 Van Dijk is into the final year of his Liverpool contract Credit: Getty

"I know they're signing the Barcelona guy (Ronald Araujo), there's going to be some strength coming in and players coming back, but they're the things you want to see fixed.

"And I don't like seeing my team give away set-piece goals again. That was a big problem for us last year."

One player who MacAnthony believes would help alleviate some of Liverpool's defensive issues is Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton.

Wharton has previously been tipped for a big move elsewhere, with Manchester United's interest already known.

Why Adam Wharton could be Liverpool's game-changer

But MacAnthony wants to see Liverpool make a big splash in the window by snaring Wharton, who he believes will be a starter for 'the next seven, eight years.'

"I'd love them to sign Adam Wharton," MacAnthony said.

3 Wharton's displays for Palace have caught the eye of several major European clubs Credit: Getty

"I think (Alexis) Mac Allister, for me, his legs were gone last year. It was only when he put an Argentina shirt on that his legs reappeared.

"If you could do business there with him going, I think you bring him (Wharton) in and you've got a player for the next seven, eight years that will be a starter.

"He's got so much upside and potential in him.

"Even if he costs £85-100m or whatever else, you're getting the player for the long term."

Wharton is poised to begin the new season at Palace, who have a Europa League campaign to look forward to thanks to their Conference League triumph.

There's also a new coach at the helm of Palace in Pierre Sage, who takes over from Oliver Glasner after he left at the end of his contract but has since joined Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could make stunning return to English football with Championship club
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy could make stunning return to English football with Championship club

West Ham have inquired about Jamie Vardy as they bid to bolster their attack ahead of the new Championship season.

The 39-year-old is a free agent having left Cremonese following their relegation from Serie A last season.

3 Vardy was training back at Leicester, but only temporarily Credit: @vardy - Instagram

The Hammers are targeting an immediate return to the Premier League following their own fall to the second tier.

The east London outfit made a winning start to the 2026/27 campaign as they beat Portsmouth in the first round of the Carabao Cup on Saturday, with Taty Castellanos scoring twice.

Nuno Espírito Santo remins keen on adding another striker to his ranks as the Hammers prepare for their league opener against Burnley this Sunday.

Concerns persist at the London stadium regarding attacking depth, with Pablo still waiting to score his first goal for the team following his £21m arrival from Gil Vicente in January.

Additionally, Niclas Fullkrug has returned from his loan spell with AC Milan but has been left without a squad number.

Their biggest coup is keeping hold of Jarrod Bowen - though talkSPORT understands he can leave next summer for £15m should they fail to get promoted.

Jamie Vardy to West Ham

As a result, West Ham are interested in Vardy, who is available on a free transfer after scoring seven Serie A goals for Cremonese.

talkSPORT understands Vardy is assessing all options with a number of clubs enquiring over his availability.

He was back training at League One Leicester, but there was never a possibility of a return to his former club.

Vardy had the option of an extra year in Italy, but it was subject to securing safety, and that never happened.

Those close to Vardy have said he has several options, including some from the MLS, and he is assessing his next steps.

Meanwhile, Manor Solomon is expected to complete his transfer to West Ham from Tottenham on Monday.

3 Solomon has been a key player for Tottenham during pre-season so far Credit: Getty

West Ham are closing in on a permanent signing for the winger in a move worth £5m up front.

During the transfer window, Nuno's side have already secured the signing of defender Joel Veltman, alongside Venezuelan winger Keiber Lamadrid on loan.

Additionally, the east London club have been pursuing AZ Alkmaar forward Troy Parrott; however, the Ireland international would require a substantial transfer fee.

Jamie Vardy's career

Signing Vardy would bring useful experience to the Championship, having earned promotion from the second tier twice during his decorated career.

3 Vardy will be forever known as a Leicester legend Credit: Getty

The 39-year-old built his reputation with Leicester City, leading the Foxes to their shock title win in 2016.

The veteran goalscorer scored 145 goals in 342 top flight appearances for them and also won the FA Cup.

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos snubs US to pursue $6bn ownership deal after shunning NFL and NBA franchises
Sports.content:
A minority stake which values Liverpool at around $6bn is expected to be sold to a consortium including Jeff Bezos.

Jeff Bezos snubs US to pursue $6bn ownership deal after shunning NFL and NBA franchises

Jeff Bezos is reportedly making his first foray into sports ownership with Liverpool.

The billionaire Amazon founder has been linked with numerous U.S. franchises, most recently the Seattle Seahawks.



4 Bezos would be the second-richest Premier League owner after Saudi-run Newcastle Credit: Getty

But he has decided to head for the Premier League instead.

talkSPORT understands Bezos forms part of a consortium set to buy around 30 percent of the Reds.

The Anfield club is owned by Fenway Sports Group (FSG) and an announcement is expected as soon as this week.

Bezos and Eduardo Saverin -- one of the co-founders of Facebook -- have been named as investors, along with Amit Bhatia, who is the son of steel mogul Lakshmi.



Between them, the trio bring a staggering fortune, with Bezos worth $280 billion and the others adding around $23 billion each.

The purchase reportedly values the Reds in the region of $6 billion.

Saverin was previously part of an unsuccessful bid to by Chelsea in 2022.



FSG purchased Liverpool in 2010 for just $404 million and have brought about a huge change in fortunes.

A spokesperson for FSG confirmed in July: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."



Dynasty Equity purchased a small stake in Liverpool in 2023, which valued the club at $4.5 billion.

4 The Amazon founder could look to take full control Credit: Getty

4 John Henry has enjoyed success with Liverpool Credit: Getty

Bezos' arrival could see his consortium try and take overall control down the road.



FSG also owns the Boston Red Sox, Pittsburgh Penguins, NASCAR's RFK Racing, and TGL's Boston Common Golf.

Liverpool transfer chief quits

Michael Edwards stepped down as Fenway Sports Group's CEO of football in July.

The transfer guru had been in the role since March 2024, having enjoyed a successful previous spell as sporting director between 2016 and 2022.

talkSPORT understands his decision to quit came as a result of FSG's failure to buy a second European club.



FSG president Mike Gordon took over operations with preparations for the new Premier League season already well underway.

4 Andoni Iraola took over from Arne Slot Credit: Getty

New manager Andoni Iraola had already added Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz to his squad before the exit.

Liverpool are also keen on Bradley Barcola, but face competition from Arsenal for the Paris Saint-Germain and France forward.



Ronald Araujo is also expected to sign after flying in for a medical.

Sports.title: West Ham interested in signing free agent Jamie Vardy as striker prepares to return to England - as Newcastle talks with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg hit stumbling block: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Hojbjerg talks hit stumbling block

Talks between Newcastle and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg have stalled. Daily Mail Sport understands there is a difference on personal terms.

The clubs were working toward agreement on a £12million deal for the midfielder.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on a Friday, talks had begun with the Denmark international to fill the void left by the departures of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

The 31-year-old is viewed as the experienced figure who can guide the new younger players Newcastle have added to their squad.

Khalaili has had his medical ahead of signing a five-year deal.

Brennan Johnson are Dwight McNeil look set to swap their Premier League teams

Everton's move for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston looks off as it stands.

West Ham are among a number of clubs to have approached free agent Jamie Vardy.

The Hammers see the former England man as an option if they fail to prise Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar.

Vardy, 39, is determined to take his time over his next move as there was a feeling he rushed a family decision to join Cremonese last year despite the value of the experience.

West Ham are one of several clubs monitoring Jamie Vardy

New Fox Franco

Leicester have signed goalkeeper Franco Ravizzoli on a free transfer from Blackpool.

The 27-year-old has signed a three-year contract at the King Power.

Blackpool are signing Middlesbrough defender Finley Munroe on loan.

City running rule over Rulli

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is undergoing a medical at Manchester City after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Araujo completes medical

Ronald Araujo has completed his Liverpool medical ahead of completing a loan move from Barcelona.

The 27-year-old's signing is expected to be announced this afternoon.

The Uruguay defender's loan also includes an option to buy for around £47.1m.

Villa keep tabs on Endrick

Aston Villa are among the growing list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid. The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024.

Read the full story here.

Masuaku closes on Turkey move

Sunderland defender Arthur Masuaku is finalising finalise his move to Konyaspor, in Turkey. A deal between the clubs was agreed over the weekend.

Masuaku joined Sunderland last summer and spent the second half of last season on loan at Lens.

Belgian club Mechelen have agreed a deal to sign Sunderland defender Leo Hjelde.

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

Sunderland are interested in signing Alex Palmer from Ipswich

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side with Anthony Patterson expected to undergo a medical at Wrexham after the clubs agreed a fee around £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Sunderland face Ipswich on the opening day of the season.

Ipswich are among the clubs interested in Newcastle's Nick Pope.

Villa on hunt for MacPhee replacement

Burnley set-piece coach Pal Fjelde is in talks to join Aston Villa.

Villa lost Austin MacPhee to Chelsea last month and 32-year-old Fjelde would be his replacement.

Fjelde joined Burnley last year and has also been his home country of Norway’s set piece coach since June 2022.

Austin MacPhee (right) left Villa to join Chelsea this summer

As a player he was a defender and midfielder and played for Norwegian clubs Viking and Bryne, before brief spells with Scottish Premiership side St Mirren and Faroe Islands Premier League side 07 Vestur.

Sports.title: Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'
Sports.content:
Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death at the age of just 45.

The Canadian, who was described as 'a respected golfer, devoted son, hilarious brother, and friend,' turned professional in 2003 after playing college golf at Oklahoma State and Georgia.

He later secured his place among golf's elite and went on to compete in 32 PGA Tour events, securing three top-10 finishes as a rookie.

But according to an obituary, he passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada. No cause of death was listed.

'Whether on the course or in everyday life, he had a remarkable ability to bring people together, offering encouragement, laughter, and genuine friendship to everyone he met,' it read, per the Kingston Whig-Standard.

'His welcoming personality and unwavering kindness made him a beloved figure within Kingston's golfing community and beyond.'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death

He passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada

McQuillan's father, Mark, began teaching him how to swing a club at the age of 10 before he went on to reach the Canadian Tour and then the PGA Tour.

'Matt developed lifelong friendships while mentoring anyone who loved the game of golf,' his obituary continued.

'He will be deeply missed by many and his spirit, love and compassion will be remembered every day. Rest easy, Matty. We love you.'

Golf Canada added in a tribute that it 'joins the Canadian golf community in mourning the passing of Matt McQuillan... one of Canada's most promising young golfers in the late 1990s.'

According to the PGA Tour, the 45-year-old returned to his hometown of Kingston, Ontario, to teach golf, 'helping introduce and develop the next generation of Canadian golfers.'

McQuillan's best PGA Tour result came at the 2011 John Deere Classic when he shot a final-round 64 to finish in a tie for third behind winner Steve Stricker.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Jose Mourinho has made a big mistake with tale that he rejected chance to replace Sir Alex Ferguson at Man United - this is what he accidentally revealed about himself
Sports.content:
OLIVER HOLT: Jose Mourinho has made a big mistake with tale that he rejected chance to replace Sir Alex Ferguson at Man United - this is what he accidentally revealed about himself

Read Oliver Holt's column every Monday with a DailyMail+ subscription - and unlock access to the best exclusives, interviews and analysis

Jose Mourinho is almost right when he says in a new documentary about his career that it hurts no one to reveal that he reneged on an agreement to join Manchester United in 2013 when he left Real Madrid and went back to Chelsea instead.

Mourinho likes to tell stories of self-aggrandisement that remind us that he was once, long ago, one of the great managers in the game, coveted by all. Back then, those who thought Cristiano Ronaldo was Lionel Messi’s equal also tended to think Mourinho was a match for Pep Guardiola.

Now that he is beginning a second stint in charge of Real Madrid, back in charge of A-list superstars like Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior, he may think it propitious to release details of the fact that he had been chosen to be Sir Alex Ferguson’s heir at Old Trafford.

The news reminds us he was a giant then, rather than the manager who has spent his most recent years as an also-ran at Spurs, Roma and Fenerbahce and was at Benfica last season, where he could only finish a distant third in the Portuguese league behind Porto and Sporting.

The main hope for Real Madrid is that Mourinho has been outmoded for so long that perhaps it is time for his negativity and his cynicism to come back into fashion, now that giants like Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp have left the club stage.

But even if we ignore the fact that Mourinho’s sudden fit of truth-telling casually lets everyone know that David Moyes was not the first choice to succeed Sir Alex at United, there is another person who does not quite escape clean from Mourinho’s revelations and that is him.

Jose Mourinho's revelation that he rejected the Man United job in 2013 reminds us of the man’s fickleness and how, sometimes, a job he takes can go wrong almost before it has started

It also reminds us that now he will have to convince Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Trent Alexander-Arnold and the rest at Madrid that he is not out of his time

Because it lets us know that Mourinho had an agreement to join one of the great clubs of the world and turned his back on it. Sure, it reminds us that he was once in demand but it also reminds us of the man’s fickleness and how, sometimes, a job he takes can go wrong almost before it has started.

It also reminds us that now that he, rather implausibly, has the reins at the Bernabeu, he will have to convince Bellingham, Mbappe, Vinicius, Trent Alexander-Arnold and the rest of the stellar cast at Madrid that he is not a man out of his time, a man who has been overtaken by football and who cannot keep up.

The new Mourinho documentary, which will air on Netflix this week, sheds new light on the conflicts that the manager endured with Ronaldo, Sergio Ramos and, particularly, Iker Casillas during his first spell in Madrid. Many believe those years at the Bernabeu curdled Mourinho’s attitude towards modern players.

It is already evident that he will have work to do to convince Vinicius to believe in him. The Brazilian forward has just signed a new six-year contract but it was only last season when, in the wake of allegations that Vinicius had been racially abused during a Champions League tie between Madrid and Mourinho’s Benfica, Mourinho accused Vinicius of inciting his players with his goal celebrations. Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was among those who criticised Mourinho’s stance.

If Mourinho retains any of the man-management smarts that were once such an integral part of his success, he will make it his mission to win over Bellingham and make the England midfielder his leader and his voice on the pitch.

Bellingham had an outstanding World Cup for England that went far beyond the tirelessness of his performances and his goal contributions. Bellingham already had little to prove to anybody but the tournament in North America was the time he answered every remaining question asked of him.

He proved, above all, that he was a leader, a player who can not only inspire by example but who can carry players with him. He proved that he is continuing to mature with frightening speed and that he is England’s captain in waiting.

Mourinho has made Federico Valverde his captain for the coming season and the Uruguay midfielder is a wonderful player who commands the respect of all. But Bellingham would have been an even better choice. He represents youth and promise and an insatiable hunger to succeed.

It is already evident that Mourinho will have work to do to convince Vinicius to believe in him

If Mourinho retains any of the man-management smarts that were once such an integral part of his success, he will make it his mission to make Bellingham his leader at Real

At a time when Madrid have lost the league twice in a row to Barcelona, Mourinho’s team is crying out for a fresh start. Bellingham symbolises everything they need to succeed and Mourinho’s relationship with him will be the key to whether Madrid can mount a successful challenge to dethrone their Catalan rivals.

If Mourinho retreats into suspicion and cynicism, then Madrid’s season will quickly become a familiar picture of the conflict and intrigue that have dogged so many of the manager’s club tenures. If he embraces the promise and the ambition and verve that Bellingham symbolises, then maybe there is a chance that even Mourinho can enjoy his very own Remontada in Madrid.

Tennis caught in a pickle

Back from nine weeks in the US, I have acquired a fondness for certain American pastimes. Chief among those is a new addiction to pickleball.

Our neighbours in New Hampshire traced out a pickleball court on their drive, bought a net from Walmart and we played every night after dinner. My son and I found a dedicated, thriving, two-storey pickleball club 20 miles away and spent a couple of evenings there, too.

My ambition for the next time I make it to the States is to play on the pickleball courts that spring up on the Wollman Ice Rink in Central Park, New York City in summer.

The surge of popularity of pickleball in the US is not dissimilar to the rise of padel in Europe. Both present a growing challenge to tennis at a time when the sport appears to be gravely lacking in leadership.

Enzo Maresca (right) will need to readjust his sights if he is to survive at Man City. There are a lot of tough jobs in English football but following Pep Guardiola (centre) is the toughest

Maresca's enormous shoes to fill

There is a man in charge at Manchester City now who helped throw more than £1billion against the wall at Chelsea and celebrated finishing fourth in the league by telling anyone who had doubted him to ‘F off’, as if what he had done was a great achievement.

Enzo Maresca will need to readjust his sights if he is to survive at the Etihad Stadium. There are a lot of tough jobs in the top flight of English football but following Pep Guardiola at City is the toughest of all of them.

Any attempt to celebrate finishing anywhere other than at the top of the table will not be viewed kindly by his new paymasters.

Sports.title: UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC presidents accuse Gianni Infantino of 'deception' in open letter demanding FIFA president is held accountable for failed plot to sell the World Cup
Sports.content:
UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC presidents accuse Gianni Infantino of 'deception' in open letter demanding FIFA president is held accountable for failed plot to sell the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA has accused under pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino of deception in a joint statement with the football federations of Asia and North and Central America.

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs football in the Caribbean, North and Central America, teamed up with UEFA on Monday to attack Infantino over his conduct during the proposed sale of stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup.

The statement said that Infantino had broken trust 'through deception' with the now abandoned proposal, had 'placed himself above the collective' and the three confederations called for a fully independent review of what had happened.

'Football's strength has always been its unity,' the statement concluded. 'We call for that unity to be honored now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.'

FIFA released a statement on Saturday criticising a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to 'undermine' both the organisation and Infantino.

UEFA announced on Thursday that they will continue to boycott FIFA competitions if Infantino remains at the top of world football after his scandalous plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes to private investors collapsed. Meanwhile, Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness called for him to resign on Friday.

UEFA (president Aleksander Ceferin, left) has accused under pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino (right) of deception in a joint statement with federations CONCACAF and AFC

Mexico's football federation broke ranks with CONCACAF to come out in support of Infantino, with Argentina, Qatar, Paraguay, Morocco and Egypt among those in favour of him remaining as FIFA president.

Infantino has also faced allegations this week that UEFA made a 'departure payment' to a female employee with whom he is alleged to have been in a relationship while general secretary of European football’s governing body.

UEFA have confirmed a payment was made, but FIFA labelled the allegation as ‘categorically untrue’.

The next FIFA presidential elections take place next March.

Sports.content:
Sunderland goalkeeper set to undergo Wrexham medical to boost promotion bid - as Hull look for cover after Jack Butland injury
