Sports.title: T10 proposal is a cry for help from counties who know they're heading for a 'cliff edge' - here's what it reveals about the future for the haves and have nots of the county game, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
T10 proposal is a cry for help from counties who know they're heading for a 'cliff edge' - here's what it reveals about the future for the haves and have nots of the county game, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

The suggestion by the new chairman of Sussex that a T10 competition may be one way of easing the financial concerns of the non-Hundred counties isn't just a sign of the times. It's a cry for help.

The ECB have insisted all along that the funds raised at last year's auction, when the Hundred was valued at £975million, would bankroll domestic red-ball cricket for a generation – an apparently powerful retort to the traditionalists who fear the tournament will devour England's 18-team domestic setup.

But the ECB's narrative does not tell the whole story. Far from it. In April, Daily Mail Sport revealed details of a secret meeting at Northamptonshire's Wantage Road involving nine of the 11 non-Hundred-hosting counties.

The mood was gloomy, with the clubs – almost all of them loss-making – worried about the growing divide between them and the seven host counties, a divide they worry will only grow once the Hundred's private investors demand a greater slice of a new TV deal for 2029, and the best players migrate inevitably to the richest clubs.

And while the non-host counties can in theory access around £25million each following the Hundred windfall, that money has to be spent on projects approved by the ECB, such as paying off structured debt or improving infrastructure.

One source who attended the meeting, held without the knowledge of the ECB, said: 'The feeling was that all the clubs are heading to a cliff edge at various speeds. They will all fall over one after the other if something is not addressed in the short term.'

Sussex are proposing a T10 competition to supposedly help non-Hundred hosting counties

And that is where Ed Warner, the new Sussex chair, comes in. Sussex were one of two non-host counties (along with Durham) to miss the secret meeting, and for good reason: they have spent much of the year trying to unravel the financial mess that led to them being placed in special measures, and docked points in all three county competitions.

After telling The Guardian that the Hundred had 'not rescued us in any way, shape or form', Warner captured the mood that day at Wantage Road by considering ways a non-host county might stage more cricket, and make more money, during the Hundred's nearly month-long duration – a period, at the height of summer and during the school holidays, when clubs are staging only four home Metro Bank 50-over matches.

Warner wondered: 'Why couldn't you have a T10 triangular competition with Kent and Essex, for example? Make it very kid-friendly, make it a day at the seaside, then go and play at Canterbury, then go and play in Chelmsford.'

His suggestion, though not itself discussed at the meeting, deserves full marks for lateral thinking. But it should concern cricket lovers on a few counts.

The first is that it would further complicate an already insane schedule, in which the response to the introduction of a fourth format – the Hundred – has been to stage it at the same time as the 50-over competition, diminishing a format in which England are now international also-rans. Our calendar is already full to bursting, without a fifth format trying to elbow its way in.

The second is that T10 feels like part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom. Yes, Abu Dhabi has been hosting its own T10 tournament since 2017, but it has made headlines mainly for reasons of corruption, both proven and alleged. If the Hundred feels like a hurry, T10 is a sprint. What next: F5, or the toss of a coin?

The third concern, and the most significant, is that Warner felt the need to air the suggestion in the first place.

Forget for a moment the financial incompetence at Hove that last week led business management consultancy firm Campbell Tickell to suggest an overhaul of the Sussex board 'as soon as is practically possible'.

The format would complicate an already insane schedule and be part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom

What matters is that the smaller counties are having to countenance alternative means of paying the bills at a time when the ECB tell us the game is richer than ever.

As one chief executive put it at the Northampton meeting, the promise of Hundred money has generated more uncertainty, not less, because of the unknown impact on the next broadcast rights deal.

The ECB will blanch at the idea of counties coming up with their own fifth-format schemes, since it would entail an admission of failure by the board. But Sussex's T10 musings are the symptom of a wider malaise – no matter the repeated insistence that the Hundred will save English cricket.

Unless the ECB get to grips with the smaller clubs' concerns, there will be more desperate ideas where that one came from.

Sports.title: Tracking private jets, Andrea Berta holding his nerve and a last-ditch plea from Matthias Jaissle: This is how Bruno Guimaraes became an Arsenal player - and why Mikel Arteta was so desperate to get him
Sports.content:
Tracking private jets, Andrea Berta holding his nerve and a last-ditch plea from Matthias Jaissle: This is how Bruno Guimaraes became an Arsenal player - and why Mikel Arteta was so desperate to get him

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The back-and-forth over whether Arsenal and Newcastle are actually in talks, the plane trackings and the staunch denials in the North East are finally at an end.

Bruno Guimaraes is an Arsenal player, theirs for £75million, and a transfer saga which has dragged on for weeks, much to the entertainment of rival fans, is over. Mikel Arteta has his man, a player he’s long admired and been desperate to sign.

This transfer has been an exhausting process, and far from straightforward. But Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has come out of it looking incredibly shrewd, having pulled off a relative ‘bargain’ in the current climate.

Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal started back in June. As Daily Mail Sport reported on June 24, the Brazilian had instructed agents to find him a new club and Newcastle were braced for an offer from the Gunners. Their interest had been registered.

Newcastle’s response was bullish. He wasn’t going anywhere, according to sources at the club. Given his status as captain and the player’s quality, Guimaraes’ value was enormous – particularly in light of the departures of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. They did not need to sell.

Money talks, however. Newcastle had briefed that they wanted closer to £100million, but internally there was acceptance that an offer of around £75million would see progress.

Bruno Guimaraes has joined Arsenal in a protracted £75million move from Newcastle

The transfer saga is finally over, with Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal starting back in June

A force of nature.



Guimaraes is a Gunner ✍️ pic.twitter.com/E7k4mIHICg — Arsenal (@Arsenal) August 8, 2026

At Arsenal, they were willing to dig their heels in over the price, in the knowledge that Guimaraes really wanted the move. He had agreed personal terms with the Gunners last month and informed Newcastle of his desire to leave if a suitable offer came in.

There were also optics at play. Newcastle didn’t want to be seen as letting their talisman and a fan favourite leave without putting up a fight. Their fans would rightly have felt aggrieved.

So the negotiations dragged on, largely involving agent Kia Joorabchian. Newcastle would claim there had been no formal contact from Arsenal and felt bewildered by the process, relayed in reports of no direct contact between the clubs.

This conflict in media coverage added to the increasing frenzy attached to a potential move.

Weeks went by, before a real acceleration came last week. As Daily Mail Sport reported on Friday, July 31, a deal had been agreed in principle with a date reserved for the medical. Though a few sticking points remained.

Newly-appointed Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle also decided he wanted a final chance to try to convince the Brazilian to stay put.

Guimaraes travelled to Newcastle’s La Manga training base in Spain on Monday, before waiting for permission to leave and have his medical at Arsenal after telling Jaissle of his desire to move.

The initial reports that he failed to arrive on Sunday resulted in social media sleuths tracking flights to see if Guimaraes was in the air. It had all got a bit mad.

Even the Arsenal players were braced for the move. When Riccardo Calafiori was asked about Guimaraes’ impending transfer on Wednesday night after Arsenal’s 3-1 defeat by Real Betis in Dublin, he turned to the press officer and asked: ‘Is it official yet, no?’

Berta is a tough negotiator. He loathes to overpay, which in this market is extremely hard not to do.

Arsenal had wanted to pay a smaller fee for the Brazil midfielder, who turns 29 in November, while Newcastle demanded a minimum of £80million.

That Arsenal decided to play the long game and stick to their guns frustrated some of their supporters. But the club were never in doubt of the end result.

Newly-appointed manager Matthias Jaissle made a last ditch plea to persuade him to stay

Arsenal chief Andrea Berta held his nerve on the transfer fee throughout negotiations

It’s a smart deal in a market which has, as one agent claimed, ‘gone out of control’. As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, even kids as young as 16 are being paid £20,000 a week, as in the case of Man City’s Mishel Nduka.

In the senior ranks, Chelsea bought Morgan Rogers for £117million, while Spurs splashed out £100million on Tonali.

The strategy of Arsenal and Berta has paid off - after they walked away from Rogers because their valuation of the player had been far exceeded.

The deal for Guimaraes represents value for money - and it is one Berta deserves credit for.

An Arsenal midfield, which was already dominant, now looks even more menacing. Alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, Guimaraes completes a formidable trio.

Rice provides the ability to cover acres of space, while also being a threat going forward and strong defensively. Odegaard is in charge of creating chances in the final third.

Guimaraes, meanwhile, is an all-round No 8 who can affect games at both ends of the pitch, and brings an aggressive edge. His attempts at more ambitious passes will add some unpredictability the Gunners lack at times.

And so, after weeks of twists, denials and negotiations behind the scenes, the saga is finally over. Guimaraes is an Arsenal player – and Newcastle’s fight to keep their captain has achieved nothing more than a sizeable cheque.

Sports.title: Former Premier League bad boy Nile Ranger claims he got into a fight with Andros Townsend on England duty after the ex-Crystal Palace star 'spat in his pasta'
Sports.content:
Nile Ranger has claimed he and Andros Townsend were involved in a heated altercation while representing England as youngsters on international duty.

Despite never representing the Three Lions at senior level, Ranger scored six goals in 11 appearances for England's U19s after bursting on to the scene as a teenager.

The former Newcastle prodigy, 35, revealed on a podcast this week that he once clashed with fellow ex-England youth star Townsend while the pair were sharing a room in Ukraine on international duty.

'He wasn't playing and getting in the team at the time, but he's a man where he's stretching at night time and keeping himself ready,' Ranger told Undr the Cosh.

'I've played but I didn't play the best. And I'm like to Andros, "Look, just go to sleep man, just relax. You're stretching and doing all of this but your chance will come". I'm actually genuinely telling him that, I'm being real.

'He's like, "You what? Did you see how you played today? You had a stinker, I don't want to play like that. I've got to make sure I'm stretched out and ready".

Ex-Newcastle star Nile Ranger (left) has claimed he and Andros Townsend (right) were involved in a heated altercation while representing England as youngsters on international duty

The forward was once regarded as one of Newcastle's brightest prospects as a teenager

'I don't know why he was coming at me. Take your anger out on someone else bro because I'm not the one. I'll just knock you out and then it's just long (not worth it).

'Anyway, we go down for food the next day and, you remember those old-school blue Lucozade bottles with the yellow top, he's drinking from it and he's spitting in my pasta. I'm looking around at players and being like - are you witnessing this as well? This is crazy antics right now.'

Continuing the anecdote, Ranger claims he and Townsend went upstairs and started brawling, surrounded by team-mates including former England international Kyle Walker.

'I can see Andros there, I'm on to Andros, and I've just crashed him,' Ranger added, making a punching gesture. 'His head hits the bin and man are trying to stop me, Kyle Walker trying to stop me, but the rage inside is just going mad, going berserk.

'We got split up, he's gone to his room. I don't know if the coaches found out about it but I've gone back later and he's like, "Look, let me stop you, I'm sorry. I think just being out here is getting to me and what not".

'I know how it feels. It's like when you get an injury or something and you're not playing. Or you feel like you can play and aren't getting the chance. It was just anger built up, that sort of thing.'

After off-field issues derailed his career, he ended up playing for a string of non league clubs

🚨 NEW SERIES OUT TOMORROW 🚨



Nile Ranger looks back on clashing with Andros Townsend while on England U19s duty 🥊 pic.twitter.com/LcqRCA5Q2n — UndrTheCosh (@UndrTheCosh) August 9, 2026

Once regarded as one of Newcastle's brightest young prospects, Ranger's off-field behaviour repeatedly overshadowed and ultimately derailed his career.

As a teenager, he spent time in a young offenders’ institution following an armed robbery, and his early professional years were subsequently punctuated by disciplinary problems and run-ins with the law.

After Newcastle opted not to renew his contract in 2013 after a string of off-pitch controversies, Ranger moved to Swindon Town before spells at Blackpool and Southend United.

He took a two-year break from football in 2018 following further run-ins with the law. Since returning in 2020, he has bounced between several non-league clubs, starting with Spalding United before brief spells at Southend, Boreham Wood, Kettering Town, Wellingborough Town and Chatham Town.

Once again a free agent this summer, the striker left Chatham Town at the end of last season after scoring six goals in 14 appearances for the club.

Ranger has also spoken openly in the past about his struggles with gambling addiction. In a 2023 interview, he claimed that, had he behaved better off the pitch and maintained a healthier lifestyle, he could have been as prolific as Manchester City's goal machine Erling Haaland.

Sports.title: Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting
Sports.content:
Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting

Arsenal are firm admirers of Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, and they are looking at potentially signing the ex-Manchester City star after missing out on Vinicius Junior

View Image Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez will reportedly push to leave Atletico Madrid this summer, with Arsenal keen on landing the Argentinian. It's claimed, though, the 26-year-old will reiterate his desire to join Barcelona, having previously said it would be his dream to move to the Nou Camp.

‌



Alvarez is due to return for pre-season training this week, with Arsenal keeping a close eye on developments. Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has been a long-term admirer of the former Manchester City forward, who has racked up 49 goals and 17 assists in 106 appearances for Atletico.

‌



However, the La Liga giants club have stood firm with their stance that Alvarez is not for sale, even after his controversial comments during the World Cup.

‌



Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I spoke with people at the club, with those I had to speak with and the best thing for everyone is ‌a transfer and I want to fulfil my dream," he said.

"It's not the time to talk about this, but I also can't hide ⁠it. I try to ⁠be an honest person."

‌



Alvarez has been the subject of bids from both Barcelona and Real Madrid, yet his manager Diego Simeone maintains that nothing has shifted and that Atletico have no plans to sanction his exit.

"The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel Gil Marin [Atletico's CEO] explained very well," Simeone said. "We are very happy with Julian, from a sporting perspective, we're very happy to have a player like Julian, and we'll help him continue to grow and improve."

Ahead of his return to Atleti, Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Alvarez will once again make his desire to join Barcelona abundantly clear, despite having already expressed this both privately and publicly, as the saga enters its 'decisive phase'.

‌



This would strongly suggest that Arsenal would be out of the running for his signature should the Spanish giants alter their position.

Atleti have remained resolute thus far, though the Argentine continues to harbour hopes that the club might eventually have a change of heart. The publication warns that 'a major crisis could erupt' between Atleti and the Argentine.

‌



It is further reported that should Atletico ease their stance and agree to open talks, Barcelona 'will submit a new offer'.

Nevertheless, Gil Marin has left no doubt that the club will not be entertaining any offers for their prized asset this summer.

"It wasn't the right day to make such statements; it was a day for [Lionel] Messi and the Argentine national team, not Julian," he previously told EFE about Alvarez's comments regarding his desire to leave.

Article continues below

"Julian has a dream [to sign elsewhere], but we Atletico fans have dreams, too. It is true that he has spoken to us, but it is also true that he is fully aware of our position because we have been very clear. Atleti do not want to transfer him. He is a great player and we are very proud that he plays for us."

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star claims he's been told Bradley Barcola 'wants to live in London'
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star claims he's been told Bradley Barcola 'wants to live in London'

Bradley Barcola is a target for both Liverpool and Arsenal amid his uncertain future at Paris Saint-Germain, and the Gunners are said to have the upper hand on their Premier League rivals

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is a wanted man (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Ex-Arsenal forward Perry Groves says he's been told that Gunners target Bradley Barcola 'wants to live in London'. Barcola, 23, is hot property this summer, with Liverpool already in talks with Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



PSG's lofty demand of £145million has put the breaks on a move, leaving his future uncertain with three weeks to go until transfer deadline day. The Frenchman returned to training with Luis Enrique's side on Monday but is open to a move.

‌



Arsenal have already missed out on two wingers this summer, Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers, and have been tipped to go for Barcola as an alternative. And Groves' claim suggests that his old club boast an advantage over Liverpool.

‌



The former Gunners man, who played for the club between 1986 and 1992, told talkSPORT: "I've got a source that says he wants to live in London. I can't tell you [who], I can't divulge my sources. I've got a source. I've got a mole. Barcola wants to live in London."

Sports.title: Golf star punished after fish eats his ball during round leaving pundits gobsmacked
Sports.content:
Golf star punished after fish eats his ball during round leaving pundits gobsmacked

The South African was given a one-shot penalty after his ball was stolen in the water.

View Image Charl Schwartzel was in the unusual situation of having his golf ball eaten by a fish during a LIV Golf tournament. (Image: Hector Vivas/Getty Images)

A LIV Golfer had to take a one-shot penalty after a fish ate his ball during a round. The incident left those watching almost speechless. South African Charl Schwartzel was taking part in the LIV Golf Bedminster tournament at the Trump National Golf Club.

‌



On the seventh hole, he hit a drive towards the tee. After hitting the green, the ball rolled towards the water. As soon as it entered, a fish jumped up and claimed it as his own, leaving Schwartzel without a ball.

‌



One commentator providing coverage of the action said: “I have never seen that.” Fans were also quick to take to social media to respond to the unusual situation.

‌



Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

“Fish swallowing a golf ball is a new one.. liv golf is taking us places we've never been before,” one said. “What’s the rule on this one?” A second asked.

“A fish steals a golf ball! Seriously this has to be a first.

‌



“It’s in a hazard, but also may have been playable. Can he replace it in the hazard since it is animal interference? Or since it’s a hazard, too bad?”

While there were questions over the next step, in the end Schwartzel was handed a one-shot penalty. The punishment means that he recorded a bogey for the par three hole, and ended the tournament two over par.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Speaking before the tournament, Schwartzel spoke about the challenges that the course presented, although he may not have envisioned fish being part of that.

“It’s a great golf course,” he told SABC Sport .

"It’s a golf course that will also suit Martin (Vosrster, his teammate), as he is a long hitter. It’s a very long golf course and it can be windy, as it’s quite exposed.

“What we’ve found in the past is it seems to suit the long hitters quite well, so you need to take advantage of the par-fives here, otherwise, you can struggle.”

Sports.title: Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move
Sports.content:
Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move

Arsenal are in talks with Galatasaray over a potential deal for Gabriel Martinelli, who is into the final 12 months of his contract at the Emirates Stadium

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal in the summer transfer window (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal and Galatasaray are in talks over a possible move for Gabriel Martinelli.

‌



Martinelli, 25, has entered the final 12 months of his contract at the Emirates Stadium and lost his spot in the starting XI to Leandro Trossard last season. While Trossard has since departed to join Besiktas, Christos Tzolis has arrived in a £34million deal from Club Brugge and the Gunners remain in the market for a new left winger.

‌



This has left Martinelli's future hanging in the balance, with speculation suggesting he could leave before the transfer window closes. Now, according to football.london, Arsenal are in negotiations with Galatasaray over a fee for the Brazilian, following an enquiry from the Turkish Super Lig side on the weekend.

‌



Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss READ MORE :

OPINION Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat by Ryan Taylor

However, no deal will be approved until there is progress in the opposite direction and Arsenal secure a left wing signing themselves, having missed out on Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior.

Tzolis has been Arsenal's first-choice on the left flank during pre-season, finding the net against Girona on his debut before providing an assist from a corner against Real Betis. He subsequently set up the Gunners' second goal in their 3-2 loss to Borussia Dortmund on Sunday and is proving to be a genuine threat down that side.

‌



Martinelli, meanwhile, was absent from Arsenal's opening pre-season fixture at Girona but has since come off the bench as a second-half substitute against Betis and Dortmund. He appeared for the final 12 minutes in the defeat to the German side and netted in the subsequent Emirates Cup penalty shootout.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli could be sold by Arsenal before the end of the summer window (Image: PA)

Speaking after the Dortmund match, Arteta confirmed the Gunners remain busy in the transfer market as they look to bolster their ranks. "Well, that's what we're trying to do (sign more players)," the Spaniard said. "It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very much looking forward to that."

‌



Arsenal snapped up Martinelli for just £6m back in 2019 and he has since gone on to make 278 appearances for the Gunners, netting 62 goals. However, he struggled to make any real impression last season, losing his regular starting berth to Trossard.

Belgian international Trossard delivered several standout moments for Mikel Arteta's side on the road to the Premier League title, before being offloaded for £15.3m to Besiktas. Martinelli could follow his team-mate with a switch to Turkish top-flight rivals Galatasaray, albeit for a considerably larger transfer fee.

While no precise transfer figure has been suggested for Martinelli, his age and profile would undoubtedly command a higher price than what Besiktas forked out for Trossard. Galatasaray are also said to be in discussions with AC Milan regarding a transfer for winger Rafael Leao, with a £43m price tag under consideration.

Article continues below

Should Arsenal secure a comparable sum for Martinelli, it would surpass the club's existing record sale, which saw Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain join Liverpool for £35m back in 2019.

Sports.title: 4 players Arsenal could sign this week as Mikel Arteta promises new arrivals
Sports.content:
Three down, three weeks to go. That's the story of Arsenal's summer transfer window after welcoming their third new signing in the form of Bruno Guimaraes over the weekend.

The Gunners' newest recruit, taking their summer spending to a cool £109million, was unveiled at the Emirates on Saturday before Mikel Arteta watched his side succumb to a second successive defeat in pre-season. Arsenal were beaten 3-2 by Borussia Dortmund, who exploited the home side's rustiness and exposed their weaknesses.

Without their spine of David Raya, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes and Declan Rice, Arsenal have looked vulnerable. Post-match, Arteta confirmed that the club are actively working on new signings.

But who could they be? And in what areas does Arteta need to prioritise?

‌



Mirror Football looks at four deals Arsenal could do ahead of their season opener against Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

Arsenal star Viktor Gyokeres stopped in his tracks and bats away Man City question READ MORE :

OPINION Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat by Ryan Taylor

Ezri Konsa

It wouldn't be a transfer window without Arsenal signing a defender who can play at centre-back and full-back. And there aren't many better when it comes to that profile than Ezri Konsa.

‌



The England international has already been the subject of a bid from Arsenal, who reportedly offered just over half of his £60m valuation. Aston Villa rejected it but it's been claimed that their dressing room are 'resigned' to Konsa leaving.

Arteta was asked directly if Arsenal wanted to sign a defender after Saliba broke down with a back injury during the World Cup. "We conceded some poor goals today in the way we competed, especially," the Gunners boss replied.

Who should Arsenal sign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images Ezri Konsa could join his England team-mates at Arsenal (Image: Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

‌



"But that's a very collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve, for sure, we want that."

Bradley Barcola

After missing out on Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers, could be third time lucky for Arsenal in their search for a big-money wide forward? Paris Saint-Germain winger Barcola fits the bill and is a top target for Liverpool.

Arsenal, however, are said to be considering a move themselves. PSG value the 23-year-old at an eye-watering £145m, although the impending arrival of Ferran Torres from Barcelona could pressure them into a sale at a lower price.

View 5 Images Paris Saint-Germain are demanding £145million for Bradley Barcola (Image: Xavier Laine/Getty Images)

‌



Kenan Yildiz

Sticking in the wide forward areas, Kenan Yildiz's name continues to be linked with Arsenal. The Juventus forward is versatile, a trait which Arteta loves, and is rumoured to be his dream target.

Yildiz, 21, is said to be valued at a cool €100m (£85m) making him a cheaper alternative to Barcola. The German-born Turkey international enjoyed his most productive season to date last term, scoring 14 goals and providing 10 assists, and is the kind of player than can give Arsenal the dynamism fans have craved in attack.

View 5 Images Kenan Yildiz is reportedly Mikel Arteta's dream target (Image: Janelle St Pierre/Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez

It's been nearly two months since Julian Alvarez revealed that he wanted to leave Atletico Madrid this summer, but he remains at the Wanda Metropolitano. Arsenal have a long-standing interest in the former Man City striker, who Atletico have already rejected bids for this summer.

‌



Barcelona and Real Madrid both tried their luck earlier this summer, but his employers insist that the only way Alvarez can be sold is if a club pays his €500m (£428m) release clause. However, if Atletico were to sell, they'd prefer to offload him abroad.

View 5 Images Arsenal would need to pay top dollar for Julian Alvarez (Image: LOF/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

That gives Arsenal an advantage and although this remains a long shot, the Gunners could try their luck. A swap deal involving Viktor Gyokeres has even been mooted.

Sports.content:

Liverpool could step up their transfer activity this week

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola is eyeing a major transfer raid (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

The clock is ticking at Anfield, with the Premier League season opener now less than a fortnight away. The urgency to get transfer business over the line is intensifying as Andoni Iraola prepares for his competitive debut at the helm against Newcastle United on August 23.

‌



A significant summer shake-up has already begun to take shape on Merseyside. The high-profile exit of Mohamed Salah to Turkish side Trabzonspor has headlined the outgoings, while the incoming recruitment drive has seen Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet put pen to paper, alongside the acquisition of promising young centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

‌



Pre-season preparations are in full swing, though Iraola's Anfield bow ended in a 3-2 defeat to Monaco on Sunday. With a pair of friendly games against Como looming next weekend, the new manager has had ample opportunity to assess his squad's deficiencies and has publicly hinted that reinforcements are needed.

‌



As the countdown to the opening day accelerates, the revolving door at the club is expected to see further traffic moving in both directions. With that in mind, here is a look at five potential deals that could be finalised in the coming days.

Ronald Araujo

One transfer which appears to be a question of when rather than if is Ronald Araujo's arrival from Barcelona. The Uruguayan will join on an initial loan deal, with Barca manager Hansi Flick already confirming the switch.

‌

"We couldn't include him like I wanted and also I think he wants to make something new," Flick said. "You know it more than me because in the past, something has happened, so this affected him.

"I saw him this morning and I said goodbye and I think he was very happy and Liverpool is also a fantastic club. I wish him all the best because he deserves it. He's a fantastic guy and fantastic player and was a great captain."

Curtis Jones

Plenty of Liverpool supporters remain hopeful Jones will stay put. Yet, he could still depart should Inter Milan match the Reds' valuation.

‌



Jones has entered the final 12 months of his deal and this may explain why the Italian outfit have been hesitant to commit substantial funds. A fee of £35m might well prove sufficient, though.

View 5 Images Inter Milan are interested in signing Curtis Jones (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Whether that represents the correct decision is an entirely different question. The England international is a homegrown product who has delivered during crucial moments, but his departure could generate resources for recruitment elsewhere.

‌



Bradley Barcola

Among the high-value targets continuing to be associated with an Anfield switch is France international Barcola. The winger has become the primary wide option, following earlier target Yan Diomande's transfer to Real Madrid.

View 5 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top transfer target (Image: Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain's pursuit of Ferran Torres might ease the disappointment of parting with Barcola. As might a price tag of approximately £110m, which appears to be what the French giants would accept.

‌



Arsenal also remain connected with the former Lyon star. Barcola, who reaches 24 in September, netted 11 league goals for PSG last term and shone during France's journey to the World Cup semi-finals.

Ibrahim Mbaye

Barcola may not be the sole player to swap PSG for Liverpool. Ibrahim Mbaye is prepared to depart the Ligue 1 club and the Reds are amongst prospective destinations.

‌



Senegal star Mbaye has found his route to regular action in Paris obstructed. Several Premier League clubs have been mentioned, with Liverpool far from the only possible landing spot.

View 5 Images Ibrahim Mbaye played for Senegal at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The 18-year-old featured 30 times for PSG last term, although numerous outings came from the bench. His youth means he would represent both an immediate and long-term addition, while a potential price tag exceeding £40m reflects his considerable promise.

‌



Cody Gakpo

Should Liverpool manage to complete that £150m double-signing from PSG, it might enable them to part with Gakpo. Tottenham hold interest in the Dutch attacker but the Reds are understood to desire two fresh forwards before considering a departure.

View 5 Images Tottenham are interested in Cody Gakpo (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Gakpo has found the net 50 times in 180 matches across all competitions since arriving from PSV Eindhoven. Yet, there are no signs of Iraola being keen to sanction a sale.

A substantial offer might alter that, however. Figures around £70m have surfaced in certain quarters online and that type of return could prove welcome to balance a major Barcola investment.

Sports.title: Harry Kane to respond to Barcelona transfer interest with new bumper contract
Sports.content:
Harry Kane to respond to Barcelona transfer interest with new bumper contract

The England captain has entered the final year of his contract with Bayern Munich.

View 2 Images Harry Kane looks set to extend his stay at Bayern Munich. (Image: Adam Pretty/Getty Images)

England captain Harry Kane will reportedly extend his Bayern Munich contract by a further two years, as the German side ward off interest from Barcelona. The striker has entered the final year of his current deal at the Allianz Arena.

‌



Reports suggested that Barcelona were interested in signing Kane this summer as the search for a replacement for Robert Lewandowski. However, it seems that a stay in Germany is on the cards.

‌



The Times reports that the 33-year-old is set to extend his contract until 2029, with no significant change to his current salary. Kane is one of the top earners at Bayern Munich, with a yearly wage of around £21.5million per year.

‌



Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers READ MORE :

Everton and Crystal Palace agree stunning swap deal as Lamine Camara bid rejected READ MORE :

The striker is yet to return to pre-season, having had an extended break following this summer’s World Cup with England. He captained the Three Lions to a third-place finish in the tournament.

He is expected to meet up with his teammates later this week as the club prepares for their Bundesliga opener against Stuttgart on Friday, 28 August (7.30pm BST).

‌



Before that, they play Borussia Dortmund in the German Super Cup final on Saturday, 22 August (7.30pm BST).

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 games in all competitions for Bayern last season, helping them to lift the Bundesliga crown for the second season in a row. He will look to continue that impressive goalscoring record in the new campaign.

View 2 Images Harry Kane captained England in this summer's World Cup. (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



The report adds that there is an 'expectation' that Kane will eventually return to the Premier League as he bids to break Alan Shearer’s long-standing goalscoring record. He currently has 213 goals in the league, 47 away from Shearer’s record of 260.

There has been consistent talk of a possible return to Tottenham Hotspur, where he scored all of his Premier League goals after coming through the academy, but it seems that Spurs will have to wait a bit longer for a possible reunion.

Kane left the club in 2023, with Spurs receiving a fee of around £86million from Bayern Munich.

In his time in Germany so far, he has scored 146 goals in 147 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
