Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Which of Antonelli’s rivals is his biggest threat for the championship this year? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s strong position in the lead of the championship standings at the summer break is remarkable enough already for a driver in his second season in Formula 1.

But what makes his position all the more impressive is that, arguably, no single driver has yet emerged as his clear rival. Antonelli has won six of the 11 rounds so far, more than the rest put together, and only his team mate George Russell has taken multiple wins.

Despite that, Russell is not Antonelli’s closest rival in the standings: Lewis Hamilton is leading a resurgent Ferrari. Plus, the final round before the summer break saw McLaren claim their first victory of the season. Three of the last five grands prix were won by teams other than Mercedes – could Antonelli biggest threat come from one of them?

Lewis Hamilton

50 points behind

The possibility of Hamilton fighting for the championship against the driver who took the Mercedes seat he vacated last year is a compelling narrative. But is it a likely outcome? Hamilton is Antonelli’s closest rival in the points but has missed opportunities due to penalties in recent races.

George Russell

59 points behind

Russell should be Antonelli’s closest rival for the championship but various factors have left him well behind including unreliability (not that Antonelli has been immune), some misfortune and his risky first-lap lunge at Spa. He’s also on course to incur a power unit change penalty before his team mate. Still, Russell should have the equipment and the experience to put Antonelli under pressure.

Charles Leclerc

81 points behind

Hamilton may be closer to Antonelli in the standings but Charles Leclerc has arguably looked more competitive. Providing he avoids a repeat of the dip he fell into around Spain and Monaco, he could emerge as Antonelli’s biggest threat.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Lando Norris

91 points behind

Like Mercedes, unreliability has dogged McLaren this year. They often haven’t been quick enough either, though Norris has now won both a grand prix and a sprint race. The MCL40’s Hungaroring upgrade clearly paid off, and may prove enough to bring the McLarens into regular contention. The reigning world champion is a long way behind, though.

Max Verstappen

110 points behind

If last year demonstrated anything, it is unwise to write off Max Verstappen if he is not mathematically out of contention. Having been 104 points off the lead with 249 remaining, he eventually lost by the narrowest margin in F1 history (relatively). But lying 110 points behind in a car which hasn’t won a grand prix yet may be too much even for him.

Oscar Piastri

127 points behind

Oscar Piastri has proved a close match on pace for his team mate as usual but he’s even further behind in the standings. He went into the final round of last season with a shot at the championship but that doesn’t look likely to happen this year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Isack Hadjar

151 points behind

Isack Hadjar has impressed with the quality of his performances alongside Verstappen and may yet recover the points he dropped after losing his podium finish in Monaco. But his points deficit to Antonelli is surely too large and the Red Bull not competitive enough yet for him to be a realistic title contender.

I say

Hamilton may be closest in the points but Russell surely has the better combination of opportunity and equipment at the moment. If he can stop the rot in the second half of the season I would back him to put Antonelli under pressure for the title.

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Errol Spence’s Decline Started Years Before Crawford
Sports.content:
“It was quite sad watching Errol Spence in that fight, to be honest with you,” Hearn said to Jai McAllister Boxing. “Having promoted him in his prime in the Kell Brook fight, like how good he was. He was a shell of himself, and I think he has been for years.”

Spence had been putting considerable strain on his body well before his October 2019 car crash. He allowed his weight to climb substantially between fights and acknowledged having to spend portions of training camp taking it back off. After his grueling win over Shawn Porter in September 2019, Spence admitted there was nothing good about gaining more than 25 pounds and then using camp to lose it. The crash came less than two weeks later and kept him out of the ring for more than a year.

Spence returned against Danny Garcia in December 2020 and won comfortably, but the destructive version that finished Brook wasn’t there. Garcia was 32 and already had losses to Porter and Keith Thurman.

The difficulties continued against Yordenis Ugas in 2022. Ugas badly hurt Spence in the sixth round before Spence recovered, took control, and ended the fight in the tenth.

Crawford then produced the most one-sided defeat of Spence’s career in July 2023, dropping him three times before the ninth-round stoppage.

The performance deserves full credit. But it also created the impression that Crawford alone was responsible for making Spence look so ordinary.

Years of difficult weight management, punishing fights, inactivity, and the physical consequences of the car crash had already taken something from Spence before Crawford got him.

Hearn saw Spence near his best against Brook. His belief that Spence had been a shell for years supports what the previous fights were already showing: Crawford didn’t destroy the prime version of Errol Spence.

Sports.title: Car Salesman Hearn Over-Sells Teremoana’s Heavyweight Future
Sports.content:
“I don’t think you guys have seen anything like this before in Australia,” Hearn said. “I think legitimately a chance for you to have a long-reigning heavyweight world champion. Got the size, got the power, got the personality.”

The physical tools are obvious. Teremoana is 11-0 with 11 knockouts, has enormous size and power, and reached the quarterfinals at the 2024 Olympics. What he doesn’t have is a professional win that supports Hearn’s enormous expectations.

Calling DeAndre Savage a “big step up” only inflates Wednesday’s fight. Savage is 35 with a 10-1 record, and Brandon Moore beat him over 10 rounds last year. He’s a reasonable opponent, but beating him tells us little about Teremoana’s ability to compete with the best heavyweights.

Hearn went further, saying he sees “something different” in Teremoana and believes he can bring heavyweight world titles to Australia.

Harrison couldn’t resist.

“You made Teremoana sound like he’s fighting Hercules,” Harrison told Hearn during an exchange in which he joked about the promoter’s ability to sell fighters.

That’s the issue. Teremoana may eventually justify Hearn’s praise, but blasting through lower-level heavyweights doesn’t establish that he’s destined for a long championship reign.

We still need to see him fight beyond the early rounds, deal with a skilled heavyweight who can neutralize his pressure and make adjustments when raw power doesn’t immediately solve the problem.

If Hearn really has Australia’s next elite heavyweight champion, give Teremoana opposition that lets him prove it.

Sports.title: How Wealth and Fame Changed Jack Dempsey
Sports.content:
Everything changed after Dempsey destroyed Jess Willard on July 4, 1919. The heavyweight championship turned Dempsey into one of America’s biggest sports celebrities. His fights generated enormous gates. Movies and endorsements brought him even more money. He also became part of Hollywood’s social world.

The fighter who once struggled financially could now afford mansions and a lifestyle that would have been unimaginable during his early years. Boxing gradually occupied less of his time.

After defeating Georges Carpentier in July 1921, Dempsey went nearly two years without defending his championship. He returned to beat Tommy Gibbons in July 1923 before surviving a wild fight with Luis Ángel Firpo two months later.

Dempsey was only 28 after stopping Firpo, an age when a heavyweight champion might normally be approaching his best years. Instead, he didn’t have another official fight for nearly three years.

During that period, Dempsey’s celebrity continued growing. Hollywood remained part of his life; he participated in exhibitions, and in 1925 he married actress Estelle Taylor. His relationship with longtime manager Jack “Doc” Kearns also ended bitterly.

The contrast with the hungry fighter who had pursued Willard was striking. Dempsey no longer needed to fight regularly to make money or establish his name. Boxing had already given him financial security and national fame.

When Dempsey finally returned to defend against Gene Tunney on September 23, 1926, he was 31 and hadn’t competed in an official bout since Firpo.

Tunney took advantage, outboxing Dempsey over 10 rounds to win a unanimous decision and the heavyweight championship. The inactivity shouldn’t be used to diminish Tunney’s accomplishment. Tunney was an exceptional fighter who defeated Dempsey again in their famous 1927 “Long Count” rematch.

But the larger question remains: what might Dempsey’s career have looked like if wealth and celebrity hadn’t pulled him so far from regular competition? Dempsey became champion at 24. By his late twenties, he had money, mansions, movie work, and access to a world far removed from the one that created the Manassa Mauler.

Success didn’t destroy Jack Dempsey. It gave him the life he had fought to obtain. The price was that boxing no longer demanded everything from him.

Sports.title: Tamm Thibeault Can’t Afford To Wait For Claressa Shields
Sports.content:
She captured the IBF and WBO middleweight titles Saturday night with a 10-round shutout of Desley Robinson, winning 100-90 on all three scorecards. It was her first time going 10 rounds, and she had to deal with a cut caused by an accidental head clash.

Gaining extra ring time would help, but there comes a point where waiting becomes counterproductive. If Thibeault spends another two or three years building her record against lower-tier middleweights, she will be 31 or 32 before getting Shields.

Who is she supposed to fight in that period that prepares her for Claressa?

There isn’t another Shields available at middleweight. Thibeault can collect defenses and complete rounds, but opponents at levels below Shields aren’t going to duplicate her hand speed, reflexes, or ability to make adjustments.

Shields hasn’t exactly been sharpening herself against elite opposition, either. Savannah Marshall in 2022 was the last opponent who presented her with the kind of threat Thibeault potentially brings. Shields has continued collecting titles since then without facing someone capable of seriously testing her.

That doesn’t make Thibeault the favorite. Shields remains the more accomplished professional and has dominated everyone put in front of her.

Thibeault’s best opportunity may come sooner rather than later. She possesses the amateur schooling, size, southpaw stance, and physical strength to make the fight interesting.

Waiting years for preparation that lesser opposition cannot provide may leave Thibeault older without making her any more ready for Shields.

Sports.title: Stopping Hrgovic Would Top Joshua’s Charles Martin Blitz
Sports.content:
He had won the vacant belt less than three months earlier when Vyacheslav Glazkov suffered a knee injury and was unable to continue in the third round. Martin never had to beat a reigning champion to get the belt, then surrendered it in his first defense against Joshua.

Hrgovic is a much tougher proposition. Gareth A. Davies believes a stoppage win would make Itauma’s first title victory more impressive than Joshua’s demolition of Martin.

“I’d like to see a stoppage of Filip Hrgovic, but if you want the major statement, that’s it. And he’s a world champion, and he’s got a stoppage. And if you compare it to Anthony Joshua winning against Charles Martin, winning the IBF title against Charles Martin, then, you know, it does have comparative values, and it’s probably a bigger performance, and it’s probably a bigger statement than that could ever have been,” said Gareth to talkSPORT Boxing.

Hrgovic has already shared the ring with Daniel Dubois, Zhilei Zhang and Joe Joyce. He is durable, physically strong and willing to trade when opponents come after him.

Itauma hasn’t faced anyone close to that level yet. Jermaine Franklin, Dillian Whyte and the other heavyweights on his record haven’t forced him through the kind of fight Hrgovic can potentially provide.

If Itauma runs through Hrgovic anyway, the belt will only tell part of the story. Joshua flattened Martin, but Itauma would have stopped the better heavyweight.

Sports.title: Catterall Could Jeopardize Haney’s Ryan Garcia Payday
Sports.content:
That could take away one of Devin’s useful tactics.

Haney repeatedly clinched Brian Norman Jr. to shut down his offense during their bout. Catterall isn’t a fighter who can necessarily be controlled that way. He uses plenty of holding himself and has the strength to handle Devin in those physical exchanges.

The larger concern is what a loss would do to Haney’s future. A lucrative Garcia rematch would likely remain marketable if Catterall pulled off the upset, but Haney’s bargaining power could take an immediate hit. Losing his WBO belt before facing Garcia could weaken his leverage when the purse split is negotiated.

It could also delay the rematch.

If Catterall beats Haney, there would be considerable pressure on Devin to avenge the defeat rather than immediately move on to Garcia. Another training camp and dangerous fight would stand between Haney and the massive payday he wants, with a second loss to Catterall potentially doing serious damage to his career.

Amino Boxing believes Catterall has been smart to avoid getting dragged into Bill Haney’s social-media battles.

“Jack a smart dude. When you responding to Bill you already lost. Jack staying ahead of the bullshit. Not letting them control the narrative and destroy his reputation.”

Catterall did what he needed to do by publicly stating that he accepted the fight. “Accepted the fight and heard nothing since,” he said on X.

Now the decision rests with Team Haney. If they go elsewhere, the business logic isn’t difficult to understand. Catterall offers Devin considerable danger without providing the payday that makes taking the risk easier to justify.

Sports.title: Top Rank Faces Big Call On Abdullah Mason Against William Zepeda
Sports.content:
“That would be a career-defining fight for me at this point,” Mason said on The Porterway Podcast. “He has everything that somebody would wanna see me face. He’s strong on the front foot, a volume puncher, he’s using his head. It would definitely be a step up from any fight that I ever had before.”

Mason is correct about the step up. Zepeda presents an extreme version of the style that caused him trouble against Sam Noakes last November.

Noakes out-slugged Mason during stretches of their fight and applied constant pressure, forcing the younger fighter to get on his bike and box from the outside during the championship rounds. Mason won the decision to take the vacant WBO title, but it was a grueling night.

His first defense against Albert Bell on July 4 brought another difficult test. Bell fought Mason to a standstill through six rounds before Mason began roughing him up inside to gain control. Mason eventually dropped and stopped Bell in the 12th.

Zepeda would bring considerably more pressure than either opponent.

The 30-year-old threw 884 punches against Roach, landing 218. He has the chin to stay in front of opponents, throws combinations almost continuously, and gives them little time to set their feet.

That could be particularly uncomfortable for Mason, who likes loading up on uppercuts and other power shots. His punch resistance has also shown vulnerability. Yohan Vasquez dropped Mason twice in their 2024 fight before Mason recovered to score a second-round knockout.

Zepeda isn’t likely to disappear after landing one big shot, either. He’ll keep coming, forcing Mason to fight at a pace and under sustained pressure that he hasn’t dealt with as a professional.

“The Sam Noakes fight was a crazy fight, an amazing fight,” Mason said. “I’ve grown from all my past fights, so me being able to implement everything that I’ve learned, it will show where I’m at in the sport facing Zepeda, who’s coming off a great win.”

Mason clearly wants to find out where he is. Top Rank must decide if it wants the answer this soon.

Sports.title: “Bodybuilder Boxer”: Thurman Unsure If Benn Has The Skill To Beat Garcia
Sports.content:
“Yeah, it’s interesting. I still don’t know what to think too much about Conor Benn. You know, he reminds me of like just those guys at the gym that are a little bit like bodybuilder boxers. You know, like they’re just shredded. They train hard, they got the physique, and they’re rough and tough, but where exactly is his IQ? Where’s the skills? Where’s the technique?” Thurman told Fight Hub TV.

Garcia gives Benn an opportunity to answer those questions. Benn can apply relentless pressure, throw with power and force grueling exchanges, but Ryan possesses the faster hands and sharp counterpunching to punish aggressive entries.

Thurman isn’t dismissing Benn’s chances. He compared that raw style to dealing with a charging rhino, pointing out that pure force remains dangerous regardless of technical shortcomings.

“It’s not that it’s a guaranteed loss for a fighter of that type of caliber. It’s not a guaranteed loss, but at the highest level, you will run into skillful opposition,” Thurman said.

Ryan provides exactly that test.

Benn’s pressure gives him a route to making Garcia uncomfortable, particularly if he can trap the champion on the inside rather than allowing Ryan to operate at his preferred range. The danger comes while crossing that distance, where Garcia’s speed and counterpunching can make Benn pay for reckless attacks.

Thurman’s criticism places the burden on Benn to show that there is more to his game than pure athleticism when he meets Garcia.

Ghana News.title: ‘We truly care’ – UGMC responds to allegations of poor-quality care
Ghana News.content:
The University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) has reaffirmed its commitment to quality patient care amid criticism of its services, urging patients and their relatives to use the hospital’s established complaint channels when they have concerns.

The response follows criticism of the facility after Ghanaian-American comedian Michael Blackson publicly raised concerns about the care his mother received at the hospital before her death.

Speaking on JoyNews’ News Desk on Monday, August 10, Head of Public Relations and Client Services at UGMC, Barbara Hemeng, said the hospital takes concerns about patient care seriously and uses feedback to improve its services.

Read Also: Michael Blackson blasts UG Medical Centre over mother’s death

“At UGMC, we truly care about our patients, and we take reviews very seriously,” she said.

Ms Hemeng also expressed sympathy to families who have lost loved ones at the facility, acknowledging the pain and distress associated with such experiences.

She explained that the hospital continuously monitors feedback from patients and their relatives to identify gaps and improve service delivery.

However, Ms Hemeng urged patients and families not to resort to social media as their first option when dissatisfied with the care they receive, arguing that formal complaints provide the hospital with an opportunity to investigate specific concerns and take appropriate action.

“Going on social media to vent out your spleen does not help us improve upon our services. Let us all remember that UGMC is for all of us,” she said.

She encouraged patients and relatives with concerns about treatment or service delivery to lodge complaints through the hospital’s established channels to enable the relevant departments to investigate and respond appropriately.

UGMC maintains that patient feedback remains an important part of its efforts to improve the quality of care and services at the facility.

Ghana News.title: UGMC demands retraction, apology from Michael Blackson over ‘worst hospital’ claim
Ghana News.content:
The University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) has demanded a retraction and apology from Ghanaian American comedian Michael Blackson over his description of the facility as the “worst hospital in Ghana.”

UGMC says the comments have damaged its reputation and do not reflect the hospital’s clinical standards or overall performance.

Speaking on JoyNews Desk on August 10, the Director of Medical Affairs Dr Baffour Gyan said the assessment of a hospital should be based on its performance records, infrastructure and qualified personnel not an individual’s experience.

“To come out and say UGMC is the worst hospital that one I disagree totally,” he said.

Dr Gyan said UGMC is pursuing Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation as part of efforts to meet international standards and position the facility for medical tourism.

UGMC management also rejected allegations of misdiagnosis or negligence in the treatment of Blackson’s 83-year-old mother. According to Dr Gyan, she was referred to UGMC from another facility with a severe infection and spent eight weeks at the hospital, including six weeks in the Intensive Care Unit.

He said clinicians followed standard treatment protocols throughout her admission.

“For diagnosis and management, 100% we did not do anything wrong,” Dr Gyan said.

He added that the infection with which she was admitted was ultimately responsible for her death.

Dr Gyan, however, expressed condolences to the family, acknowledging the difficulty of losing a loved one despite efforts to save them. UGMC has confirmed that its lawyers have formally written to Blackson over his social media comments.

Dr Gyan said the hospital is seeking a retraction and apology and is awaiting the comedian’s response.

“Our lawyers have written to him just for him to retract and apologise for all that he said on social media,” he said.

Ghana News.title: X1 Division One League Super Cup launched as Attram De Visser draw 3-3 with Debibi United
Ghana News.content:
Attram De Visser staged a spirited second-half comeback to draw 3-3 with newly promoted Premier League side Debibi United as the fifth edition of the X1 Division One League Super Cup got underway at the Len Clay Stadium in Obuasi on Monday.

The Accra-based side found themselves 3-1 down in the opening Group A fixture after Debibi United took control of the game, but goals from Abdul Majid Maswud and Thomas Okyere completed the comeback and earned Attram De Visser a point.

Debibi United opened the scoring through Ibrahim Alhassan before Attram De Visser Junior restored parity to make it 1-1.

Kwadwo Antwi then restored Debibi United's lead before Clement Nketiah extended their advantage to 3-1.

Attram De Visser responded through Abdul Majid Maswud to reduce the deficit before Thomas Okyere completed the comeback with the equaliser.

The result saw both teams pick up a point as Group A action began, with former Premier League campaigners Real Tamale United scheduled to face Cape Coast Mysterious Ebusua Dwarfs in the second match of the opening day.

Before kick-off, Obuasi Municipal Chief Executive, Hon. Faustilove Appiah Kannin, performed the ceremonial kick-off to officially launch the fifth edition of the competition.

Attram De Visser's comeback was inspired by Abdul Majid Maswud, who was named Man of the Match after scoring his side's second goal.

“We were giving up, but our coach backed us up with his words and motivated us to come back and equalise when we were down,” Maswud said after the game.

“The group is very tight and the teams are well experienced and good. So, we have to come up with a good game and good tactics so that we can overcome them and, at the end, become the winners.”

Debibi United assistant coach Francis Makiya attributed the collapse to a lapse in concentration after his side had built a two-goal lead.

“We led 3-1, but I think in the last hour, there was a lack of concentration from my boys and Attram were able to come back,” Makiya said.

“I think they’re doing well, but there is more room for improvement.”

For Attram De Visser coach Godwin Attram, the tournament provides an important opportunity to assess his squad ahead of the new season.

“It’s a very exciting pre-season tournament and good for the players,” Attram said.

“We just want to see team organisation, structures, advantages and disadvantages of how the team attack and defend.”

The tournament is sponsored by Hoshii International Limited, producers of X1 Energy Drink and Hoshii Instant Rice, with the company represented at the opening day by Ivy Udanoh.

Udanoh said the partnership is aimed at strengthening the company's connection with football supporters while creating greater brand awareness.

“Ultimately, the partnership will help us build brand awareness and also get a stronger connection with the football community,” Udanoh said.

“So far, it’s been positive and quite exciting to see people passionate about football coming together to support their team and the brand as a whole.”

The opening Group A fixture produced a six-goal thriller, setting the tone for the remainder of the competition as the participating clubs continue their preparations for the new campaign.

Ghana News.title: World’s oceans hit record-high July temperatures
Ghana News.content:
The world's oceans hit their hottest-ever recorded temperatures in July, partly fuelled by developing El Niño conditions in the Pacific, according to the EU's climate monitoring service.

The average sea surface temperature (SST) outside the world's polar regions - between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south - was 20.96C last month, beating the previous high of 20.89C, set in 2023.

Last month was the joint second-warmest July globally on record, with temperatures 1.47C above the estimated pre-industrial average, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

Meanwhile, Western Europe experienced its hottest ever June and July, with prolonged hot and dry conditions fuelling extreme wildfires across the region.

Elsewhere, the UK is braced for its fifth heatwave of the year this week, as persistent dry weather puts further pressure on water supplies and could see more areas officially declared in drought.

Around Europe, sea surface temperatures in July reached record highs along the Atlantic coast and in the western Mediterranean, contributing to widespread strong and severe marine heatwaves.

Sea temperatures remained exceptionally high across much of the tropical Pacific, where El Niño conditions are developing and forecast to strengthen in the coming months.

El Niño is a natural weather pattern in the Pacific that combined with human-driven global warming can cause temperature spikes and more extreme weather.

Oceans are a vital regulator of the climate, absorbing most of the excess heat generated by greenhouse gas emissions and producing half of Earth's oxygen.

The greatest effect of ocean warming is on sea level rise. As seawater warms it expands, and this thermal expansion accounts for roughly a third of sea level rise recorded by scientists to date. That water encroaches on low-lying coasts and island nations.

Hotter seas are also driving longer and fiercer marine heatwaves, which have bleached coral reefs on a mass scale and decimated kelp forests and fisheries.

Warmer ocean surfaces also evaporate more heat and moisture into the air, intensifying tropical storms and loading them with heavier rainfall.

'Climate change is intensifying heat extremes'

Western Europe is experiencing an exceptional run of extreme heat - with record-breaking temperatures in June and July, and some areas facing their third or fourth heat wave since May.

The average temperature across western Europe for June and July was 21.62C - 2.79C above average and the highest for the two-month period.

"July 2026 was the third consecutive month of exceptional heat in western Europe," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.

Persistent high-pressure systems trapped heat over the region, she said, while dry soils reduced the ability to provide natural cooling.

"This is a clear example of how climate change is intensifying heat extremes, with heat and drought increasingly reinforcing one another," she added.

France, Spain, parts of Germany and the UK recorded exceptionally low rainfall and/or soil moisture, while soil moisture levels across much of western Europe were significantly lower than in 2022, when the region experienced severe drought.

River levels have been much lower than average - in some places exceptionally low -with the Seine, Rhine and Danube among those particularly affected.

Low flows exacerbate pressure on water supplies and irrigation, aquatic ecosystems, river transport and energy production.

Some rivers in Europe have recorded extremely low water levels, including the Danube

The prolonged hot and dry conditions have created favourable conditions for wildfires, with massive wildfires raging across western Europe last month and "exceptional activity" in terms of the area burned and smoke and emissions generated.

"Climate change is increasingly bringing the kinds of hot and dry conditions that favour large, high-intensity wildfires in southern Europe while extended the fire season northwards," said Laurence Rouil, director of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service.

Larger fires produce more smoke and inject it higher into the atmosphere, allowing it to travel much further, he said.

That means countries that experience relatively few wildfires could be increasingly affected by smoke traveling long distances.

Extreme weather 'new normal'

European wildfires haven been called "completely unprecedented" this summer

In the UK, meanwhile, the prolonged dry spell is increasing pressure on already-stretched water supplies.

England and Wales recorded their driest July since records began 190 years ago, according to the Met Office, while large parts of England and all of Wales have already been officially declared in drought.

The Environment Agency has warned that more areas of England could be declared in drought if dry conditions persist.

Weather that was once considered extreme is becoming the "new normal", according to the latest Met Office report on the UK's climate.

Its latest assessment found that the hottest day of the year in southern England is now 4.5C warmer than it was between 1961 and 1990.

"We are right now living in a time of historic and unprecedented change," said Mike Kendon, Met Office climate information scientist, adding that "evidence shows the climate of the 20th century has now gone".

Scientists say El Niño may temporarily push global temperatures even higher. Its effects are being felt against a backdrop of man-made warming, particularly the burning of fossil fuels.

The world is now about 1.4C warmer on average than it was in the late 19th Century.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod to roll out gold traceability system this year – Sammy Gyamfi
Ghana News.content:
Sammy Gyamfi, GoldBod CEO

The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says Ghana is set to begin implementing a national gold traceability system this year to track gold purchased from small-scale miners.

According to him, the absence of a formal traceability system has meant that GoldBod currently cannot determine what proportion of the gold it purchased from small-scale miners was responsibly mined.

Mr Gyamfi made the disclosure in response to questions about GoldBod’s purchase of 3.1 million ounces of gold from small-scale miners, compared with 2.8 million ounces produced by the large-scale mining sector.

Asked what percentage of the 3.1 million ounces could be traced to responsibly mined gold, he told 'Beyond The Numbers' Isaac Kofi Agyei that there was currently no component that could be traced.

“There is no component that we can trace because since Ghana started mining gold and trading gold, no government has pursued a traceability system,” he said on JoyNews.

He, however, noted that GoldBod has developed a responsible sourcing policy which prioritises traceability and is now taking steps to implement a system capable of tracking gold from its point of origin.

“We are currently involved in a national competitive tendering process to acquire that traceability technology. Following which, the onboarding process of eligible licensed small-scale miners or registered cooperatives will begin,” he explained.

Mr Gyamfi said 27 companies submitted bids for the traceability system, with the process now narrowed to about 17 companies following the completion of the technical evaluation.

“We're going onto the financial proposal to evaluate that, and then we'll be awarded. I don't think that the process will go beyond this year for the system, and we will get a system done in the next few months,” he said.

He stressed, however, that acquiring the technology would only constitute the first stage of the process.

According to him, the system is expected to eventually enable GoldBod to trace every gram of gold it purchases and sells back to its mine of origin.

The system will also help establish whether the source is licensed, how the gold was produced, whether mercury was used and whether child labour was involved.

Mr Gyamfi said the broader objective is to formalise gold production and bring Ghana's small-scale mining supply chain into compliance with international responsible-sourcing standards.

He believes this will strengthen Ghana's ability to access premium international markets, including the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), and secure better prices for the country's gold.

“How can we formalize those sources to be OECD compliant so that we can get LBMA market access for our gold and get better prices, better value, which means more revenue from our gold resources?” he asked.

He added that the onboarding of eligible small-scale miners onto the system is expected to begin this year.

“So that is what we are developing, and I can tell you that the system we acquired this year and implementation in terms of onboarding will start this year,” Mr Gyamfia added.

Ghana News.title: IGP promotes 25 police personnel over robbery, cocaine interception operations
Ghana News.content:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Christian Tetteh Yohuno has promoted 25 police personnel for their roles in a series of operations that led to the arrest of robbery suspects and the interception of suspected cocaine at the Tema Harbour.

According to a post shared on Facebook by the Service on Monday, August 10, the personnel, drawn from the Bono East, Tema and Western Central Police Regions, were recognised for their involvement in three separate operations, including the arrest of six suspects in connection with a robbery involving GH¢300,000, the apprehension of four suspected members of a robbery syndicate and the seizure of 866 parcels of suspected cocaine.

The promotions, according to the IGP, were based on performance and contribution of the personnel to the investigations and operations.

One of the operations for which the personnel were recognised was a robbery on July 19 along the Portor to Kawempe stretch off the Kintampo-Buipe Highway.

Six suspects were arrested in connection with the robbery, during which GH¢300,000 was reportedly stolen from a victim.

The operation formed part of the police response to robbery-related incidents along the highway and resulted in the arrest of the suspects believed to have been involved in the incident.

The personnel involved in the operation were subsequently considered for promotion based on their contribution to the arrests.

Another group of personnel was recognised for their role in the arrest of four suspected members of a robbery syndicate linked to a violent robbery at Wassa Akropong in the Tarkwa area.

The third operation involved the interception of 866 parcels of suspected cocaine at the Tema Harbour. It said the seizure represents one of the major drug interceptions cited by the police administration.

Personnel involved in the operation were recognised alongside officers who participated in the robbery investigations in Bono East and the Western Central Police Region.

The circumstances surrounding the shipment, including its intended destination and the identities of persons linked to it, were not detailed in the announcement.

Among those promoted are Chief Inspectors Bede Nwinbomeh and Joe Tetteh, who have also been granted automatic entry to the Police Academy.

Other promoted personnel include General Sergeants Elijah Ndaga Yinimi and Kaifan Sulemanna, as well as General Corporals Owusu Ansah Evans and Tansang Jonathan.

General Lance Corporals Osei Christopher Bonny, Kyei Francis, Ofori Francis, Anim Dominic and Asante Isaac were also promoted.

General Constables Adam Bakari Alhassan and Bakai Mark are among those elevated to their next ranks.

The detective personnel promoted are Detective Chief Inspector Frank Dzah; Detective Inspectors Edem Ametowoga, Abroso and Vincent Dankwah; and Detective Sergeants Salifu Yakubu and Samuel Mordzifa.

The police administration said six other personnel were also promoted to their next ranks in recognition of their contribution to the fight against crime.

Chief Inspectors Nwinbomeh and Tetteh's automatic entry to the Police Academy represents an additional recognition of their service.

The IGP and members of the Police Management Board (POMAB) congratulated the promoted personnel and urged them to maintain the standards that led to their elevation.

The police administration also indicated that it would continue to recognise personnel whose work contributes to crime prevention, investigations and public safety.

Ghana News.title: New York Times Billboard features Afua Asantewaa
Ghana News.content:
Two-time Guinness World Records (GWR) contender Afua Asantewaa O. Aduonum has been featured prominently on the renowned New York Times Billboard in New York City, Manhattan, USA.

The music marathon diva's exploitation attracted the attention of the historical, famous and busiest intersections in the world, resulting in her capture on the massive digital screen.

In 2023, the young lady made an audacious attempt to sing for five days continues in Accra, Ghana to break and set a world record.

However, she missed her target on technical grounds.

And daring as she is, she attempted it again a year later in Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city.

And having domiciled currently in Canada due to consistent attacks from a section of people and cyber bully, she is considering a third attempt on foreign land.

"It's an honor for me, my country, team and all who have contributed to making the Afua Asantewaa (Singathon) brand what it is today," she said after the feature.

The New York Times Billboard platform captures photo, video, or brand displayed on a massive digital screen in one of the busiest, most famous commercial intersections in the world. It symbolises elite celebrity or corporate status.

Ghana News.title: EOCO escalates Ghana investigation into Asante Berko bribery case after US conviction
Ghana News.content:
Asante K. Berko

The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has escalated its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the bribery case involving former Goldman Sachs investment banker and former Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) Managing Director, Asante Kwaku Berko.

The development follows Mr Berko’s conviction in the United States in connection with allegations of bribery arising from his period in the private sector.

In a statement issued on Monday, August 10, 2026, EOCO said it received a request last year from its counterparts in the United States in connection with investigations into the alleged bribery scheme.

The request sought information on specific individuals in Ghana who were considered relevant to the investigations, including a former Minister of State and public servants.

“Following receipt of the request, EOCO, in collaboration with the Attorney-General and Ministry of Justice, commenced preliminary work in relation to the Ghanaian aspects of the matter,” the Office said.

EOCO said it also closely monitored the proceedings in the United States because of the international dimensions of the case.

“Given the nature of the allegations and the international dimensions of the case, EOCO considered the evidence emerging from the U.S. proceedings to be potentially material to determining the appropriate scope and direction of any comprehensive investigation in Ghana,” it said.

The Office explained that its approach was deliberate, stressing that investigations must be properly grounded in evidence and capable of supporting subsequent criminal proceedings and asset recovery where appropriate.

“EOCO’s responsibility is not merely to commence investigations for the sake of public perception, but to ensure that investigations are properly grounded in evidence, conducted lawfully and capable where appropriate of supporting subsequent criminal proceedings and asset-recovery action,” it said.

Following the conclusion of the US proceedings and Mr Berko’s conviction, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice engaged the appropriate US authorities to obtain relevant evidence, records and information required to advance the Ghanaian investigation.

EOCO said the Attorney-General has subsequently directed it to escalate its investigations as the relevant information and official records are obtained from the competent authorities in the United States.

“EOCO has accordingly commenced the process of intensifying its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the matter,” the Office said.

EOCO stressed that the investigation will be conducted independently and in accordance with Ghanaian law.

It cautioned that Mr Berko’s conviction in the United States does not automatically establish criminal liability against any individual in Ghana.

“Any individual whose name appears in evidence obtained through the international cooperation process will be assessed independently on the basis of the evidence relevant to that person and in accordance with Ghanaian law,” it said.

The Office said its collaboration with US law enforcement authorities and the Attorney-General’s Office remains active.

It added that it would not disclose sensitive operational information that could compromise ongoing investigations, the integrity of evidence or any future prosecution.

EOCO assured the public that further information would be provided at the appropriate time.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Why choosing low-fat dairy is not necessarily better for your health
World.content:
For years, we thought low-fat dairy was the way to manage obesity. New research is increasingly questioning this logic.

Low-fat dairy products may not be healthier than full-fat, researchers say, challenging decades of common knowledge linking full-fat dairy to weight gain and cardiovascular conditions.

For decades, scientists and nutritionists preached switching to low-fat dairy to counter obesity and cholesterol, but new research suggests otherwise and goes a step further to indicate that, instead, a full-fat dairy serving could even offer some health benefits.

Research by Harvey Anderson, professor at the University of Toronto, adds to growing evidence that full-fat dairy can be part of a healthy diet.

The researchers found that eating three servings of full-fat dairy per day did not negatively affect body weight, body composition, energy metabolism, or blood lipid levels, as per a report published in The Journal of Nutrition.

So, what did the research find and how? And does low-fat make any difference?

What does the study show?

The researchers at the University of Toronto assigned 74 adults with overweight or obesity to one of three dietary groups, studied between September 2020 and February 2023.

One group followed a low-dairy, calorie-restricted diet; the second group followed an energy-neutral diet with three servings of dairy each day; the third group ate an unrestricted diet with three daily servings of dairy. Those assigned to the dairy groups were supplied with full-fat dairy products during the study.



After 12 weeks, researchers found no meaningful differences in weight gain, body composition, or cholesterol levels between people following the low-dairy diet and those eating three servings of dairy each day.

The research cites food guides in Canada and the United States recommending three servings of low- or no-fat dairy a day for adults, noting that the countries are not recognising recent evidence that full-fat dairy may be beneficial.

The study found that participants consuming more dairy showed improvements in blood pressure and better intake of calcium, protein and vitamin D.

“Those that had three servings of dairy didn’t have adverse levels of blood cholesterol or lipids or evidence of insulin resistance,” Anderson told the ScienceDaily website.

Why has full-fat dairy been frowned upon?

The basic nutritional logic has been straightforward: whole-fat dairy contains substantial saturated fat, and saturated fat raises LDL cholesterol, known as “bad cholesterol”; therefore, cutting the fat content of dairy should reduce cardiovascular risk.

Dietary guidance treated saturated fat as a major health risk and encouraged people to switch from whole milk and other full-fat dairy to low-fat or fat-free versions.

The underlying logic was not entirely wrong. Saturated fat raises cholesterol, and replacing saturated fat with unsaturated fats, particularly polyunsaturated fats found in foods such as nuts, seeds and vegetable oils, is associated with lower cardiovascular risk.

However, a large Harvard analysis published in 2016, involving more than 220,000 participants across three US cohorts, found that dairy fat itself was not associated with higher cardiovascular disease risk, but replacing dairy fat with polyunsaturated fat was associated with a 24 percent lower cardiovascular risk, while replacing it with vegetable fat was associated with a 10 percent lower risk.

Prof Anderson, who led the latest research, said the evidence from human research has not always matched those concerns. Some studies, including recent research led by Temerty Medicine professor Kozeta Milliku, have even reported positive or protective effects associated with dairy consumption, he noted.

How does new research counter it?

Existing popular understanding suggests that removing dairy fat was expected to help prevent excess weight gain. The new study complicates this assumption.



If three servings of full-fat dairy per day do not cause measurable increases in weight, body fat, or cholesterol, it suggests that the presence of dairy fat in a person’s diet does not automatically translate into the adverse metabolic effects that the old model predicted.

It also challenges the idea that the fat content printed on the dairy label is, by itself, a useful proxy for the food’s health effects.

However, the bigger question it posed was for the food matrix itself.

Older nutritional thinking often focused on individual nutrients: saturated fat was considered a risk factor, so a food containing more saturated fat was presumed to be worse.

But researchers are increasingly looking at dairy as a whole food matrix containing protein, minerals, vitamins, carbohydrates and fat. The way those components interact may affect how the body responds to the fat.

In simpler words, the health effects of a food may depend on how its components interact rather than simply on the amount of one nutrient it contains.

“With dairy products, it’s got two proteins – casein and whey – that are bound together with fat and with nutrients mixed in,” says Anderson.

World.title: One million evacuated as Typhoon Dolphin pummels east China: What we know
World.content:
Hundreds of flights have been grounded in China due to weather conditions caused by Dolphin.

Provinces in eastern China have been inundated with heavy rain and flooding caused by Typhoon Dolphin, the strongest storm to make landfall in China this year.

Dolphin struck eastern China, including Shanghai, with winds up to 150 kilometres per hour (93 miles per hour), forcing more than one million people to evacuate their homes. The storm has disrupted flights and other transport while bringing heavy rain, flooding and the risk of landslides across the region.

About 40 percent of flights in Shanghai were grounded on Monday due to the weather.

After Dolphin made landfall late on Sunday, it weakened to below cyclone strength and is forecast to weaken further as it moves inland.

Here is what we know:

When and where did Typhoon Dolphin make landfall?

The typhoon made landfall in Yuhuan in China’s Zhejiang province about 5:30pm (09:30 GMT) on Sunday, according to China’s meteorological authorities.

On Monday, Shanghai was badly hit with residents circulating the hashtag “Shanghai turns into the sea” on the Chinese social media platform Weibo.

Last month, Typhoon Bavi also made landfall in Zhejiang, causing the evacuation of 1.7 million people.

Where is the storm moving, and how much damage will it cause?

Torrential rain was expected on Monday across Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Fujian, northeastern Jiangxi, central and southern Anhui and much of Jiangsu.

Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250mm to 500mm (10 to 20 inches) of rain in all, according to forecasters.

China’s Ministry of Water Resources warned that the Qiantang, Yong, Jiao and Shuiyang rivers could experience major flooding while smaller rivers in the hardest hit areas could rise above warning levels.



Authorities also warned of a high risk of geological disasters in parts of Zhejiang with residents in areas under a red mountain-torrent warning told to follow local evacuation orders.

Since making landfall, Dolphin is forecast to track westwards before slowing over central and southwestern China and gradually losing strength, Wang Haiping, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Centre, told state broadcaster CCTV.

The slower movement could prolong heavy rainfall and increase the threat of flooding and landslides, particularly in mountainous areas and along smaller rivers.

How have the authorities responded?

The authorities have warned of the risk of severe flooding and landslides as the storm moves further inland and continues to bring heavy rain to densely populated areas of eastern China.

Shanghai evacuated at least 30,300 people while, in neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

Authorities also evacuated about 390,000 people in the Zhejiang city of Taizhou before Saturday evening.
