World.title: In Solving World War II ‘Puzzle’, Young Greeks Help ‘Heal a Wound’
World.content:
After wading through the archives at Arolsen, municipal registers, the Internet and other documents, the tram was able to return a wristwatch to the family of Vangelis Kerasiotis, who spent time in a forced labour camp in Germany in 1944, aged 19.

Having worked at the camp as an interpreter, Kerasiotis returned to Greece in 1945, where he moved in with a Jewish woman and joined the police. He died at the age of 25.

“The objects are of zero value in terms of their literal value, but they are of enormous value in terms of mental upliftment,” said his niece, Chrysanthi Kerasotou, who received the watch with her sister and mother during an event organised by the Greek government in late June.

Hotzidis, a historian, said that between 50,000 and 60,000 Greek Jews perished in the Nazi camps and at least 10,000 other Greeks were sent to labour camps, including leftists involved in the resistance against the Nazi occupation of Greece.

“We do not know if Kerasiotis was engaged in any political activity,” Hotzidis said. “The relatives did not mention anything, but even if wasn’t, his name was certainly heard somewhere by Greek collaborators of the German battalion security forces and some gendarmes who collaborated with the Germans.”

“It is important to remember, because this way we know not only our recent history, but we can think that it is good that all these events do not happen again,” he said. “So, first we must know them and secondly remember them, ensuring they are never forgotten.”

In Arolsen, Meiwes said that some 2,000 envelopes remain. For some, they known neither the nationality nor the identity of the person whose belonging are inside.

“It is possible that some of these still belong to Greek nationals,” she told BIRN.

The Nazis turned people into numbers, Meiwes said, so it is important “to give them back their names and to tell their stories”.

World.title: A Decade After North Macedonia’s Deadliest Floods, Dangers Remain
World.content:
On August 6, 2016 torrential rain triggered a devastating flash flood in the north-east outskirts of Skopje, killing 22 people and causing more than 30 million euros in damage.

Suburbs of the capital like Singelic and Cento, villages like Stajkovci and Aracinovo, and surrounding areas were among the worst hit, as torrents of water and mud swept through streets and homes within minutes.

“We narrowly escaped death. The water was almost two metres deep. I have never seen this kind of weather,” one Stajkovci resident said at the time. “It was terrible. We had only half a minute to get outside [the house] and save ourselves when the water surged,” said another.

In the aftermath, experts pointed to several factors that had turned an extreme weather event into a disaster. Around 93 litres of rain per square metre fell on the heavily deforested southern slopes of Skopska Crna Gora Mountain in just four hours, allowing water and mud to rush towards the settlements below.

World.title: Albania Could Face Costly Arbitration Battle After Scrapping Vlora Airport Plans
World.content:
An international arbitration dispute is looming after Albania’s Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy announced last week that it has officially started the procedure to terminate the concession contract for Vlora International Airport.

The decision follows a bitter legal tussle between the two consortium partners, Mabco Construction and 2A Group, which began in the autumn of 2025 over a dispute concerning the division of shares between them.

There have also been large confrontations between workers from the two companies over access to the site, and a series of court rulings. The deadlock persisted even after the Supreme Court in May rejected 2A Group's requests for interim measures to secure its lawsuit. That decision was later followed by additional blocking rulings issued by the Court of First Instance Tirana.

World.title: Albanian Court Puts Turkish Activist in Custody After Extradition Demand
World.content:
Protesters rally with pictures of victims of the 2013 Gezi Park protests in Istanbul, April 2022. Photo: EPA-EFE/SEDAT SUNA.

The Tirana Court on Friday ordered a custody remand for Julide Yazici, who is wanted for extradition by Turkey to serve a prison sentence for aiding a terrorist organisation – charges that she claims are motivated by her political activism.

Yazici was arrested on August 4 at Tirana Airport while travelling from France to Albania after it was discovered that she was wanted for extradition to Turkey.

The judge granted the prosecution’s custody request despite Yazici’s lawyer’s arguments that his client “holds political asylum status in France and poses no danger”, and could be placed under house arrest instead.

The lawyer, Artan Shllaku, said that the decision will be appealed.

Shllaku added that Yazici, who teaches at an elementary school in France, had visited Albania a year earlier to see relatives and had encountered no issues.

Yazici is wanted by Turkish authorities to serve the remainder of a four-year prison sentence – three years, five months and 22 days – for providing logistical support to and participating in a terrorist organisation.

According to a decision by the French National Court of Asylum dated November 2020, a document obtained by BIRN, Yazici was involved in political activism in Turkey and participated in the Gezi Park mass protests in 2013 against the administration led by Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

She actively supported the former People’s Democratic Party, HDP, a left-wing political group that supported Turkey’s Kurdish minority, and which later became the DEM Party.

The French court decision granting asylum to Yazici stated that she was arrested in January 2016 “for having allowed a young woman she did not know, who had been introduced to her by a friend, to stay in her student room”.

The French court decision in the document that Yazici had “a well-founded fear … of being persecuted if she returns to her country due to her political activism”.

Yazici is not the first Turkish national to be arrested in Albania for extradition in controversial circumstances in recent years. Teachers and others linked to the movement previously led by the now-deceased cleric Fethullah Gulen, which is classified as a terrorist organisation by the authorities under Erdogan, have also been detained and then deported in line with Ankara’s demands.

World.title: Secrecy Surrounds Croatia’s Arrest of Alleged Serbian State-Linked Hacker
World.content:
Photo illustration: EPA/SASCHA STEINBACH.

The Croatian and Serbian authorities are remaining tight-lipped over the arrest last week of a Serbian businessman named as Georgije V., 33, on suspicion of hacking into the computer systems of various Croatian state institutions and public agencies.

The Serbian man is reportedly suspected of hacking into the Croatian Interior Ministry, the Central Register of Pension-Insured Persons, the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, the Croatian Regulatory Agency for Network Activities, the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute, the Croatian Tax Administration and the Croatian Automobile Club.

Tomo Medved, the Minister of Croatian Veterans, was asked about the case on Friday but declined to provide details.

“I would like to commend the entire security and intelligence system for its responsible and vigilant monitoring and protection of the interests of the Republic of Croatia. Given the ongoing proceedings, I cannot comment further than that,” Medved told journalists.

Croatian daily Jutarnji list has reported that the arrest took place on July 28, when Georgije V. was on holiday in Croatia. He had arrived with his wife, two children and mother at a tourist resort on the Adriatic coast a few days earlier.

Following his arrest, police searched his electronic devices, vehicle and accommodation under court orders. They seized items and digital data allegedly linking him to criminal acts, including two mobile phones and a laptop containing a large amount of data.

The court ordered one month of pre-trial detention, despite the man offering 20,000 euros in bail money and his family home in Novi Sad as collateral.

Croatia’s Chief State Attorney, Ivan Turudic, initially sparked public interest on Monday when he made a comment about a case related to national security. It was then reported by Jutarnji list that Turudic was referring to the arrest of an alleged hacker linked to Serbia’s Security Intelligence Agency, BIA.

It is not known whether the suspect’s alleged access to the computer systems of various institutions and agencies endangered Croatia’s national security in any way, or what he did with any data he may have obtained.

Nera Gajdarov Beg, the suspect’s lawyer, told Jutarnji list that the court’s custody order is being contested.

“An appeal has been filed against the decision to order pretrial detention because we believe that not all legal requirements for such a decision have been met. At this point, I cannot provide details of the defence because the proceedings are in the investigation phase, which is secret,” Gajdarov Beg said.

The Serbian authorities have not commented on the arrest so far. However, Serbian media have reported that Georgije V. is the owner of an active Novi Sad-based company specialising in computer programming and cybersecurity.

World.title: Croatian Serb Leader Deplores Hate Speech at Operation Storm Commemoration
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Milorad Pupovac, president of the Independent Democratic Serb Party, SDSS, and MP, on Friday said that slogans and chants heard on the streets of Knin on August 5, the day marking the 31st anniversary of Operation Storm, represented a “serious attack on constitutional values and democracy”.

Pupovac, leader of the main party representing Serbs in Croatia, argued that “hatred and incitement to crime are incompatible with true patriotism”.

At a press conference, he showed a compilation of recordings from Knin, the town that was the headquarters of a rebel Serbian statelet crushed by the Croatian Army’s Operation Storm in 1995.

They included sports fans and army veterans singing songs glorifying the Ustasha – the army of the Independent State of Croatia, NDH, a World War II fascist puppet state operating under the patronage of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy.

The recordings also showed people chanting: “We Croats do not drink wine, only the blood of Chetniks [Serbian nationalists] from Knin”; “The battle is fought, it is fought, the Ustasha flag is flying”, as well as insults directed at St Sava, the patron saint of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

“Those who have been trying to pass this off as an act of patriotism for years are actually seriously violating the true values of patriotism. In peacetime, the greatest patriotic virtue is constitutional patriotism,” Pupovac said.

He added that such behaviour was a “vicious attack on democracy”.

The SNV cited articles of the Croatian Constitution that it believes were violated by the shouting of the Ustasha salute “For the Homeland, Ready” and other glorifications of the NDH. The violations came after, not during, the official anniversary celebrations, it said.

Every year, Knin hosts a commemoration of Operation Storm, which liberated about 18 per cent of Croatia’s territory from rebel Serb forces and was followed by the flight of around 200,000 Serbs from Croatia. Some of them later returned.

SDSS leader Pupovac also criticised the Croatian judicial authorities, questioning why the State Attorney’s Office often does not react to hate speech and incitement to violence, appealing for an end to what he called a policy of appeasement.

He warned that failure to condemn such phenomena represents a direct threat to the Serb community in Croatia, and to all citizens who advocate for a state governed by the rule of law.

World.title: Iraq unveils dual pipeline plan to Faysh Khabur and Baniyas via Chevron
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Monday, August 10, 2026, plans to construct a major new pipeline network featuring two strategic export routes toward Faysh Khabur and the Syrian port of Baniyas. The infrastructure push aims to diversify Iraq’s crude oil export outlets beyond its primary southern Gulf terminals.

Deputy Oil Minister for Extraction Affairs, Nseer Aziz, chaired an executive planning meeting to establish implementation frameworks for the multi-billion-dollar project. Discussions centered on finalizing investment mechanics under a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) model with a consortium of global energy firms including UCC, TI Capital, and Chevron.

Key Infrastructure & Project Details

Dual Export Corridors: Route 1:Basra – Haditha – Faysh Khabur (connecting southern oilfields to northern export infrastructure near the Turkish border). Route 2:Haditha – Baniyas (reactivating the strategic Mediterranean export route across Syria).

Investment Model: To be executed under a BOOT (Build-Own-Operate-Transfer) framework in partnership with international consortium partners Chevron, UCC, and TI Capital.

Inter-Agency Coordination: Attended by leadership from Basra Oil Company (BOC), North Oil Company (NOC), Missan Oil Company (MOC), state oil marketer SOMO, and the Ministry’s Studies and Planning Directorate.

Syrian Transit Agreement: Follows a U.S.-sponsored Memorandum of Understanding signed between Iraq and Syria on July 17, 2026, to reactivate the historic Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline corridor.

The dual-pipeline initiative marks a decisive effort by Baghdad to reduce its reliance on southern Gulf ports following severe disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

By linking Basra’s southern production hubs directly to northern transit corridors at Faysh Khabur and Mediterranean terminals at Baniyas, Iraq aims to secure uninterrupted crude flows to global markets, lower war-risk freight costs, and enhance long-term energy marketing flexibility.

World.title: Iraq Stock Exchange trades surge 55% in July as ISX60 Index gains 2.1%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraq Stock Exchange (ISX) recorded a sharp acceleration in trading volume during July 2026, with total shares traded jumping 54.9% month-on-month despite broader regional economic headwinds.

Official exchange data shows that 166.66 billion shares changed hands across 21 trading sessions, generating an aggregate turnover of 120.03 billion Iraqi Dinars ($91.6 million)—a 1.2% increase compared to June figures.

Key market performance metrics

Trading Volume: 166.66 billion shares traded, marking a 54.9% surge from June.

Trading Value: 120.03 billion IQD (~$91.6M), up 1.2% month-on-month.

Transaction Count: 24,342 executed deals, declining 8.3% month-on-month.

Corporate Participation: 85 out of 125 listed joint-stock companies actively traded during the month.

Index Movements: ISX60 Main Index: Closed at 1,041.07 points, gaining 2.1% from June’s close of 1,019.39 points. ISX15 Benchmark: Closed at 1,267.67 points, edging down 0.48% from 1,273.79 points.



The ISX operates under the oversight of the Iraq Securities Commission (ISC), facilitating electronic trading for 125 listed companies through 38 licensed brokerage firms.

Banking and financial institution equities continued to dominate overall trading volume and liquidity during July, offsetting softer performance across industrial and hospitality counters as retail and institutional investors repositioned portfolios heading into the second half of the year.

World.title: Iraqi Airways resumes direct Basra to Delhi flights
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Airways announced on Monday, August 10, 2026, that it will resume direct commercial flights between Basra International Airport and Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi starting August 18. The route will operate once weekly on Tuesdays.

The direct service had been suspended since early March due to regional security escalations. According to an official statement from the state-owned carrier, flight operations are being reactivated following regional de-escalation and rising passenger travel demand between Iraq and India.

Key Operational Details

Route: Basra (BSR) to New Delhi (DEL) direct service.

Flight Frequency: Weekly service operating every Tuesday, beginning August 18, 2026.

Background: Suspended in early March 2026 due to regional airspace and security disruptions.

Network Expansion: Iraqi Airways has launched or resumed more than 10 regional and international flight routes over the past two months.

The resumption of the Basra–Delhi line reflects a broader push by Iraqi Airways to expand its international flight network and restore routes linking major Iraqi cities with key international destinations.

India remains a major destination for Iraqi travelers seeking medical care, commercial partnerships, and higher education, making the direct link between Iraq’s southern economic hub and Delhi a key commercial route for the national carrier.

World.title: Shiite political rift widens over militia disarmament
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Health and National Approach Alliance (Al-Nahj Al-Watani, formerly Al-Fadhila) leader Abdul Hussein Al-Musawi addressed growing political divisions among Shiite leadership regarding the federal mandate to restrict weapons strictly to state control on Sunday, August 9, 2026.

Speaking in a televised interview with journalist Zainab Rabiee monitored by the 964 Network, Al-Musawi—a key figure within the ruling Coordination Framework—emphasized that armed factions represent patriotic Iraqis who made monumental sacrifices during the war against ISIS.

However, he firmly defended the government’s disarmament initiative, stating that anyone denying that weapons restriction is a formally approved parliamentary program suffers from “cognitive strabismus” (intellectual blindness).

Key Takeaways from Al-Musawi’s Statements

State Monopoly on Arms is Law: Al-Musawi stressed that restricting weapons to state institutions is not an arbitrary executive decision, but a core government program explicitly voted on and passed by the Iraqi Parliament.

Direct Dialogue with Factions: He called for candid, unmediated conversations with armed factions, warning against “viewing the future through the lens of the past” and urging groups to adapt to current political realities.

Preventing Economic Isolation: Citing Iran’s struggles under international sanctions, Al-Musawi warned that maintaining rogue armed structures risks plunging Iraq into global economic isolation and targeted blockades.

U.S. Coalition Drawdown: He noted that foreign military forces have largely completed their exit from Iraq, claiming remaining U.S. and coalition personnel now number fewer than 60 across the country.

Al-Musawi’s remarks highlight deepening friction within Shiite political circles as Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administration approaches its September 30 deadline for non-state armed groups to hand over heavy weaponry or fully integrate into state security organs.

While hardline factional leaders continue to push back against full integration, moderate framework figures like Al-Musawi are increasingly advocating for pragmatic compliance to safeguard Iraq’s financial system, maintain international investment, and establish full institutional sovereignty.

World.title: Embattled Infantino target of letter from three confederations
World.content:
Lausanne – FIFA president Gianni Infantino came under renewed fire on Monday as a joint letter from three confederations — UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC — declared football “belongs to no individual”.

Infantino has been the butt of scathing criticism ever since launching, and then withdrawing within days, a plan to bring in private investment into FIFA competitions, including the World Cups.

FIFA had hit back on Saturday at “a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine” football’s governing body and Infantino.

However, Monday’s letter from the governing bodies of European football (UEFA), North and Central America (CONCACAF) and Asia (AFC), showed his critics were unbowed.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the confederations added.

World.title: Chinese AI drives price competition among US labs
World.content:
Beijing – Artificial intelligence users are shopping around as US giants face fierce competition from Chinese rivals — and in Beijing’s tech district, drinkers at an AI-themed bar can even plug in to DeepSeek for free.

A new generation of cost-efficient, high-performance Chinese AI is putting pressure on Silicon Valley’s leading labs to lower prices to grab market share as they try and find ways to turn a profit.

ChatGPT maker OpenAI has slashed fees by 80 percent for its latest lightweight model “Luna”, and Anthropic has unveiled a model approaching its most powerful system’s performance at half the price.

Meanwhile some of China’s buzziest AI companies are raising fees as their open-source offerings gain traction among businesses and programmers worldwide.

DeepSeek — whose V4 Flash tops the usage leaderboard of technical platform OpenRouter — said last week it plans a “significant increase” in prices for programmers.

Thirsty Beijingers have another option: free AI for customers at AGI Bar, which opened last summer as a hub for developers, founders and investors.

The bar is decorated with references to China’s AI boom, with logos of the country’s major labs on the walls and the menu full of jokes riffing on tech jargon.

Its signature drink AGI — “Artificial General Intelligence”, meaning future AI tools as clever as humans — is a glass almost entirely full of beer foam, a nod to the frothy hype rife in the industry.

“It’s quite common for bars to provide free Wi-Fi with routers, so I’ll provide free tokens,” or units of AI usage, bar owner Song De told AFP.

– Challengers –

The bar in Zhongguancun, often called China’s Silicon Valley, has two boxy Nvidia workstations to self-host DeepSeek V4 Flash — meaning Song doesn’t need to pay the Chinese startup to use its model.

Large language models are the technology that underpins chatbots and other AI tools by crunching vast amounts of digital data.

Song, an independent AI developer himself, is one of many swapping the most cutting-edge, bells-and-whistles — and expensive — models, like Anthropic’s Fable 5, for leaner alternatives like V4 Flash.

These are much cheaper to run and good enough for many purposes, such as helping run AI agents that can carry out real-world tasks autonomously, experts say.

“There’s a lot of stuff that can be done with older models, or lesser models, or small language models,” said technology analyst Jack Gold, founder of J.Gold Associates.

“Especially as we move into the agentic world, a lot of the models will be running locally.”

New Chinese AI models big and small — from Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 to Alibaba’s popular Qwen series — are grabbing attention as challengers to Anthropic and OpenAI’s lead.

Both US companies are preparing to go public, which means they “need to start showing a profit”, Gold told AFP.

“I hesitate to say it’s a price war because we’re not quite there yet. But it’s certainly a price competition to try and get more users on board,” Gold said.

“Also there’s a lot of pressure from enterprises to say: agents are great, AI is great, but I can’t be spending twice the annual salary for (a given employee) on AI.”

– ‘The cheaper, the better’ –

Chinese AI models are often open-source, meaning they can be modified by programmers — unlike top US options, where the underlying code and data is locked away.

“Open-source is closing the performance gap with closed models faster than anyone expected,” said Wang Tiezhen, an independent AI consultant and former head of APAC ecosystem at developer platform HuggingFace.

“Last year’s frontier is quickly becoming today’s commodity,” he told AFP.

Smaller US players are also fuelling competition in the fast-evolving sector.

Elon Musk’s xAI has slashed the price of some Grok models, while Meta just released a low-cost option called Muse Spark 1.2.

Leo Feng, founder of Chinese agent operating system Cola.APP, said price cuts are “an inevitable trend” that “may lead to a boom in downstream applications”.

And Max Liu of LobeHub, another agent system, sees international AI price competition as “a good thing for the world as a whole”.

“The cheaper AI is, the better,” Liu said.

World.title: One woman confirmed dead in western Canada wildfire
World.content:
Montreal – An 80-year-old woman died while fleeing her home to escape a massive wildfire in Canada’s British Columbia province, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) said late Sunday.

The Summerland fire, which broke out Friday near Okanagan Lake, has spread rapidly and led to the evacuation of more than 20,000 people, with Canadian officials declaring a state of emergency.

The fire covered more than 13,600 hectares (33,600 acres) as of late Sunday and was considered out of control, according to the BC Wildfire Service.

The RCMP confirmed that “an 80-year-old woman has died as a result of the Summerland (Bald Range) wildfire.”

The Meadow Valley resident “was attempting to leave her home, along with one member of her family, due to the wildfires when she reportedly died suddenly,” police said.

No other known fatalities have been reported, according to police.

British Columbia Premier David Eby said he was “deeply saddened by the news.”

Emergency responders on Saturday had to airlift 50 people to safety as the Summerland wildfire forced overnight evacuations, CTV News reported.

Prime Minister Mark Carney earlier posted his gratitude to firefighters and first responders on X, thanking them for “working tirelessly to keep people safe.”

“The federal government stands ready to help and support the government of British Columbia in these efforts. I’m keeping everyone forced from their homes in my thoughts and hoping they can return safely soon,” Carney said.

The BC Wildfire Service reported more than 100 active wildfires in the province as of late Sunday.

“We are expecting a high potential for lightning-caused wildfire starts, particularly in the central Interior and the Okanagan which are receiving limited precipitation and dry lightning,” the service said.

Human-induced climate change doubled the likelihood of the extreme fire conditions behind this year’s Canadian wildfires, researchers at the World Weather Attribution group earlier said.

World.title: Asian stocks track Wall St higher after US job losses ease rate fears
World.content:
Hong Kong – Stocks rose Monday as investors pared their bets on a US interest rate hike after data showed thousands of jobs were lost in July, though sentiment was dented by another spike in oil prices as hopes for an end to the Middle East crisis fade.

Tech firms enjoyed a fresh bout of buying following a volatile run in recent weeks, with Japanese and Korean chipmakers leading the charge.

The positive mood was fuelled by figures from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics that showed 23,000 jobs were lost last month, while growth in May and June was revised down.

The reading suggested the world’s number one economy was slowing, though traders welcomed the prospect the Federal Reserve will hold off hiking borrowing costs for the time being.

The chances of an increase in September were slashed to about 43 percent from 64 percent a week ago, according to Bloomberg.

Inflation data due later this week will be the next guide for investors.

The news helped Wall Street higher, with the S&P 500 ending at a fresh record high, while tech firms — which benefit from lower rates — helped the Nasdaq pile on more than one percent.

And the gains filtered through to Asia, with Tokyo climbing two percent thanks to healthy advances for Kioxia, Tokyo Electron and Advantest. Seoul was also up as chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung rallied.

Hong Kong, Taipei, Shanghai, Wellington and Jakarta were also up.

“Markets treated the report as a meaningful challenge to near term Fed rate hike expectations, effectively concluding the Fed has time on its side,” wrote National Australia Bank’s Rodrigo Catril.

But he added: “The report reduces the case that the labour market is adding inflation pressures, but it does not provide a clean green light for a dovish pivot.

“The report is unlikely, by itself, to deter a September hike… inflation remains the more pressing side of the mandate. The next (consumer price index) prints (for July and August) ahead of the September Federal Open Market Committee meeting are the key data releases to watch.”

The dollar clawed back the losses suffered Friday in reaction to the jobs figures, and continued to gain against the yen after plunging earlier this month when US and Japanese authorities embarked on a historic joint intervention to support the Japanese unit.

Crude prices jumped around one percent to extend gains at the end of last week as Iran’s Revolutionary Guards insisted Sunday that they would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the United States complied with a list of demands.

Tehran insists on retaining control of the waterway — through which a fifth of world oil and LNG pass — after the war and wants to charge tolls for passage, which Washington has pushed back against.

Attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire, and mediators have urged both sides to return to the terms of a subsequent June memorandum that set out a path for peace talks.

Iran on Saturday released a list of conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to the war on all fronts, the lifting of a US counterblockade of Iranian ports, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage, the Tasnim news agency reported.

Those conditions echoed the terms of the June agreement, which included a provision to create a $300 billion reconstruction fund for Iran.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday that their strategy was to maintain their blockade “until the enemy accepts all our conditions… the strait is now actually a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway”.

For his part, US President Donald Trump said in an interview: “We are low-keying it.”

“We are only semi-negotiating with them,” he was quoted as saying. “We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”

“It will work out,” he added. “It’s like a chess game.”

World.title: Jharkhand protesters defy tear gas, lathi charge to enter assembly premises - top developments
World.content:
Job aspirants clash with police during a protest near the Jharkhand assembly in Ranchi

Protesters enter assembly premises; House adjourned

Former JPSC chief L Khiangte arrested in recruitment exam case

Rahul Gandhi condemns use of force against students

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Protesters demand cancellation of exams, independent probe

Government accuses BJP of hijacking protest

NEW DELHI: Thousands of job aspirants protesting alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations clashed with security forces on Monday after breaching multiple barricades and attempting to reach the state assembly. Police used water cannons, fired tear gas shells and carried out a lathi-charge as protesters moved towards the assembly premises.The protest, now in its 17th day, has intensified despite several rounds of talks between the government and demonstrators.The agitators are demanding cancellation of several recruitment exams, reforms in the JPSC and JSSC, and an independent probe into alleged irregularities.Some protesters breached barricades and entered the Jharkhand assembly premises. Police used water cannons and fired several rounds of tear gas when the protesters reached the final barricade near Jagannathpur Temple, around 200 metres from the assembly.Despite the security action, a section of protesters managed to symbolically enter the assembly premises. Police also resorted to a lathi-charge after the demonstrators attempted to move forward.Several protesters claimed they were injured, including female students.The assembly was adjourned for the day in the afternoon.Four policemen were injured after protesters allegedly pelted stones at security personnel during a march towards the Jharkhand assembly in Ranchi, city SP Paras Rana said.The march began around 10.30am from outside the old assembly building and coincided with chief minister Hemant Soren's 51st birthday.Jharkhand CID arrested former JPSC chairperson L Khiangte in connection with alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 20.Khiangte, a 1988-batch IAS officer, was appointed JPSC chairperson in February last year after retiring as the state's chief secretary. He resigned from the post on July 22, saying he had voluntarily stepped down to facilitate an impartial investigation.The former JPSC chief had been questioned four times since July 28. His arrest came a day after all three JPSC members â Ajeeta Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmad â resigned after being summoned by the CID for questioning.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticised the use of force against the protesting students, saying they had a right to peaceful protest."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong," Gandhi said, adding that only dialogue could resolve the issue. He urged the state government to continue listening to the protesters and resolve their concerns immediately.The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which is spearheading the agitation, has demanded comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission.The protesters are seeking cancellation of several recruitment examinations, including the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, and an independent probe by either the CBI or a panel of retired High Court judges from outside the state.They said the government had agreed to cancel only three of the 13 examinations they want scrapped.State minister Sudivya Kumar alleged that the agitation had moved beyond a students' movement and was being driven by the BJP's political agenda. He claimed the government had already fulfilled 95% of the protesters' demands.BJP Yuva Morcha state president Shashank Raj, however, called the police action a "black day for democracy" and urged chief minister Hemant Soren not to be "insensitive" towards the students' demands.

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday restated his three demands, which he termed as"non-negotaibles", to break the Parliament deadlock.In his "unnegotiable list of demands", the Congress leader reiterated that the Union home minister Amit Shah must tell Parliament who ordered firing against students during NEET paper leak protest. He said, apart from Shah's statement, PM Modi should apologise for what happened and he called for an accountablity over the donation theft in Ayodhya Ram Mandir."The question was always that Amit Shah has to make it clear who authorised the shooting of our youngsters in Delhi. Pellet guns were fired, students were beaten with lathis with nails on them. He should come clean. Did he order it or did he not order it? If he ordered it, he is guilty of getting our children shot. And if he didn't know about it happening, he's incompetent. Either way, he should go. This was the discussion," Rahul Gandhi said in a presser.He further said: "Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi says, "The question was never that Mr Amit Shah is going to come and give a speech on some general topics in Parliament. Second, the Prime Minister apologises for what has happened. And third was the issue of the Ram temple theft.People very close to the Prime Minister have stolen from the Ram Mandir. These are the three issues."Rahul said opposition was not "interested in Amit Shah's fantasy conversations", saying: "We are interested in whether he authorised or didn't authorise the shooting of our children. First, he should make that abundantly clear. After that, the question of any discussion arises. That is the situation. And that is what the opposition is demanding. That is what we have been demanding for the last 15 days"."For 15 days, neither Prime Minister nor home minister had courage to come to Parliament, guts to own up to what they have done," he said.Rahul Gandhi's remarks comes hours after Union Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said that home minister Amit Shah was prepared to respond in Parliament on the student protest crackdown. Rijiju, however, asked members not to disrupt the proceedings when the statement is made."The offer made by the government is very clear that it is ready to have a full and detailed discussion on students' movement and activities related to it," news agency ANI quoted Rijiju saying.Emphasising the need for an uninterrupted parliamentary process, Rijiju urged the opposition to hear the government's response before raising further issues."My only point made to the opposition is that while the discussion and a reply are being made, the opposition should not create disturbances to prevent the statement of the home minister," he added. "They must listen to the reply of the home minister and the government. Once discussion begins, we must have a threadbare discussion."

World.title: Right wing commentator TG Mohandas gets bail over controversial remarks on NEET student protest
World.content:
A court in Thiruvananthapuram on Monday granted bail to right-wing political commentator T G Mohandas, who was arrested over alleged remarks in a YouTube video concerning a student protest in New Delhi linked to the NEET paper leak.

Mohandas was produced before the Thiruvananthapuram Additional Chief Judicial First Class Magistrate Court for remand proceedings. Judge Mithun Gopi G S granted him bail after hearing arguments from both sides.

Police had taken Mohandas into custody from his residence in Mattancherry, Kochi, on Sunday evening. His arrest was formally recorded on Monday.

ALSO READ |

The case has been registered under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Information Technology Act and the Kerala Police Act.

The Thiruvananthapuram Cyber Police also informed the court that additional charges had been added for allegedly using words, sounds, gestures or objects intended to insult a woman's modesty, as well as for criminal intimidation involving severe threats.

The prosecution asked the court to allow Mohandas to remain in custody for further investigation. It argued that he was an influential person who could potentially influence witnesses or interfere with evidence if released.





His defence opposed the request, citing his age and health condition. His lawyer also argued that all the offences invoked against him were bailable.

After considering the submissions, the court granted Mohandas bail. It directed him to appear before the investigating officer for three days as part of the ongoing probe and to appear before police whenever required.

What did he say

The case stems from a complaint against videos posted on Mohandas' YouTube channel, 'Pathrika'. The complaint alleged that the videos were capable of disturbing public order and creating fear and unrest.

In one of the videos, Mohandas allegedly said the Delhi students' protest "could lead to incidents of gang rape" and claimed that there would be no complaints because "those attending the protest like rape and there are girls who enjoy being raped".

He further claimed that although some people would be killed or permanently injured, the situation would be brought under control within hours and the bodies shifted to hospitals.

World.title: Government says LoP Rahul Gandhi to sit per the table of precedence during Independence Day
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Defence secretary RK Singh on Monday said leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on August 15 and will be seated immediately after the Union Cabinet ministers.

"Leader of opposition has been invited, and his seating would be as per the Table of Precedence, which is exactly after Cabinet ministers," Singh told news agency ANI.

In 2024, Congress criticised the government over Rahul Gandhi's seating arrangement during the Independence Day celebrations, alleging that he was seated in the "fifth row" and calling the move a display of "pettiness" and a disregard for democratic norms.

Officials from the ministry of defence, which organises the event, had then said the seating was arranged "according to the Table of Precedence".

Congress had also accused the Centre of violating established protocol and undermining democratic decorum after Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge were seated in the third row during the Republic Day celebrations earlier this year.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

However, the Centre clarified the that the seating arrangements were made as per the protocol.





As per protocol, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha has a rank equivalent to that of a Cabinet minister.

According to the Warrant of Precedence issued by the President's Secretariat, seating arrangements at state and ceremonial occasions are decided based on constitutional rank and office, and not political affiliation.

The Table of Precedence is a protocol list that applies to state and ceremonial occasions, including national events such as Republic Day celebrations, and has no application to the day-to-day functioning of the government.

World.title: 80th Independence Day: In a 1st, Vande Mataram to be sung from ramparts of Red Fort
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time during this year's Independence Day celebrations, which will be led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, according to a statement by the defence ministry.

The occasion will also mark 150 years of Vande Mataram. PM Modi will unfurl the National Flag and address the nation from the historic monument in Delhi.

"Vande Mataram will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time," the statement said.

This year's celebrations will focus on Yuva Shakti, highlighting the contribution of India's young population to the country's journey towards becoming a Viksit Bharat by 2047.

World.title: Watch: Jharkhand protesters echo Bihar, dance as police turn water cannons on them
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Echoing scenes from Bihar where student protesters recently danced under police water cannons, Jharkhand job aspirants on Monday broke followed suit as police turned water cannons on them during their 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march in Ranchi.

Thousands of protesters breached multiple barricades while marching towards the Jharkhand assembly over alleged recruitment exam irregularities, prompting police to use water cannons, tear gas shells and lathi charges.

Tensions escalated when the protesters reached the final barricade near Jagannathpur Temple, on the road leading to the assembly.

Police used water cannons to disperse the gathering, followed by lathi charges when protesters attempted to move forward.

Several rounds of tear gas shells were also fired when the crowd came within around 200 metres of the assembly.

The protest comes as the agitation led by the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch entered its 17th day. The march began around 10.30am from outside the old assembly building and coincided with chief minister Hemant Soren's 51st birthday.

The scenes in Ranchi came weeks after student protesters in Bihar similarly danced under police water cannons during a march towards the chief minister's residence over alleged examination paper leaks, unemployment and recruitment irregularities.

In Patna, protesters had broken into dance as water jets were used to stop them from advancing, while others sat on the road and raised slogans.

World.title: Prosecution for money laundering after conviction for predicate offences is not double jeopardy: Karnataka High Court
World.content:
When a person is convicted for offences under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) or other laws, which are described as a scheduled offence/predicate offence under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), the subsequent prosecution of such convicted persons exclusively under the provisions of the PMLA does not amount to second trial for the same offences, said the High Court of Karnataka.

“The prosecution under the PMLA is neither the second trial for the same offence nor a Constitutional transgression. The offence under the PMLA derives its existence from the laundering of proceeds of crime, though emanating from the commission of predicate offence,” the court observed.

Justice M. Nagaprasanna passed the order while dismissing the petitions filed by 11 persons, who were convicted for various offences under the IPC, for looting some persons in 2016 in the guise of exchanging the demonetised notes, and cheating the people of several lakhs of rupees

The convicted petitioners are Dilip alias JCB Dilipa, Aananda D.B alias CCTV Ananda, Rajesh D.M. alias Raji, Ananda alias Mysurammana Mommaga, Umesh R.K. alias Bonda, Channakeshava C. alias Sanju, Cheluvaraju C.S. alias Onduvare, Mahadevaswamy D.R. alias Keera, Purushothma D.R. alias Purushi, Babu D.G., and Ramalinga alias Buka. The petitioners were convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for six years in 2024 by the trial court, and their appeals against conviction are pending before the High Court.

“It is a prosecution of an independent statutory offence (under PMLA), in which the petitioners have to come out clean in a full blown proceeding before the special court, as the prohibition under Section 300 of the Criminal Procedure Code extends only to a second trial for the same offence and not to a prosecution for a distinct offence under another enactment,” the High Court said while dismissing their petition.

World.title: GVMC Commissioner unveils poster for photo exhibition
World.content:
GVMC Commissioner Ketan Garg on Monday unveiled the poster for the annual ‘News in Frames’ photography exhibition, to be organised by the Vizag Photo Journalists’ Association (VPJA) at Visakha Museum on August 19 and 20.

VPJA representatives met Mr. Garg and invited him to inaugurate the exhibition on August 19. They showed him a video featuring rare photographs captured by photojournalists on various occasions.

Mr. Garg appreciated the photographs and suggested displaying selected images on digital screens at the exhibition. He said photography could preserve events, emotions and history for future generations, and highlighted the role of photojournalists in bringing significant developments to the public.

The exhibition will feature photographs on public life, culture, nature, development and other aspects of society. It will be open from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on both days. Entry is free.

World.title: T.N. forms Anti-Narcotics Task Force to combat drug menace
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government has created an ‘Anti-Narcotics Task Force’ - a new unit to combat the menace of drugs. A total of ₹264 crore has been sanctioned to operationalise the force that would function under the direct control of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.

A total of 65 ANTF units would be established across the State to detect and take stringent action against drug-related crimes. Dedicated police stations manned by an Inspector of Police and other supporting staff are set to come up in all cities and districts. An officer in the rank of an Additional Director General of Police would head the ATNF.

In a proposal sent to the government, DGP and Head of the Police Force Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, said that the emergence of ANTF police stations would transform anti-narcotics enforcement into a State-wide policing mission. Besides police officers and personnel, the unit would have specialised investigation units comprising intelligence analysts, technical experts, legal officers and others.

Dedicated teams would form part of the Intelligence and Cyber Surveillance, Enforcement & Investigation, Financial Investigations, Prosecution and Awareness and Rehabilitation verticals of the force.

The State government accorded sanction to create posts of 65 Police Inspectors, 260 Sub-Inspectors and 1,300 police personnel for the ANTF. The primary objective of the new force would be to initiate strict legal action on the smuggling and sale of narcotics drugs and abuse by way of collecting intelligence, registering cases, conducting financial investigation, and pursuing effective prosecution of the cases.

A dedicated 24/7 control room would be set up at the ANTF headquarters in Chennai. It would function as the central coordination and communication hub for statewide anti-narcotics enforcement, facilitating the receipt, processing and dissemination of intelligence inputs and maintaining real-time communication with field units engaged in operations.

The manpower and infrastructure of the existing Narcotics Control Bureau CID would be utilised to strengthen the administrative and logistic capabilities of the ANTF. This would enhance operational efficiency, and ensure effective and sustainable functioning of the State’s anti-narcotics enforcement framework.

In the order issued by the government creating the ANTF a couple of days ago, other departments such as Health and Family Welfare, School Education, Higher Education, Youth Welfare and Sports Development, Municipal Administration and Water Supply, and Directorate of Information and Public Relations among others, were tasked with specific responsibilities in paving the way for a drug-free Tamil Nadu.

CM to administer pledge

In a related development, police sources said that Mr Vijay would administer ‘Anti-Drug Pledge’ to 2,000 students in-person and to many students across the State through video conference at Presidency College Auditorium here on Tuesday.

He would also launch the ‘Drug and Tobacco Free Campus’ initiative and present the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Police Medal for outstanding work eradicating of drug production and illicit trafficking.

World.title: Man electrocuted from wild boar trap in Kerala’s Palakkad
World.content:
A 33-year-old man was found dead in a paddy field at Thathanappully, Kulukkallur, here on Monday (August 10, 2026) allegedly after being electrocuted by a live-wire trap set to catch wild boars. The deceased was identified as Ravi Prasad.

Mr. Prasad had parked his bike by the roadside after it developed a mechanical problem on Sunday night and was walking home along a footpath across an agricultural field when he got electrocuted.

The landowner, Manoj, found him lying dead in the field on Monday morning and informed the police. The police took Manoj into custody and said a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder would be registered against him.

World.title: Jharkhand students protest LIVE: Police lathi-charge protesters again outside Jharkhand Assembly
World.content:
August 10, 2026 19:54

Shiv Sena targets Rahul Gandhi; questions 'silence' of some sections

The police action against job aspirants in Ranchi came under severe criticism from Shiv Sena, with party leaders accusing Rahul Gandhi of pursuing a political agenda in the name of students and questioning the purported bias of some MPs, celebrities and activists against the NDA.

The remarks come after police in Ranchi used water cannons, lobbed tear gas shells, and lathi-charged job aspirants as they breached barricades and attempted to reach the State Assembly, protesting the alleged recruitment exam irregularities.

Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam alleged that Rahul Gandhi never held a dialogue with protesters in Jharkhand, where demonstrations have been staged for the last two weeks, but people are baton-charged.

“Rahul Gandhi is doing politics in the name of students. He has not engaged with (protesting) students. If he is really concerned about the issues of the students, then he should resolve it,” Mr. Nirupam added.

He claimed that neither the Opposition leader in the Lok Sabha visited Ranchi nor has the Congress (which is part of the Hemant Soren government in Jharkhand) issued any statement on the protests by students.

Referring to Jharkhand protests, Mr. Nirupam’s party colleague and MP Milind Deora questioned “selective outrage”, which he said depends on who is in power and where the paper leak happens. - PTI

World.title: In backdrop of student protests, Bihar CM outlines four-point educational blueprint
World.content:
At a time when students in neighbouring Jharkhand are protesting for education reforms and a fair examination system, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary proposed a four-point education blueprint from quality schools to Artificial Intelligence-powered examinations for the students in the State.

Mr. Choudhary on Monday (August 10, 2026) also kicked off the Har Ghar Tiranga (the national flag in every household) campaign in Patna saying: “Our ancestors as freedom fighters, sacrificed their lives to establish democracy in India and gave us this tricolour. This [flag] is not just a piece of cloth but it is our pride and marker of Indian democracy.” In a nearly 1.5 km-long tiranga yatra campaign, hundreds of participants waved the national flag from J.P. Roundabout to Kargil Chowk thoroughfare near Gandhi Maidan in Patna.

Follow Jharkhand students protest LIVE updates

“Important decisions have been taken in Bihar to further strengthen, make qualitative and a student-centric education system,” Mr. Choudhary said in a late night social media post on August 9.

He further elaborated the four points comprising a State-level special committee that has been constituted to ensure quality education reaches every school while a State-level examination reform committee would make examinations in Bihar smooth, transparent, fair and modern. The committee will provide suggestions for better assessment of student’s knowledge, understanding and analytical abilities through the use of technologies and AI in board and competitive examinations as well as class-based evaluations; special collaboration camps will be organised for education reforms in which suggestions and problems will be heard through dialogue with the Chief Minister, State Ministers, MPs, MLAs and students. The fourth and last point in the blueprint was that students welfare directorates will be constituted in all relevant departments for better coordination and effective implementation of works related to students welfare.

“The Bihar Government is committed to quality education, a better examination system and building a bright future for students,” asserted Mr. Choudhary. “Students will be able to access online classes until 11 p.m. from August 15. The government would also work towards providing computer and English education to all children while promoting Sanskrit, Urdu and the five languages of Bihar,” he added while stating that “the government wants to create an education system that would reduce the need for students to leave Bihar in search of better opportunities”.

During the tricolour’s flag-off, the Chief Minister said that ”tiranga is not just a piece of cloth divided into three colours but it is our pride and marker of Indian democracy”.

Remembering freedom fighters, Mr. Choudhary added, “...Without their sacrifices and efforts, we would not have attained freedom 78 years ago.”

State party president Sanjay Saraogi, Minister for Cooperatives Ram Kripal Yadav, Agriculture Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha and others were also present on the occasion.

“Tiranga yatra has become a mass movement,” said Mr. Saraogi while announcing that “we will carry out a similar yatra at all district headquarters of the State on August 12”. “The tiranga yatra sends a message to enemies and traitors whose negative mindset weakens the nation,” Mr. Sinha said on the occasion.

However, both the Deputy Chief Ministers of the State from the ruling NDA ally, Janata Dal (United), Bijendra Prasad Yadav and Vijay Kumar Choudhary were conspicuous by their absence on the occasion.

World.title: Modernised Thalli Bidda express vehicles to be launched on August 11
World.content:
Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav will launch a new fleet of 102 Thalli Bidda Express vehicles at Narasaraopet on August 11.

According to a press release issued by the Health Department on Monday, the modernised vehicles have been designed to ensure safer and more convenient transportation for pregnant women and mothers.

The State government is procuring 500 vehicles. In the first phase, 300 vehicles will be introduced, with the remaining 200 to be rolled out later.

The vehicles will be equipped with air-conditioning, six airbags, rear seat belts, child-lock sliding doors, GPS tracking, SOS buttons and other safety features. They will also have charging ports and first-aid kits, besides carrying health-awareness messages on breastfeeding, newborn care, nutrition and vaccinations.

The government has entrusted the operation of the service to the Vidyaveda Foundation and M/s Srinivasa Tours and Travels consortium. It has proposed a budget of ₹37.40 crore for the service in 2026–27.

The upgraded 102 service is aimed at reducing transportation difficulties and improving maternal and newborn care, thereby contributing to a reduction in maternal and infant mortality in the State.

Free drop-back services will be available only to women who deliver at government hospitals. The mother and infant can be accompanied by two attendants.

The toll-free 102 service can be accessed from any phone in the State.

World.title: PM Vishwakarma initiative: Kodagu artisans trained in AI, e-commerce
World.content:
The Branch MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Mangaluru, under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, organised a one-day awareness programme on branding and marketing for beneficiaries of the PM Vishwakarma scheme at Kushalnagar, Kodagu district, recently. The programme was conducted in association with the Kushalnagar Taluk Tailors’ Association.

The programme aimed to create awareness among traditional artisans about enterprise development, branding, digital marketing, e-commerce, financial assistance, Udyam Registration, and various government support mechanisms available for strengthening and promoting their businesses.

Around 150 tailor beneficiaries, registered under the PM Vishwakarma scheme, participated in the event. Participants received practical guidance on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools for business promotion, digital marketing techniques, onboarding on e-commerce platforms, QR code generation, and registration on the Udyam Portal to access benefits under various Union and State government schemes, a press release said.

Presiding over the programme, Sundar Sherigar, Assistant Director and Head of Office, Branch MSME-DFO, Mangaluru, stressed the importance of adopting AI-based marketing tools and digital technologies to enhance the visibility, reach, and competitiveness of small enterprises. He encouraged artisans to leverage digital platforms to expand their customer base and improve business prospects.

Suman S. Raju, Assistant Director and programme coordinator, explained the various stages and benefits of the PM Vishwakarma scheme. She also highlighted the significance of Udyam Registration in accessing government schemes, incentives, and support available to MSMEs.

Hanumatharaya, Joint Director of the District Industries Centre, Madikeri, delivered a session on the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme, explaining its key features, eligibility criteria, and application process for financial assistance to establish and expand micro enterprises.

Shaik Ahmed, president of the Kodagu District Tailors Association and Nagaraj, president of the Kushalnagar Taluk Tailors Association, also spoke.

World.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact ‘entirely for defensive purposes’, not aggression: PM Shehbaz
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday affirmed that the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz recalled that he, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact in Makkah on Friday.

The prime minister stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

“Its purpose is definitely not that any aggression occurs. It is entirely for defensive purposes, for peace, tranquillity and progress in the region,” he affirmed.

“I believe this agreement is a source of strength not just among these three countries, but for the entire Muslim ummah,” he noted.

PM Shehbaz particularly felicitated Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar as well as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir on the signing of the agreement.

Efforts for the joint defence pact had been underway for “many years and materialised this Friday”, the prime minister said.

He noted that while Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already entered the “Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement” in September 2025, Islamabad and Ankara also had “arrangements for decades” between them.

PM Shehbaz recalled that the Pakistani nation and the army had been honoured to “defend the world’s holiest places” of Makkah and Madina for years along with the Saudi forces.

“Last year, with Allah’s grace, this arrangement was officially recognised so that a proper agreement was signed. Friday’s agreement is another extension of it, with a trilateral agreement signed.”

In a statement issued by the Foreign Office earlier in the day, Dar felicitated the nation on the agreement’s signing. He reiterated his comments from Sunday wherein he said the pact was defensive in nature and not directed against any country.

Dar also noted that the term of treating an attack on one of them as an attack against all three was “consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter”.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait, Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

‘Once in power, AJK govt will offer dialogue to those willing’

Speaking on Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), PM Shehbaz favoured dialogue with protesters who have been at odds with the authorities over the 12 seats reserved for refugees and other issues, leading to a tense situation in the region for the past two months.

He said that once the new government comes to power in AJK — with PML-N already claiming a two-thirds majority — the matter of continuing talks with the protesters “will progress”.

The prime minister declared that those “who only want to cause anarchy will not be allowed to do so, but those who want to peacefully and patiently discuss the situation, the new government will provide a chance for that”.

“In any respected society, no permission can be given for lawlessness. If there is any demand or any matters, they should be resolved through talks at a table,” he said.

PM Shehbaz went on to say that the government had “clear evidence that those who purposefully worsened the situation there were working on the directives of the enemy”.

He recalled that despite that, the government had held a multi-party conference in Muzaffarabad before the elections, with only one political party being absent — apparently referring to the PTI which has boycotted the polls.

“Every aspect was discussed there, and […] those who wanted refugee seats to be changed, reduced or abolished were advised to let the elections go on as planned and bring forward their case in the new assembly,” he said, adding that this would resolve the matter as per the constitution of AJK.

“All matters were settled, but they remained adamant on this and needlessly insisted, which unfortunately worsened the situation,” the prime minister said.

Speaking about the ongoing elections in AJK, PM Shehbaz asserted that Kashmiris have “overwhelmingly voted” for his PML-N.

The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats out of a total 45 — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The third phase of elections in Poonch Division began today.

The prime minister noted that based on the results from Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions, along with the seats reserved for refugees from India-held Kashmir, the PML-N has “almost established a majority”.

“This vote is a vote of trust in Mian Nawaz Sharif and for his leadership. I am hopeful that once we set up a government there, under his leadership, AJK will once again set out on the journey to progress and prosperity,” he said, thanking those who voted for his party.

‘Terrorists being annihilated day and night’

At the federal cabinet meeting, PM Shehbaz also touched upon the issue of terrorism in the country and mentioned the lives lost in recent terrorist attacks.

He noted that terrorists escalated their activities in “some areas of Pakistan in the past few days”.

The premier recalled the August 2 Swat suicide bombing that claimed 17 lives and the martyrdom of Deputy Superintendent of Police Diyar Khan in an attack on a Hangu police checkpost.

He paid tribute to the sacrifices of the personnel, including Captain Hamza Akram and Major Hafiz Ihsan Elahi, who were martyred during operations in Hangu and North Waziristan, respectively.

The prime minister affirmed that “Fitna Al Khawarij are being annihilated day and night”, referring to terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

“These sacrifices will not go in vain and will bear fruition. One day will come when Pakistan will once again be free from terrorism and will move rapidly towards peace and progress,” PM Shehbaz said.

The prime minister also expressed his condolences over the death of PML-N MNA Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar, describing him as a “longtime friend”.

“He was a person who was a supporter in bad times,” he said, adding that he and PML-N President Nawaz Sharif knew Channar since 1985. The cabinet also prayed for the elevated ranks of the martyrs and Channar.

World.title: Sindh govt defers judicial commission decision on Mir Raza Ali murder case probe
World.content:
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Monday the provincial government had deferred the decision on the formation of a judicial commission to probe the Mir Raza Ali murder case.

Lanjar made the announcement on X, saying that Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab had spoken to Ali’s family, who had expressed “confidence in the new police team” constituted to investigate the case and was of the view that it should conduct the probe.

“Therefore, the decision of establishing a judicial commission has been deferred for the time being,” the home minister said.

Owner of eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report after the exhumation and a second postmortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide.

Controversy fueled by ‘miscommunication’

Sindh Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho said that the investigation into the murder should be conducted in a better manner, expressing hope that the new investigation team would consider all available evidence.

Speaking to the media in Sukkur, he said the government, public and police were all concerned about the case and stressed the need to examine it “with an open mind and open heart”.

He said action had been taken against officers found guilty of misconduct and negligence during the investigation.

IG Odho said the controversy surrounding Ali’s murder had been fuelled by “miscommunication”.

“I have strictly instructed the entire investigation team to keep communication open and transparent this time, whether with the deceased’s family or the media,” he said.

On Sunday, PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission to probe the case, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Lanjar and Wahab had reached Ali’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice. Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar had said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case.

However, Jibran Nasir, the family’s lawyer, posted on X that they had not requested or consented to any judicial commission.

“Nor do we believe it’s required at this stage. A new investigation team has been formed, which the family will meet tomorrow. The Sindh government should not try to create hurdles/confusion in the name of ‘facilitation,’“ he said.

He had earlier also objected to the initially constituted police team probing the case and demanded that it be replaced.

Speaking to the media on Saturday after the results of the second autopsy came out, he had said that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team.

Subsequently, the Sindh inspector general of police’s office notified on Sunday the reconstitution of the investigating team probing the case. The order to this effect said the new investigation team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem.

The same day, Karachi police chief Azad Khan also suspended Sharea Faisal Sub-divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after Ali’s body was found.

The city police chief also ordered the case be transferred to Zaman Town Police Station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was initially registered.

Controversy over autopsy

The latest developments in the case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination.

Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel last week that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another.

The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case.

Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation.

The statement, however, said that exhumation of the body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday.

After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said.

She said the body bore “injuries in the right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in the mouth and throat”.

World.title: Major earthquake rocks Colombia and other countries, causing damage and injuries
World.content:
A powerful earthquake rocked Colombia and other Latin American countries on Monday, causing unspecified damage and injuries and building evacuations in Bogota.

The Colombian geological service put the magnitude of the quake at 6.6 while its American counterpart USGS put it at 7.4, with an epicentre 100km underground in the west of Colombia.

It was felt in Ecuador and as far away as Panama to the north, and prompted building evacuations in Bogota, AFP reporters saw.

The governor of Colombia’s Choco province wrote on X that there were injuries and serious damage to buildings in the department’s capital Quibdo.

The mayor of Cali, Colombia’s third largest city, also reported “major damage”. At least 20 buildings collapsed in the city, with people trapped inside, Mayor Alejandro Eder said.

The city has requested teams from Bogota and Medellin to aid in rescue efforts, he added.

Six airports damaged in the earthquake have suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said. These airports serve Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, the agency wrote on X.

News outlets aired footage of some buildings with their facades ripped off by the quake.

In Bogota some people ran out into the street in their pajamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw.

Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage.

More to follow

World.title: Peshawar High Court grants transit bail to Noreen Niazi in Peca case
World.content:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Monday granted transit bail to Noreen Niazi, the sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, in a case registered under the Peca Act 2026, directing her to appear before the relevant Islamabad court on or before August 20.

In July, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) registered a case against Noreen, accusing her of passing derogatory and inflammatory remarks against state institutions during a podcast interview and in subsequent clips shared on X.

A single-member PHC bench comprising Justice Arshad Ali heard Noreen’s petition, represented by a panel of lawyers, including Ali Zaman, Amir Zeb and Barrister Sarwar Muzaffar Shah

In its order issued on Monday, the bench stated that the petitioner had approached the court seeking transit bail in connection with a first information report (FIR) registered against her at the NCCIA police station in Islamabad on July 27 under various provisions of the Peca Act 2016 and the Pakistan Penal Code, enabling her to approach the competent court.

The order noted that the petitioner had claimed to have been falsely implicated in the case and that, except for the bare allegations contained in the FIR, there was no other cogent evidence on record to connect her with the alleged offence.

“In the circumstances of the case, the petitioner’s request, being reasonable, merits consideration,” the order noted, adding that “consequently this application is accepted and the accused petitioner is granted ad-interim transit pre-arrest bail provided she furnishes bail bonds in the sum of Rs80,000 with two sureties,” it said.

The bench also directed the petitioner to approach the competent forum in Islamabad for bail on or before August 20, as the PHC order would be effective till that day.

Meanwhile, the counsels for the petitioner argued that their client was innocent and falsely implicated in the case registered at the NCCIA police station.

They said the local police were trying to arrest their client with mala fide intentions, to humiliate and unjustly harass her for some ulterior motive.

The counsels also said the allegations contained in the FIR were false and politically motivated, and were based on an erroneous interpretation of statements allegedly attributed to their client.

Talking to reporters after the hearing, Noreen said she came to know about the NCCIA case against her after arriving in Peshawar.

“I did speak inside in my house, which I do not have recollection of, and someone got that to them and they made a case against me,” she claimed.

Noreen further alleged that cases had been lodged against her other sisters and that now one had been registered against her as well. “Too many cases are being registered across Pakistan, and no one knows why they have been lodged. The case against me is the same,” she said.

In response to a question, she said they had never been to Peshawar, so the question of their interfering in KP affairs did not even arise.

Earlier, the Lahore High Court had also granted her an interim protective bail, directing her to approach a relevant Islamabad court.

Before registering an FIR, the NCCIA had summoned Noreen to appear before it on July 20 over allegations of disseminating “false, offensive and inflammatory” content against state institutions.

While the notice did not specify the content in relation to which Noreen has been summoned, it was issued after the clip of her making claims in relation to last year’s brief military conflict between Pakistan and India was widely shared on social media.

In the clip, she is seen alleging during an interview that the conflict was “orchestrated” to improve the image of Pakistan’s military.
