World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Odesa in summer 2026: Life between sea and war. VIDEO
World.content:
Beaches, bomb-damaged homes and explosions in broad daylight. In the summer of 2026, Odesa is caught between its traditional seaside resort atmosphere and the constant threat of Russian attacks. While some people relax by the sea and stroll through the city centre, others sift through the rubble left by the latest strike.

JAMnews visited Odesa to show what life in the city looks like today.

Odesa and the surrounding region remain frequent targets of Russian strikes. Residential neighbourhoods, critical infrastructure and port facilities have all come under attack.

Russia has carried out combined attacks using drones and missiles, seeking to overwhelm Ukraine‘s air defence systems.

The impact of these attacks is visible across the city. Residential buildings have been damaged, windows blown out and flats destroyed. Strikes have also hit Odesa’s historic centre, including heritage buildings and universities.

Ports in Odesa Region, along with the logistics hubs and warehouses that support them, are also regularly targeted. Attacks on port infrastructure have disrupted Ukraine’s transport network and Black Sea export routes.

The strikes often occur in broad daylight, when the streets are busy, cafés and shops are open, and beaches are filled with residents and visitors. At any moment, the familiar sounds of the city can be interrupted by explosions, air defence fire or the buzz of attack drones.

On several occasions, missiles have been intercepted directly over the coastline while beaches were crowded with people.

Today, it is possible to spend the day at the beach and the night in a bomb shelter.

World.title: Colombia hit by 7.4-magnitude earthquake, with injuries and damage reported
World.content:
A powerful earthquake has collapsed buildings and trapped residents under rubble in western Colombia and shaken parts of neighbouring Ecuador.

The Colombian geological service and its American counterpart the USGS put the magnitude at 7.4, with an epicentre 100km underground in the west of the country.

The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) said it had begun surveying cities and provinces for damage.

Injuries and significant damage were reported in the Pacific Colombian province of Choco, while the mayor of the nearby city of Cali reported that at least 20 buildings had collapsed from the quake, trapping people inside.

Footage showed people climbing over rubble attempting to move debris in Cali.

Following the quake, Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella said he had "directly assumed leadership of the emergency response in José del Palma".

"I have requested from the director of the UNGRD a detailed report on the situation and the most urgent needs. I will also be personally in Pereira to accompany the affected people and verify the Government's response," he wrote on X.

" You are not alone. The State is present and acting. "

The worst reports of damage were in the Colombian city of Cali. (AP: Santiago Saldarriaga)

The US's Tsunami Warning System said there was no risk of a tsunami following the earthquake.

The provincial governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi took to X to provide an update on what she described as "a major earthquake", warning local residents about aftershocks.

"Although the epicentre was near San Jose del Palmar, there are injuries and significant damage to buildings in the capital, Quibdo," she said.

Local officials from multiple provinces were reporting damage and collapsed buildings following the quake. (AP: Santiago Saldarriaga)

The governor of neighbouring Risaralda province, Juan Diego Patino, told local Blu Radio there was "serious damage to some buildings" in Pereira, the provincial capital.

"What has just occurred is very severe. The images are truly shocking, with people injured and building facades collapsed," he said.

At least six Colombian airports suspended operations after the quake, news agency AFP reported.

The temblor follows two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela in late June. Those earthquakes destroyed hundreds of buildings and killed more than 5,000 people.

Wires/ABC

World.title: 'Loyalty doesn't pay': Car insurers asked to explain soaring premiums
World.content:
Car insurance companies are under pressure to explain what is driving sharp and sustained increases in premiums after a review by the corporate regulator found prices soared far beyond inflation last year.

The review, released by ASIC today, found that motor vehicle insurance premiums increased by 8 per cent in the year to July 2025, following growth of more than 42 per cent between 2019 and 2024.

To examine the industry, ASIC looked at eight insurance brands under five insurers, which collectively make up nearly three-quarters of the market, after seeing a significant increase in consumer complaints about the industry.

"Car insurance was the most complained about insurance product in 2024-25, and the biggest reason that people complained about their car insurance was premiums," ASIC commissioner Alan Kirkland said.

"This is a real source of consumer pain, and that's not a surprise given that many people are battling cost-of-living concerns.

" Those rises are well above the rate of inflation, and … consumers are unhappy, they're complaining, and they want to understand more about the reasons for those significant premium increases. "

The corporate watchdog found that the renewal notices of the five insurance companies did not clearly explain why premiums were rising more than inflation, leaving consumers in the dark.

Car insurers reviewed by ASIC: AAI Limited (AAMI and Suncorp)

Allianz Australia (Allianz and Territory Insurance Office (TIO))

Insurance Australia Group (IAG) (NRMA and RACV)

RAC Insurance

Youi Source: ASIC 'Road testing transparency into car insurance premiums' report, August 2026

"[Insurers] tell us there are a range of reasons for these significant increases, but the problem is they're not explaining the reasons for those increases," Mr Kirkland said.

"That's important because people need to understand how much their premium has actually gone up, but also the reasons, because that may prompt them to push back on their insurer or shop around."

Insurers that charged consumers more when they paid in instalments (weekly, fortnightly, monthly or quarterly) did not make it clear in renewal notices that they could save between 10 and 20 per cent by paying annually.

The report also found that of the two-thirds of people who renewed their policy with their insurer, 40 per cent did not contact their provider or compare quotes, with many believing it would not be worthwhile or result in a lower premium.

However, almost one in three people who questioned their premiums ended up with a better deal.

"[It] shows that the price that you are offered may not be the lowest price that you could pay," Mr Kirkland said.

"This also shows that loyalty doesn't pay. Customers who are loyal stay with the same insurer year after year and don't push back on prices are likely to be paying more than the customers that do push back, or the newer customers who've just come through the door."

Alan Kirkland says insurers need to be more transparent with consumers about changes to their premiums. (ABC News: Adam Wyatt)

But the findings by ASIC are not evidence that insurers are gouging consumers, Mr Kirkland warned.

"We don't regulate the prices that insurers offer to their customers, but what we do regulate is the way in which they communicate with their customers, and that's what we looked at through this report," he said.

"What are they saying? Are they displaying increases in premiums prominently in a way that consumers can understand? And are they explaining the reasons for those increases?

" What we found is that insurers across the board are falling short. "

Insurance industry facing further scrutiny

The focus on car insurance premiums by ASIC comes as it takes IAG-owned insurance brand RACQ to court.

The regulator announced the legal action in September 2025, alleging RACQ sent thousands of car insurance customers over half a million renewal documents with misleading comparison pricing for more than five years, despite customers' complaints.

It is the second time RACQ has been pursued by ASIC through the Federal Court, with the insurer fined $10 million in November 2023 for misleading customers about discounts for certain types of insurance cover.

"ASIC has a strong track record of taking action against insurers in relation to misleading practices when it comes to pricing," Mr Kirkland said.

"We will continue to do so if we find insurers misleading their customers about what they'll pay or what discounts they might be entitled to."

The release of ASIC's report also coincides with broader scrutiny of insurers.

The federal government is planning to legislate standard definitions in premium notices, while the industry's peak body is working on a code of conduct that will be enforceable by the corporate regulator for the first time.

In a statement, the Insurance Council of Australia (ICA) said it is exploring options to explain premiums more clearly to consumers and is looking forward to engaging with the federal government.

The corporate regulator is responsible for overseeing how insurers communicate with consumers, not premiums. (ABC News: Callum Flinn)

A spokesperson for Youi declined to comment on the report, while spokespeople for RAC Insurance, IAG and AAI Limited deferred to the ICA's statement.

Allianz Australia, which offers insurance through its Allianz and Territory Insurance Office (TIO) brands, said its premiums take several factors into account but encouraged customers to get in touch if they had questions.

"Where premiums have increased, this reflects rising repair and replacement costs, including parts, labour, supply chain pressures and the impact of severe weather events," an Allianz spokesperson said.

"We outline factors that may have influenced a customer's premium and provide options to help manage their premium — including reviewing their excess, sum insured or optional benefits."

In June, financial comparison site Canstar released its annual car insurance report, finding that the average comprehensive car insurance premium had risen by 5 per cent (or $111) over the past 12 months.

Despite the increases to premiums, the Canstar report also noted that more than a quarter of motorists remained loyal to their insurer.

Mr Kirkland acknowledged while it can be inconvenient contacting insurers, he advised that doing so is ultimately in consumers' best interests.

World.title: Ukraine kills 13 in drone attack on Russian city of Nizhnekamsk
World.content:
At least 13 people have been killed, including a child, and 75 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on industrial and civilian targets in the Russian city of Nizhnekamsk, authorities said.

It was one of the heaviest civilian tolls in Russia in recent months.

Ukraine's military said it had hit Tatneft's TANECO oil refinery in the Tatarstan region, about 800km east of Moscow, adding that a fire was recorded at the facility.

Russian investigators said they had opened a criminal case into what they qualified as a terrorist attack, saying in a statement that Ukraine had struck residential areas and that a child was among those civilians killed.

The head of Russia's Tatarstan region, Rustam Minnikhanov, has declared a period of mourning, Radmir Belyayev, the mayor of Nizhnekamsk, said in a statement.

In verified videos on social media, smoke can be seen rising over the oil refinery.

The TANECO refinery, which was also hit by Ukraine in early June, processed 17 million tons of crude oil in 2024, producing 2.7 million tons of gasoline and 8.5 million tons of diesel fuel.

Ukraine has stepped up its strikes on Russian oil refineries in recent months in a campaign that has caused fuel shortages in many parts of Russia, although authorities say that most of those initial problems have since been resolved.

The aftermath of Sunday's Ukrainian drone attack in Belgorod, Russia. (Reuters)

Ukraine says it wants to bring the price of Russia's war home to ordinary Russians. Moscow has imported fuel from overseas to help bolster supplies.

On Sunday, both sides accused each other of lethal attacks.

Three people were killed and 37 wounded in a Russian attack on the eastern Ukrainian city of Kharkiv, where a multi-storey apartment block was hit, while authorities in Russia's Belgorod said five were killed and 25 wounded by a Ukrainian drone attack.

Ukraine and Russia have repeatedly said they do not target civilians.

Russia's attack on Ukrainian infrastructure has left Odesa residents without electricity. (Reuters: Nina Liashonok)

In Ukraine's southern Odesa region, tens of thousands of households were still without power after Russian struck the power grid over the weekend.

Zelenskyy says 50,000 North Koreans will help Russia Mr Zelenskyy took to social media to announced that "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", while calling on South Korea to provide support for Ukraine's air defence.

Concerns are rising in Kyiv over the upcoming winter, with the energy network still reeling from four years of Russian strikes.

Last winter, millions were plunged into darkness and had their heating and water cut for hours as temperatures sunk to -20C.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on the weekend that his country has "virtually no intact thermal power plants" following the Russian attacks.

Kyiv has also been running short of vital missile interceptors as Russia has significantly escalated its attacks with hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles.

Dozens have been killed in Kyiv over the last two months in direct hits on apartment buildings.

Wires/ABC

World.title: Five accused of using dating apps for homophobic attacks in Melbourne
World.content:
Five males have been arrested after a series of attacks on men who police allege were targeted through dating apps and social media.

Police say groups of offenders have been posing as legitimate users on these platforms to lure men into meeting them.

The victims are then assaulted, robbed, threatened and subjected to what police described as homophobic comments.

If this story has raised concerns for you, help is available: Urgent help: Lifeline — 13 11 14

Kids Helpline — 1800 551 800 LGBT and mental health support: Switchboard — 1800 729 367

Qlife — 1800 184 527

Headspace — 1800 650 890

Beyond Blue — 1300 22 4636

Five males aged between 16 and 18 have been arrested in relation to 11 incidents that were reported to police in the Greater Dandenong area.

They are facing various charges including kidnapping, sexual assault, intentionally causing injury and armed robbery.

Police said there had been 113 reports of similar attacks across the state since January 2024, which resulted in 47 arrests.

Acting Inspector Jarrod Dwyer said police were treating the alleged attacks as concerning.

"There is no place for it in our society, and it will not be tolerated by police," he said.

He said police were investigating distressing allegations, and he urged any victims of attacks to contact police and not just rely on reporting incidents to the dating apps.

"Everyone has a right to go about their lives, meet new people and start a relationship in safety.

"It is never too late to make a report, so when you're ready, please speak to us. The more we know, the more we can do something about it and keep victims safe."

A Victoria Police spokesperson said investigators were continuing to work with dating apps and were publishing proactive safety messaging on the platforms, including reporting options and support services.

They said detectives could request information from the apps to help with their investigations, including when one party had blocked or deleted someone from the app.

They said a Victoria Police LGBTIQA+ Liaison Officer was available to anyone who needed support.

Crimestoppers has published this advice for anyone in the broader community using any dating apps.

World.title: 'Generational change': Melissa Donnelly named as new ACTU boss
World.content:
The new boss of Australia's biggest union is confronting a question that is increasingly worrying workers: not just whether AI will take their jobs, but if any jobs will be left for their children.

Public Sector Union boss Melissa Donnelly will take the helm of the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU), inheriting a movement at the height of its political influence but facing a long-term decline in membership and a fight over the impact of AI on the workforce.

"Lots of workers aren't just worried about what it means for their jobs, they're worried about what it means for their teenage kids," Ms Donnelly said.

"Are there going to be jobs for them in the future?"

Melissa Donnelly will first focus on cost of living when she takes over as head of the ACTU. (ABC News: Abbey Haberecht)

Things are very different from when Ms Donnelly was a 15-year-old union member clocking in to shifts at her local Target.

Today the average union member is 44 years old and, like her, a working mum.

Trade union membership has been in general decline since 1992, but under outgoing secretary Sally McManus it increased for the first time since 2011.

Despite that gain, less than 4 per cent of members were aged 15 to 19, while about 7 per cent were aged 20 to 24.

Sally McManus was ACTU secretary from 2017 to 2026. (ABC News: Briana Fiore)

Ms McManus said her replacement represented generational change.

"With two school-aged children and having led a large union, she well knows the pressures working people are under," she said.

The cost of living will be Ms Donnelly's first focus when she takes the helm at the end of August.

"Every time you go to the checkout it costs more and more," she said.

"It will continue to be a key focus for our movement."

Donnelly inherits fight to win back young workers

Ms Donnelly inherits the long-held challenge to bring more workers into the base.

She will also have to deal with a series of reputational hits to the union movement in recent years, particularly in Victoria with the CFMEU forced into administration and a looming royal commission into the state's Big Build program.

Despite those headwinds, trade unions have had an exceptional run under the current federal Labor government, with wins including Same Job Same Pay and the Right to Disconnect.

Ms Donnelly said these real gains were the way the union movement must continue to appeal to younger workers most at risk of losing work to AI.

McManus and O'Neil quit ACTU leadership The heads of the Australian Council of Trade Unions have announced that they are making way for the next generation.

"We're already making good progress," she said.

"We've got to continue that work, we've got to remain relevant, and that's the way I believe we will continue to have young people join our movement."

Beyond real wage growth and a push for better working conditions, there remains unanswered questions and an inherent tension around the ability to raise living standards through productivity gains without ultimately replacing workers with AI.

"[AI] obviously has the capacity to bring fundamental change to workers, and our job is to make sure there are strong guardrails in place," Ms Donnelly said.

Public sector boss takes the lead

Ms Donnelly has trotted a very Labor path.

She worked for left-leaning think tank The McKell Institute, and started her union career as a 25-year-old lawyer fighting the Howard government's bid to stop unionised public sector workers participating in protest action against WorkChoices laws.

"For me, that was a galvanising experience," she said.

"It really motivated me in my career on behalf of working people to advance the interests of union members."

BHP, unions gauging impact of strikes BHP's Port Hedland operations just faced 48 hours of industrial action, how much of an impact did it have?

Ms Donnelly went on to spend seven years at the helm of the Community and Public Sector Union as secretary.

Her major wins during her tenure include the reversal of the outsourcing of government work to big consultancy firms, and securing work-from-home rights for public service employees.

Ms McManus said Ms Donnelly had "overwhelming support" from all unions.

The ACTU will announce a replacement for outgoing president Michele O'Neil later this year.

World.title: 'Unexpected' closure of Adelaide wedding venue leaves couples scrambling
World.content:
Many Adelaide couples are scrambling to find a new venue for their weddings after a popular restaurant and cellar door announced its "unexpected" closure.

Ondeen, which opened in Adelaide Hills' Verdun two years ago, posted to social media last week announcing it had been forced to close.

"It is with incredibly heavy hearts that we share that Ondeen has unexpectedly received notice of the termination of its lease and has been forced to close for now," the post read.

Adelaide bride Mia Anfiteatro told 891 ABC Adelaide she was now $15,000 to $20,000 out of pocket after having to change her wedding venue.

"We've got two young girls who were really excited to get photos with the highland cows," she said.

Ms Anfiteatro said the couple had purchased 700 golf balls for guests to use on the driving range and had selected Ondeen's culinary expertise as "the art and centrepiece" of their wedding.

Ondeen is also home to four highland cows and two calves. (Supplied)

She said it was disappointing to have to find a new venue but the Adelaide community had rallied around her in helping to secure a spot on her original date.

"We put a post up on the Adelaide wedding chitchat page and we had some outstanding responses," she said.

Ondeen is a popular choice for weddings. (Supplied)

Riverland bride Nicola Thiele said she had managed to secure another venue in nearby Hahndorf for her upcoming wedding next month — but said the change had been stressful.

"I'm a busy mum — I've got three children under six, and then I'm trying to get married," she said.

"It did really throw me off because I picked somewhere like Ondeen because they had everything there … they do the food, they do the drinks, they supply most of the crockery, cutlery, chairs and everything.

"Leaving it this late to try to find somewhere that's got all of that — I think I was in the deep end."

Scott Edwards and Nicola Thiele had been looking forward to celebrating their wedding at Ondeen. (Supplied)

Ms Thiele said the venue closure had other flow-on effects, including that she was unable to get her money back from other vendors.

Both brides were also disappointed that they had been notified of Ondeen's closure via email, and had struggled to get in contact with the business via other channels

In the email, Ondeen co-founder Deborah Kingsbury told couples the business was "pursuing our legal options" and they would work with customers to find another suitable venue.

Dispute over rent payments

In a statement from its legal representative, the landlord said Ondeen had "been served with four notices of default".

"The tenant remains in default under the lease and the landlord has taken steps to protect its position," the statement read.

"Our client preference is to see the matter resolved promptly and appropriately and as the matter is currently the subject of ongoing communications and it would not be appropriate to comment further on the detail."

Deborah Kingsbury says Ondeen has numerous events booked for the months ahead. (ABC News: Katie Spain)

In a statement, Ms Kingsbury disputed this — saying the rent had been paid in full last week.

"On Tuesday we made the requested payments, covering the period right through to the end of August," she said.

"After that payment was made, we were advised the termination would remain in place."

Ms Kingsbury said the lease was due for a two-year renewal at the end of November.

"We have invested hundreds of thousands of dollars in this property over the last two and a half years, and we have numerous functions, weddings and events booked in the months ahead.

"Like everyone in regional hospitality, we have traded through a tough winter and faced the real pressures of rising business costs.

"Through it all Ondeen has continued to grow, celebrating our first two award-winning years and achieving our strongest ever forward bookings."

Ondeen has been at the Verdun site for more than two years. (Supplied: Duy Dash)

Ondeen staff said they had not been allowed on the property at all, including to feed the highland cows.

The landlord's representative said the animals on the property were being looked after.

World.title: Victorian teachers to vote on new pay offer before strike
World.content:
Victorian teachers and education staff are being asked to vote on a new pay offer which could avert a third statewide strike and end a protracted pay dispute.

An extraordinary Australian Education Union (AEU) council meeting was held this evening to discuss the Victorian government's latest pay offer to the state's public school teachers and education staff.

The new deal maintains the previous 28 to 32 per cent pay rise depending on an educator's role but adds in a $2,000 lump-sum payment for signing the agreement, a limit on the number of face-to-face teaching hours and a one-hour reduction in the time spent attending meetings.

There would also be a 1 per cent annual lump-sum payment for teachers, learning specialists, assistant principals and education support employees who had reached the top of their pay scale.

Ben Carroll says Victoria will boost school funding to meet federal Gonski standards New Premier Ben Carroll says Victoria will fulfil the state’s funding obligations to public schools under the once-called Gonski plan

The offer comes ahead of another planned statewide 24-hour strike on Wednesday, August 19.

The council meeting has resolved to put the offer to a vote of all union members, with the ballot opening tonight and running until August 17, two days before the planned strike.

If a majority of union members accept the government's offer, the strike will be called off.

The offer comes a day after Premier Ben Carroll promised Victoria would increase funding to state schools in accordance with its obligations under the former Gonski plan.

The government and union said signing the full funding agreement with the federal government would mean Victoria's schools were no longer the lowest-funded in Australia.

The union has not said whether it recommended its members accept the deal.

The last time the AEU recommended its members accept a government pay offer, it was voted down by 58 per cent of teachers and education staff who were concerned about workloads and school funding.

The latest government offer comes a little more than a week out from another planned 24-hour statewide teacher strike. (Supplied: Emily Pinney Brown)

But earlier today, AEU Victorian branch president Justin Mullaly said the new offer was a significant step towards recognising and rewarding experienced teachers while achieving sought-after funding improvements for schools.

"It is a significant offer that has been built upon over a period of time," he said.

However, he could not guarantee that teachers and education staff would accept it.

"Our union is a proudly democratic union. Members get to have a say about their terms and conditions."

Justin Mullaly says the deal builds on previous offers made by the state government. (ABC News)

Gabrielle Williams was sworn in as the new education minister in Mr Carroll's cabinet.

She said she spoke to Mr Mullaly over the phone on the day she was appointed to the ministry and met face-to-face with the union the next day.

She said getting the $5 billion agreement across the line remained her first priority in the new portfolio.

"We, of course, hope that our teachers and education support staff will have a close look at this offer and understand that we come to this in good faith and wanting to genuinely ensure that we respect the incredibly important work that they do," she said.

"We believe it's a good offer. In fact, we believe it's an excellent offer."

She said the government was doing all it could to minimise disruptions for Victorian students and their families.

She said active discussions were underway with the Commonwealth about school funding.

World.title: Thailand rocked by second shooting tragedy in three days
World.content:
A gunman has killed a Thai official inside a local government office on the capital Bangkok's outskirts, authorities said, days after a teenager's shooting spree at a school in the same province reignited debate over gun control.

Police said the shooting came after a disagreement over borrowed money.

The suspect, former politician Chalong Riewrang, allegedly fired at Thongchai Yenprasert, the chairman of the Provincial Administrative Organisation in Nonthaburi, which borders Bangkok.

"The motive was personal," Police Lieutenant General Wattana Yijin said, adding that the provincial official's driver was also wounded but is not in a critical state.

Thongchai Yenprasert died in hospital after being shot in the neck. (Facebook)

After being shot in the neck, Mr Thongchai died of his wounds at Nonthaburi's Phra Nang Klao Hospital, its director Dr Sakol Sookprome said.

The 71-year-old joined the Thai police force in 1984, before rising to become a prominent identity in Nonthaburi politics.

In a statement to reporters while in police custody, Chalong said he had gone to confront the victim over a long-standing dispute but the latter declined to talk things out.

"But when he was driving away, he pulled a gun," Chalong said, referring to Mr Thongchai.

" I fired. "

Police did not provide any information on whether the slain official was armed.

His driver was hit in the arm and hand.

Nine dead in mass shooting in Thailand. Here's how it unfolded. The Thai Prime Minister has vowed to introduce a new firearms control law after a teenager killed nine people at a high school and a home outside Bangkok.

Earlier, Chalong had dialled into a YouTube livestream hosted by a political commentator, shortly after the shooting, to discuss the incident.

He was formerly a member of Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's party.

Mr Anutin announced that legal action would be taken against Chalong "without exception", according to local media.

The attack in Nonthaburi province, north of Bangkok, came just three days after a school shooting in the same region that raised questions over gun control in Thailand.

There does not appear to be any link between the two attacks.

Friday's rampage began at the teenager's home and continued at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School, leaving nine people dead, including the shooter, and more than 20 wounded in the country's deadliest mass shooting in nearly four years.

Thai school children returned to their classrooms on Monday, some going through metal detectors and other checks, as Prime Minister Anutin reiterated his intention to tighten gun controls in the wake of the shooting.

Shoes left behind by evacuated students at Debsirin Nonthaburi School. (Reuters: Chalinee Thirasupa)

School director Withan Promsintusak said officials had acted immediately after the attack, introducing weapons screening to reassure parents and protect students.

"We never imagined that a school, which should be the safest place, is where something like this would happen," he said.

Following Friday's shooting, Thailand's Education Ministry has said it would develop new school safety protocols over the next three months, including mental health screenings, emergency response drills, measures to tackle bullying and improved detection of weapons and other prohibited items.

The prime minister also ordered tougher enforcement against people carrying guns in public and said police would set up checkpoints as part of a crack down, which would include tightening controls on the possession, carrying and use of firearms.

Thailand had ​an estimated 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, equating to around 15 guns per 100 residents, the highest rate in South-East Asia by a wide margin, according to a 2017 estimate by the Small Arms Survey.

Wires/ABC

World.title: ‘I haven’t done enough’: Weatherald admits he could be dropped without top end runs
World.content:
SportCricketAustralian cricket ‘I haven’t done enough’: Weatherald admits he could be dropped without top end runs Daniel Brettig Updated August 11, 2026 — 12:26am ,first published 6:25pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Darwin: As Travis Head committed to opening the batting throughout Australia’s strenuous next 12 months of Test series, his opening partner Jake Weatherald has admitted he won’t last long at the other end without hometown runs against Bangladesh. Former opener Matt Renshaw was part of the extended 19-man training squad ahead of this week’s first Test, and the plain-speaking Weatherald was frank about his prospects should he not make a couple of notable scores in the top end. Jake Weatherald leaves the field during an Ashes Test last summer. AP Allrounders Beau Webster and Cameron Green are likely to play together this week after both played key roles at Australia’s main training session, which was brought forward to give the fast bowlers more recovery time from Darwin’s heat. Josh Inglis would then miss out. Josh Hazlewood appears to be shading Scott Boland for the third pace bowling spot.



Mark Waugh has been one seasoned judge to state that Weatherald must make the top order spot his own after a patchy debut series in last summer’s Ashes, and while a recent stint in county cricket helped the left-hander iron out some technical issues exposed by England, the proof will be in the run-scoring in Darwin and Mackay. Editor's pick Australian cricket Bowled out for 54 in their warm-up game, can Bangladesh avoid Test match humiliation? “With someone like Mark Waugh saying that, he’s probably just stating the obvious isn’t he, to be fair,” Weatherald said on Monday. “You are required to make runs all the time when you’re out there, and I’ve got a good opportunity to play two games hopefully and make some runs. If I don’t do that, then yeah I put my fate in someone else’s hands and I haven’t done enough. “It’s a challenge when people you respect say things about your batting, or your game. You’re naturally always looking for affirmation, and people to respect what you’re doing, but at the same time it’s a part of cricket. “I understand now it’s just a part of the game I’m playing, but it’s a great challenge as well. That’s what makes Test cricket so hard, you’re in the spotlight, you need to do a lot of things, not just make runs. If you can do it all, it makes for a good career.”



Jake Weatherald has proven to be a prime lbw candidate. 7 Network As a former Territorian who moved to South Australia and then Tasmania to earn his chance in Tests, Weatherald is everywhere this week, from promotional posters and media rounds to a growing group of fans wandering around Darwin in skull caps to mimic his shaved head. “I won’t hide away from the fact it’s always nerve-wracking to play for your country, but I’m just excited to get out there and try to put on a bit of a show,” he said. “It’s such a big thing for the Territory to have a Territorian play ... it’s not just for me, it’s for everyone else too.” Full deliveries at the stumps got Weatherald into trouble against England, but a fruitful county stint (483 runs at 60.37 with a century in six games for Leicestershire) gave him a chance to tighten up. Editor's pick Exclusive

Australian cricket ‘They hid it away’: The DNA test that revealed an Australian cricketer’s family secret



“There’s been a few tinkerings, hopefully someone sees it,” he said. “It feels completely different, but everyone says I’m pretty similar, which is sort of what I wanted. “I tried to understand what I was really good at and do well in first-class cricket, and what I can improve on what I did in the Ashes to make a better game plan overall. I think I’ve done that, so I’m pretty pumped to go out there and show that. “The conditions were very conducive to improving my technique, getting the ball straighter and hitting the stumps a lot more. So it was a great learning curve for me.” Head, meanwhile, has advised Weatherald not to think too much about high expectations this week. As a state and national teammate, Head is hopeful of the partnership enduring beyond this series, into what are likely to be bruising encounters with South Africa, New Zealand, India and England.



“Sometimes playing the better countries, you sit there with expectations going into a Test and say ‘I just hope I get through it’ sometimes,” Head said. “Then you may come up against a team like Bangladesh with the week they’ve had and the expectation of ‘I really expect myself to get runs’. Related Article Australian cricket Cricket hoped the AB Medal would rival Brownlow glitz and glamour. This year’s award was not even broadcast on TV “That’s sometimes the hardest place to be, when you go out there expecting to, because the game is brutal. So it’s just about tempering expectations around the next little period.” Australia’s head coach Andrew McDonald has confirmed a reduced role for assistant coach Dan Vettori, following the New Zealander’s increased role for the Sunrisers Hyderabad network of franchise teams. “I think there’s choice in the marketplace,” he said. “There’s a market for players and there’ clearly. market for coaches. Dan’s explored that market and we’ve been able to balance that out with him doing some great work with us, so long may that continue.”

World.title: ‘First-world problem’: Why Wallabies star says Suaalii shouldn’t be pigeonholed
World.content:
SportRugby UnionWallabies ‘First-world problem’: Why Wallabies star says Suaalii shouldn’t be pigeonholed Nick Wright August 10, 2026 — 9:17pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Wallabies fullback Tom Wright believes versatility will prove both Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Australia’s greatest weapon, dismissing the notion the game’s $5 million man needed to be cemented in one position. Every pundit in rugby circles has had an opinion on where the former NRL star’s future must lie in the build-up to the 2027 Rugby World Cup, having been largely used in the centres but deployed at fullback for the Waratahs this year. In the latter stages of the Wallabies’ 35-32 triumph of Japan to launch a new era under coach Les Kiss, Suaalii was shifted from outside centre to the wing – the same position he began his rugby league career in, where his near two-metre tall physique made him a lethal aerial threat. Les Kiss speaks to Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii during a Wallabies training session. Getty Images But when asked in Brisbane if the flank or in the midfield getting his hands on the ball more frequently was where the 23-year-old’s long-term future rested, Wright did not believe he should be confined to one role.



“I think it depends what lens you want to put on it; if we leave it ambiguous they [our opposition] won’t know what we’re going to do, so that’s awesome. Being that talented is a first-world problem, for there to be so many opinions on it means he’s almost too good,” Wright said. Related Article Wallabies ‘Is this the end?’: Contract call twists fate for plagued Wallaby “Everyone has an opinion on someone who’s that talented and has brought so much good coverage to our game. I think the versatility we’ve got pretty much across the entire backline is something that potentially is a weapon for us, being able to change the point of attack. “I think ‘Su’ could jump in anywhere; you could mould him into an inside centre if you wanted, you could give him enough time to play five-eighth I think he’d jump at the opportunity to do that. “He’s going to be brilliant wherever we put him. There are so many opinions on it, so you can run with how you will, but he’s such a good player for us, and such a team-first guy – there’s no mention from him that he wants to do this, or doesn’t want to do this.”



While Wright conceded the victory against the Brave Blossoms was far from the polished performance the Wallabies had sought to put in place, he said there were signs Kiss’ philosophies would reap rewards between now and the World Cup. Since arriving at the Queensland Reds three years ago, Kiss has encouraged his players to trust their instincts and skill sets – pushing them to freely express themselves with the ball and backing their judgement. Loading That mentality led to five tries in sweltering Osaka conditions – the first three to outside backs Wright, Harry Potter and Max Jorgensen – but also yielded four unforced dropped balls between Wright, Aukuso-Suaalii and five-eighth Declan Meredith. However, Wright – speaking ahead of Saturday’s return bout with Japan in Townsville – remained undeterred, adamant the group would continue chancing their arm under Kiss’ tutelage, while continuing to develop an understanding of when to pull the trigger depending on the conditions.



“You want to be able to trust your instincts, you love having a coach and coaching staff from top to bottom who push that style of play as well. We speak about bringing the game back to how you grew up playing in the backyard, and that was all systems go,” Wright said. Related Article City life Rugby star on the family ties that bind him to Brisbane “You want to trust the first thing that comes into your mind, but understand we’re versing the best of the best in the world. To be able to think in the next five or 10 minutes what’s going to give us the best chance … finding that balance is probably what every team in world rugby is trying to chase. “The way the coaching staff here, directed by Les, give you that confidence to play what comes to mind, and then everyone getting on the same page and backing that first call, has been awesome.” Wallabies assistant coach Tom Donnelly also confirmed forward Tom Hooper would be available for selection, having overcome a shoulder injury suffered in last month’s loss to Ireland.



“He trained with his club team down in Canberra during the week and ticked off everything he needed to do to become available,” Donnelly said of the 25-year-old, who will join the Reds from Exeter in mid-2028 ahead of the 2029 Super Rugby campaign. “He’ll train with us fully this week.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

Al Wetten of Scarborough wonder: “Maybe the Pope can forgive a sin-bin offence?”

Brian Doughan of Leichhardt swears by the veracity of this tale: “Many years ago, I watched an Italian movie on SBS. One of the characters used some choice language to another, along the lines of ‘F… off, you f...wit.’ However, the subtitle (C8) came up with ‘Out of here, you scoundrel.’ At the end of the movie, the subtitler’s name appeared: Sister Mary Joseph.
